{
  "teamId": "6fc98d18-8a80-4c49-8c42-a6e2a4d3d722",
  "title": "Per-task `model_set` override for capability-bound tasks (FS2A web search → openrouter_anthropic)",
  "priority": 2,
  "description": "## What this is\n\nSurfaced while verifying the SPI-276 fix on staging. Once the bare-prefix 400 was unblocked, the next layer surfaced: under `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm` (current staging default), `resolve_task_model(\"FS2A.web_search_assistant\")` returns `local/vllm/qwen2.5-3b-instruct`, and vLLM rejects the Anthropic `web_search_20250305` tool shape:\n\n```\nlitellm.BadRequestError: Hosted_vllmException - {\"error\":{\"message\":\"2 validation errors:\n  {'type': 'literal_error', 'loc': ('body', 'tools', 0, 'type'), 'msg': \\\"Input should be 'function'\\\", 'input': 'web_search_20250305' ...\n  {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body', 'tools', 0, 'function'), 'msg': 'Field required' ...\nReceived Model Group=local/vllm/qwen2.5-3b-instruct\n```\n\nThe Anthropic web-search tool is provider-specific; the local SLM has no equivalent. FS2A.web_search_assistant is a **capability-bound task**, not a quality/tier choice — it must route to Anthropic via OpenRouter regardless of the active `LLM_MODEL_SET`.\n\n## Proposed approach\n\nAdd a `model_set` field to `LLMTaskDefinition` and let `[FS2A.web_search_assistant]` (and any future capability-bound task) declare its required set.\n\n```toml\n[FS2A.web_search_assistant]\ntier = \"medium\"\nmodel_set = \"openrouter_anthropic\"\ndescription = \"Use the Anthropic web search tool via OpenRouter; this capability is not available on the local SLM.\"\n```\n\nResolution change in `packages/inference/llm/tiers.py` `resolve_task_model()`:\n- If the task definition declares `model_set`, use it instead of the active env-or-context selection.\n- Otherwise fall back to the current chain (explicit arg → context → env → default).\n\nTests:\n- A task with `model_set = \"openrouter_anthropic\"` resolves to the openrouter alias even when `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm` is in the env.\n- A task without `model_set` continues to honour the active env selection.\n- An invalid `model_set` value raises clearly at load time.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- [ ] `FS2A.web_search_assistant` resolves to `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` regardless of `LLM_MODEL_SET`.\n- [ ] FS2A web-search call against the staging proxy returns a 200 (not the vLLM tool-shape 400) when the staging stack is running under `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm`.\n- [ ] All other tasks unchanged.\n- [ ] One new unit test pinning the override behaviour and one pinning the no-override default.\n- [ ] No new direct-LiteLLM calls (per SPI-276 invariant).\n\n## Related\n\n- SPI-276 — bare-prefix bug fix (PR #265) — landing first; this builds on it.\n- The wider question of \"should the local SLM be the staging default at all\" is separately tracked.\n\n## Evidence\n\n* Live wire probe from `elijah-staging-worker-1` against staging LiteLLM (2026-05-19), `model=openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` returned HTTP 200 with `message.annotations[].url_citation` populated. So the Anthropic route is fine; only the resolution layer needs to be told FS2A is capability-bound.\n* PR #265 unit tests cover the parser side (annotations + provider_specific_fields shapes)."
}

  "body": "## Follow-up surfaced during staging verification (no Linear ticket — workspace at issue cap)\n\nThe PR #265 fix unblocks the bare-prefix 400. Live probe against the staging LiteLLM with `model=openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` + the Anthropic `web_search_20250305` tool returned HTTP 200 and `message.annotations[].url_citation` with two real sources — confirming the fix end-to-end on the openrouter_anthropic route.\n\nRunning the actual `get_web_search_candidates()` against the live worker surfaced the **next layer**: under `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm` (current staging default), `resolve_task_model(\"FS2A.web_search_assistant\")` resolves to `local/vllm/qwen2.5-3b-instruct`, and vLLM 400s on the Anthropic tool shape:\n\n```\nHosted_vllmException - 2 validation errors:\n  {'loc': ('body', 'tools', 0, 'type'), 'msg': \"Input should be 'function'\", 'input': 'web_search_20250305'}\n  {'loc': ('body', 'tools', 0, 'function'), 'msg': 'Field required'}\nReceived Model Group=local/vllm/qwen2.5-3b-instruct\n```\n\nThe Anthropic web-search tool is provider-specific; the local SLM has no equivalent. FS2A.web_search_assistant is a **capability-bound task**, not a tier/quality choice — it has to route to Anthropic via OpenRouter regardless of the active `LLM_MODEL_SET`.\n\n### Proposed follow-up\n\nAdd an optional `model_set` field to `LLMTaskDefinition` so capability-bound tasks can declare their required set in `config/llm_tasks.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[FS2A.web_search_assistant]\ntier = \"medium\"\nmodel_set = \"openrouter_anthropic\"\ndescription = \"Anthropic web search via OpenRouter; not available on the local SLM.\"\n```\n\nIn `resolve_task_model()`: if the task definition declares `model_set`, use it; otherwise fall back to the existing explicit-arg → context → env → default chain.\n\n### Why this isn't bundled into PR #265\n\nSPI-276 is scoped to \"stop sending the bare-prefix alias.\" The capability-bound routing change is a new concept (a new field on `LLMTaskDefinition`, a new resolver rule) that affects all tasks and warrants its own review. PR #265 already pins this in `### Out of scope (deliberately)` and the parser fix it makes is unlocked once the capability-bound routing follow-up lands.\n\n### Plan\n\nWill stack a follow-up branch on top of `sumeet/spi-276-strip-openrouter-prefix-direct-litellm-calls` once PR #265 is ready for review or merged. Will note \"Gated on PR #265\" in the follow-up PR body so the verification checklist doesn't run prematurely."

def load_llm_task_definitions(
    *,
    config_path: Path | str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, LLMTaskDefinition]:
    path = resolve_llm_tasks_config_path(config_path)
    mtime_ns = path.stat().st_mtime_ns if path.exists() else -1
    cached = _load_llm_task_definitions_cached(str(path), mtime_ns)
    return {
        task_id: LLMTaskDefinition(
            task_id=task_id,
            tier=LLMTier(task_payload["tier"]),
            description=str(task_payload["description"]),
        )
        for task_id, task_payload in cached
    }


@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def _load_llm_tier_profiles_cached(path_text: str, mtime_ns: int) -> tuple[tuple[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]], ...]:
    path = Path(path_text)
    if mtime_ns < 0 or not path.exists():
        raise ValueError(f"LLM tier config is required but missing: {path}")

    payload = _load_toml_mapping(path)
    default_models = _parse_tier_model_table(payload.get(DEFAULT_MODEL_SET_NAME), model_set_name=DEFAULT_MODEL_SET_NAME)
    profiles: dict[str, dict[LLMTier, str]] = {DEFAULT_MODEL_SET_NAME: default_models}

    raw_model_sets = payload.get("model_set")
    if isinstance(raw_model_sets, Mapping):
        for raw_name, raw_table in raw_model_sets.items():
            name = str(raw_name or "").strip()
            if not name:
                continue
            profiles[name] = _parse_tier_model_table(raw_table, model_set_name=name)

    return _freeze_profiles(profiles)

@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def _load_llm_task_definitions_cached(path_text: str, mtime_ns: int) -> tuple[tuple[str, dict[str, str]], ...]:
    path = Path(path_text)
    if mtime_ns < 0 or not path.exists():
        raise ValueError(f"LLM task config is required but missing: {path}")

    payload = _load_toml_mapping(path)
    tasks: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    _collect_task_definitions(payload, prefix=(), out=tasks)
    if not tasks:
        raise ValueError(f"LLM task config at {path} does not define any tasks")
    return tuple((task_id, dict(task_payload)) for task_id, task_payload in sorted(tasks.items()))


def resolve_tier_model(
    tier: str | LLMTier,
    *,
    model_set: str | None = None,
    llm_profile: str | None = None,
    config_path: Path | str | None = None,
) -> str:
    resolved_tier = normalize_tier(tier)
    selection = resolve_model_set_selection(model_set, llm_profile=llm_profile)
    model_sets = load_llm_tier_profiles(config_path=config_path)
    tier_models = model_sets.get(selection.name)
    if tier_models is None:
        available = ", ".join(sorted(model_sets))
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown model_set {selection.name!r}; available model sets: {available}")
    model = str(tier_models.get(resolved_tier) or "").strip()
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"model_set {selection.name!r} does not define tier {resolved_tier.value!r}")
    return model


def resolve_llm_profile_capabilities(
    *,
    model_set: str | None = None,
    profile_name: str | None = None,
    config_path: Path | str | None = None,
) -> LLMModelSetCapabilities:
    selection = resolve_model_set_selection(model_set, llm_profile=profile_name)
    capabilities = load_llm_profile_capabilities(config_path=config_path)
    model_set_capabilities = capabilities.get(selection.name)
    if model_set_capabilities is None:
        available = ", ".join(sorted(capabilities))
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown model_set {selection.name!r}; available model sets: {available}")
    return model_set_capabilities

def _collect_task_definitions(
    node: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    prefix: tuple[str, ...],
    out: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
) -> None:
    if "tier" in node or "description" in node:
        if not prefix:
            raise ValueError("LLM task definitions must live under a task_id path")
        if set(node.keys()) != {"tier", "description"}:
            extras = ", ".join(sorted(set(node.keys()) - {"tier", "description"}))
            raise ValueError(f"LLM task {'.'.join(prefix)!r} has unsupported keys: {extras}")
        task_id = ".".join(prefix)
        tier = normalize_tier(node.get("tier", ""))
        description = str(node.get("description") or "").strip()
        if not description:
            raise ValueError(f"LLM task {task_id!r} must define a non-empty description")
        if task_id in out:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate LLM task_id declared: {task_id}")
        out[task_id] = {"tier": tier.value, "description": description}
        return

    for raw_key, raw_value in node.items():
        key = str(raw_key or "").strip()
        if not key:
            raise ValueError("LLM task config keys must be non-empty")
        if not isinstance(raw_value, Mapping):
            raise ValueError(f"LLM task namespace {'.'.join((*prefix, key))!r} must be a TOML table")
        _collect_task_definitions(_mapping(raw_value), prefix=(*prefix, key), out=out)

) -> dict[LLMTier, str]:

        raise ValueError(f"model_set {model_set_name!r} must be a TOML table")

def resolve_task_tier(
    task_id: str,
    *,
    tasks_config_path: Path | str | None = None,
) -> LLMTier:
    normalized_task_id = str(task_id or "").strip()
    tasks = load_llm_task_definitions(config_path=tasks_config_path)
    task = tasks.get(normalized_task_id)
    if task is None:
        available = ", ".join(sorted(tasks))
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown LLM task_id {normalized_task_id!r}; declared tasks: {available}")
    return task.tier

> DEVELOPER

so tell me exactly what this thing does???

> AGENT

The two PRs together fix FS2A web search on staging. Plain English:

**The job of FS2A web search**: when the pipeline researches a forecasting question, one of the things it does is "go ask Claude to search the web and tell me what it found." That's the FS2A web_search_assistant call — it uses Anthropic's built-in web search tool (Claude actually queries the web, gets back articles, and hands us URLs + titles + snippets to feed into FS3 indicator extraction).

**What was broken** (three layers, peeled one at a time):

1. **The bare-prefix 400** (PR #265, SPI-276): the old code called `litellm.completion(model="openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4", api_base=<our proxy>)`. LiteLLM's client library saw the `openrouter/` prefix, decided "ah, OpenRouter call," and stripped the prefix before sending — so the proxy received the bare `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`, didn't recognise that alias (we only register `openrouter/anthropic/...`), and rejected every request with HTTP 400. Web search returned zero candidates. Pipeline fell back to template indicators.

2. **The parser was looking in the wrong field** (also PR #265): even if the 400 hadn't fired, the original parser was reading `message.provider_specific_fields["web_search_results"]` — a field that LiteLLM's *client* library invents when you call Anthropic directly. Once you go through the proxy (which routes through OpenRouter, which currently routes through Google's Anthropic-compatible endpoint), the web-search results come back in a different shape: OpenAI-style `message.annotations[].url_citation`. So the parser would have returned zero results either way. PR #265 now reads both shapes.

3. **The local SLM has no web search** (PR #268): staging's default `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm` routes every "medium tier" task to the local Qwen 3B running on vLLM. But Qwen doesn't have a web-search tool — it only accepts standard OpenAI function tools. So FS2A web search would 400 again, this time from vLLM rejecting the unfamiliar tool shape. Fix: declare FS2A as "capability-bound" in `config/llm_tasks.toml` (`model_set = "openrouter_anthropic"`), so it always routes to Anthropic via OpenRouter regardless of what the rest of the pipeline is using.

**What the combined change does for you**:

When the pipeline runs FS2A web search now, it: (a) calls the proxy with the full model alias preserved → no 400, (b) the proxy forwards to OpenRouter → Anthropic, which actually does the web searching, (c) the results come back as `url_citation` annotations, (d) the parser picks them up and turns them into Candidate objects for FS3, (e) FS3 indicator extraction now has real source titles to work with instead of falling back to template indicators, (f) the downstream stage scorecards flip from `partial` back to `ok`, and (g) all of this works whether you have `LLM_MODEL_SET=openrouter_anthropic` or `local_slm` — the rest of the pipeline can run on the cheap local SLM while web search alone gets the Anthropic capability it needs.

Proven on staging: under `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm`, calling `get_web_search_candidates("IAEA Iran nuclear inspection 2026")` returned 2 real candidates (IAEA + Al Jazeera) with titles, URLs, and summaries.

Confirmed via `grep -r extract_causal_relationships` — no callers.\n  * Drop the now-unused `json` import and renumber section headers.\n\n* `tests/test_llm_task_enforcement.py`\n  * Empty `DIRECT_LITELLM_ALLOWLIST` and rename the test to `test_production_code_has_no_direct_litellm_calls` with a docstring pinning the SPI-276 explanation.\n\n* `packages/inference/llm/tiers.py`\n  * `LLMTaskDefinition` gains `model_set: str | None = None`.\n  * `_collect_task_definitions` accepts the new key, requires it to be non-empty when present, and rejects unknown keys as before.\n  * Factor out `_lookup_task_definition()`; `resolve_task_tier()` is now a thin wrapper around it.\n  * `resolve_task_model()` chooses the effective model_set as: explicit caller arg → `task.model_set` → existing (context → env → default) chain.\n\n* `config/llm_tasks.toml`\n  * `[FS2A.web_search_assistant]` gains `model_set = \"openrouter_anthropic\"`. Description rewritten to explain *why* (Anthropic web search has no SLM equivalent).\n\n### Tests\n\n* New `tests/test_research_driver_web_search_client.py`:\n  * `test_get_web_search_candidates_preserves_full_model_alias` — patches `openai.OpenAI`, captures `chat.completions.create(**kwargs)`, asserts `kwargs[\"model\"]` is the full openrouter alias (not the bare form) and asserts the Anthropic web-search tool ships in `extra_body` rather than at the top level.\n  * `test_get_web_search_candidates_short_circuits_when_proxy_unconfigured` — without `LITELLM_PROXY_BASE_URL` / `LITELLM_API_KEY` we return `[]` and never construct an OpenAI client.\n  * `test_parse_search_results_reads_provider_specific_fields_from_dict` — LiteLLM-native shape end-to-end (two results, missing-URL skip, citations grouped by URL).\n  * `test_parse_search_results_reads_openai_url_citation_annotations` — exact wire shape captured from the staging proxy: `annotations[].url_citation` with title + url; verifies both entries surface and the assistant-text fallback attaches `cited_text` by domain match.\n  * `test_parse_search_results_annotations_and_psf_dedup_by_url` — same URL in both shapes is returned once.\n  * `test_parse_search_results_handles_web_search_tool_error_block` — error block logs and returns no results.\n  * `test_parse_search_results_with_empty_provider_specific_fields_is_safe` — empty / `None` paths don't blow up.\n* `tests/test_llm_tiers.py`:\n  * `test_live_fs2a_web_search_assistant_pins_to_openrouter_anthropic` — guards the live TOML declaration; under `LLM_MODEL_SET=local_slm`, FS2A still resolves to an `openrouter/anthropic/...` alias.\n  * `test_task_model_set_override_pins_task_to_declared_set` — three-way: per-task override wins over env, plain tasks still honour env, explicit caller-supplied `model_set` still wins over the per-task override.\n  * `test_task_model_set_override_must_be_non_empty` — empty string raises at load.\n  * `test_task_model_set_override_unknown_set_raises_at_resolution` — unknown name raises with the existing \"Unknown model_set\" error message at resolve time.\n\n### Verification\n\n- [x] `uv run ruff check .`\n- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`\n- [x] `uv run python -m pytest --ignore=tests/frontend -x -q` — 1355 passed, 8 skipped (full suite green on commit 7db89af). BODY:
## What this is

@kungfusaini This draft PR adds a standalone, exportable UI wireframe package for the Elijah workspace router. It is intentionally isolated to `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/**` so reviewers can inspect or copy the prototype without pulling in live app code, product APIs, persistence, migrations, or process metadata.

The package includes a logon flow, workspace menu, Analyst Workspace, Bet Pricer, and Operator Lab wireframe screens. The Analyst screen includes the old-UI-style graph workspace, local Cytoscape/Dagre vendor files, Graph/Table/Both display modes, node and edge table views, source document placeholders, and wireframe-only interactions.

## Technical detail

### Summary

- Adds one self-contained static wireframe directory under `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/`.
- Keeps the PR to one commit and 15 files, all under that directory.
- Excludes `agent_rules` run records, sprint metadata, and unrelated dirty worktree changes.

### Approach

- Branched from current `dev` at `47c8693`.
- Restored only `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/` from `dev_sprint` commit `7574603`.
- Vendored all runtime assets needed by the static Analyst graph inside the directory.

### Tests

- `git diff --check dev...HEAD`
- `node` syntax parse over executable script tags in `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`
- Focused Playwright smoke from a local static server covering direct `index.html`, login -> menu, direct `analyst-workspace.html`, Analyst Graph/Table/Both modes, node-type table filtering, table-row node/edge viewer activation, and desktop/mobile layout sanity.

### Verification

- `git rev-list --count dev..HEAD` returned `1`.
- `git diff --name-only dev...HEAD` contains only `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/**` paths.
- Broad repo pre-push gates were deliberately not run because this is a draft PR for a static isolated wireframe artifact.

### Risks

- The vendor JavaScript files increase the diff size, but keep the artifact exportable and offline-friendly.
- The wireframe is static demo behavior only; it is not wired to production auth, APIs, persistence, or routing.

### Branch-merge

- Source branch: `codex/workspace-router-wireframe`
- Target branch: `dev`
- Draft PR for review; do not merge until explicitly approved.

### Out of scope (deliberately)

- Product authentication, API integration, database persistence, migrations, and live frontend route changes.
- Agent run-record metadata and `agent_rules/runs/INDEX.md` updates.
- Broad repository formatting, mypy, pytest, Docker, or compose gates.

=== kungfusaini at 2026-05-18T13:18:32Z ===
@hqmf8104 — first pass of review feedback below. Grouping by area for readability. Happy to chat through any of these.

## Auth + landing flow

**Drop the `#login` form entirely.** Cloudflare Zero Trust already authenticates the user at the edge (Cloudflare emails a one-time code, sets cookies, and the request hits the SPA already carrying the `Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email` header that SPI-243 wires into `request.state.user`). An in-app login form would be a second auth step that does nothing real and risks looking like a phishing redirect.

**Drop the workspace picker too.** For the Monday demo, the Bet Pricer and Operator Lab aren't audience-facing — they'll be moved to separate URLs outside this main flow. So: after Cloudflare, the user lands **straight in the Analyst Workspace (Graph Review)**. No tile picker, no choice screen. The `#bet-pricer` / `#operator-lab` / `#menu` routes can stay in the codebase as scaffolding for the post-demo workspace router vision, but the demo build should route directly.

**Branded login moment.** The "branded login" lives on the Cloudflare Access page itself, not in the app. The plan for that:
- **For the Monday demo:** Layer 1 — Zero Trust dashboard branding (brand color, header text, footer text). Free, ~10 min in the CF dashboard.
- **Already in place** by virtue of the team-slug subdomain (`elijahintelligence.cloudflareaccess.com`). A true custom auth subdomain (e.g. `auth.elijahintelligence.com`) is a separate CNAME setup if we want it.
- **Post-demo:** Layer 3 — fully custom HTML/CSS login page (CF Teams Standard+) when we want pixel-perfect match with the workspace UI.

**Logo:** intentionally leaving it out of both the CF login page and the wireframe's branding slots for the demo. Assets are available in `frontend/assets/log2{l,d}.{svg,png}` when we're ready, but it's not blocking.

## Analyst Workspace — top nav + chrome

**Show the currently signed-in user.** The top nav has no indication of who is signed in. Add an identity badge — top-right of the nav strip is the natural home — showing the user's email (the value SPI-243 lands as `request.state.user`). Minimum for the demo: just the email as a small chip. Logout / "switch user" / account menu can wait for SPI-176 / 177.

**Drop the sidebar "E" watermark.** The decorative "E" at the bottom of the left sidebar (`<div class="sidebar-watermark">` around `analyst-workspace.html:189`) is visual noise. The brand "E" in the top nav already covers identity.

## Analyst Workspace — Job Status card

**Replace the "Status options" disclosure with a hover tooltip.** The current `<details class="job-state-disclosure">` gallery shows all 7 status states as a list, which doesn't help anyone. Drop the disclosure entirely. Instead, when the user hovers the **current** job-status pill, surface a tooltip that explains only that state. The pill is the source of truth; the hover answers "what does this state mean?" in context, not "here's every state we could be in."

## Analyst Workspace — prediction visibility

**Make the headline prediction the visual hero.** The workspace currently surfaces the question, graph, drivers, indicators, edges, and job status — but the actual predicted probability isn't obvious at a glance. The whole point of a run is to produce that number; it shouldn't require hunting. Add a prominent prediction card (likely top of the left sidebar, above the "Active question" card, or a hero strip below the top nav) showing the headline probability for a binary, or ranked option probabilities for a multi-choice, plus a confidence indicator. A user glancing at the screen should be able to read "67% — yes, with medium confidence" without scrolling.

## Analyst Workspace — run history

**Surface previous runs of a question.** The wireframe shows the latest state for the active question but exposes no way to see prior runs or load their graphs. Add a "Run history" picker (likely beside or under the question selector in the top nav) listing past runs for the active question with timestamp and headline metric (e.g. Brier, completion status). Clicking a past run loads its graph, edges, and supporting data into the workspace view. The backend data is already there: `runs` is keyed by `question_id`, and `nodes` / `edges` / `llm_prompt_traces` rows are all scoped by `run_id`. For the demo this can be read-only; compare-runs and annotations are post-demo.

## Graph interaction

**Hover affordance on graph elements.** Hovering over a node or edge currently does nothing. Add a hover tooltip surfacing useful at-a-glance information — exact contents TBD, but reasonable starting set:
- **Node hover:** title, type (driver / indicator / question / option), baseline probability, confidence, evidence count, one-line summary
- **Edge hover:** parent → child relationship label, conditional P(child|parent), odds multiplier, direction

Implementation can lean on Cytoscape's `mouseover` event + a tooltip layer. The full detail panel can stay a click affordance.

**Make rationale prominent in the node detail panel.** When a user clicks a node, the side panel currently hides or de-emphasises the rationale text. The rationale is the most useful payload of a node — promote it to a prominent position in the panel (near the top, clear heading, full text body), not buried under collapsibles or below low-value metadata.

## Graph legend

**Dotted-line legend swatches don't render as dotted.** Legend entries labelled as "dotted" lines look solid (or whatever the default is). Either the `stroke-dasharray` isn't being applied to the legend swatches, or the swatch markup is using the wrong shape — visual-fidelity bug; the legend needs to actually match the lines drawn in the graph.

**Drop ALL CAPS and rewrite the cryptic edge-type copy.** Entries like `CONDITIONAL influence` and `REFERENCE provenance/evidence` read like raw enum values bleeding into the UI, and the meaning isn't clear at a glance. Fix:
- Title Case the type name (or drop the type name entirely).
- Replace the cryptic descriptors with a plain-English explanation. Suggested rewrites (final wording TBD):
  - **Conditional influence** → "Causal influence — parent driver shifts the child's probability"
  - **Reference provenance/evidence** → "Evidence link — source document that supports this node"
- Worth a sweep for the same all-caps-enum pattern elsewhere (node types, statuses) so the wireframe doesn't ship with raw schema values in the chrome.

1	(function () {
2	  const routeLabels = {
3	    login: "Workspace Logon",
4	    menu: "Choose Workspace",
5	    analyst: "Analyst Workspace",
6	    "bet-pricer": "Bet Pricer",
7	    "operator-lab": "Operator Lab",
8	  };
9	
10	  const workspaceRoutes = new Set(["analyst", "bet-pricer", "operator-lab"]);
11	  const screens = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-screen]"));
12	  const workspaceViews = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-route]"));
13	  const routeButtons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-route-target]"));
14	  const workspaceScreen = document.querySelector(".workspace-screen");
15	  const workspaceTitle = document.getElementById("workspaceTitle");
16	  const loginForm = document.getElementById("loginForm");
17	  const printButton = document.getElementById("printButton");
18	
19	  function currentRoute() {
20	    const raw = window.location.hash.replace(/^#\/?/, "");
21	    return routeLabels[raw] ? raw : "login";
22	  }
23	
24	  function setRoute(route) {
25	    window.location.hash = route === "login" ? "login" : route;
26	  }
27	
28	  function render() {
29	    const route = currentRoute();
30	    const isWorkspace = workspaceRoutes.has(route);
31	
32	    screens.forEach((screen) => {
33	      const name = screen.getAttribute("data-screen");
34	      const activeName = isWorkspace ? "workspace" : route;
35	      screen.classList.toggle("active", name === activeName);
36	    });
37	
38	    workspaceViews.forEach((view) => {
39	      view.classList.toggle("active", view.getAttribute("data-route") === route);
40	    });
41	
42	    routeButtons.forEach((button) => {
43	      const target = button.getAttribute("data-route-target");
44	      button.classList.toggle("active", target === route);
45	      if (target === route) {
46	        button.setAttribute("aria-current", "page");
47	      } else {
48	        button.removeAttribute("aria-current");
49	      }
50	    });
51	
52	    if (workspaceTitle) {
53	      workspaceTitle.textContent = routeLabels[route] || routeLabels.login;
54	    }
55	
56	    if (workspaceScreen) {
57	      workspaceScreen.setAttribute("data-active-route", route);
58	    }
59	
60	    document.title = `Elijah - ${routeLabels[route] || routeLabels.login} Wireframe`;
61	  }
62	
63	  routeButtons.forEach((button) => {
64	    button.addEventListener("click", () => {
65	      setRoute(button.getAttribute("data-route-target"));
66	    });
67	  });
68	
69	  loginForm.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
70	    event.preventDefault();
71	    setRoute("menu");
72	  });
73	
74	  printButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
75	    window.print();
76	  });
77	
78	  window.addEventListener("hashchange", render);
79	
80	  if (!window.location.hash) {
81	    setRoute("login");
82	  } else {
83	    render();
84	  }
85	})();
86

Largest type in the sidebar — it's the whole point of\n   running the pipeline; users shouldn't have to scroll to find the number. */\n.prediction-hero-card {\n  border-color: rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.45);\n  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(8, 47, 73, 0.55), rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.65));\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-head {\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 8px;\n  margin-bottom: 6px;\n}\n\n.prediction-confidence {\n  padding: 2px 8px;\n  border-radius: 999px;\n  background: rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.15);\n  color: var(--t2, #cbd5e1);\n  font-size: 10.5px;\n  letter-spacing: 0.02em;\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-body {\n  display: flex;\n  flex-direction: column;\n  gap: 2px;\n  margin-bottom: 6px;\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-value {\n  font-size: 36px;\n  line-height: 1.05;\n  color: #a5f3fc;\n  letter-spacing: -0.01em;\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-label {\n  font-size: 12.5px;\n  color: var(--t1, #e2e8f0);\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-meta {\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 8px;\n  font-size: 10.5px;\n  color: var(--t2, #94a3b8);\n}\n\n.prediction-hero-delta {\n  color: #6ee7b7;\n}\n\n/* Job-state tooltip. Replaces the old `<details>` gallery; hover/focus the\n   current pill to see what *this* state means. */\n.job-state-pill-hover {\n  cursor: help;\n  outline: none;\n}\n\n.job-state-pill-hover:focus-visible {\n  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.45);\n}\n\n.job-state-tooltip {\n  margin-top: 8px;\n  padding: 8px 10px;\n  border: 1px solid rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.28);\n  border-radius: 8px;\n  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.92);\n  color: var(--t1, #e2e8f0);\n  font-size: 11.5px;\n  line-height: 1.4;\n}\n\n.job-state-tooltip[hidden] {\n  display: none;\n}\n\n/* Graph hover tooltip. Floats above the cytoscape canvas; the click affordance\n   still opens the full detail panel. */\n.graph-hover-tooltip {\n  position: absolute;\n  z-index: 240;\n  max-width: 280px;\n  padding: 10px 12px;\n  border: 1px solid rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.32);\n  border-radius: 10px;\n  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.96);\n  color: var(--t1, #e2e8f0);\n  font-size: 11.5px;\n  line-height: 1.4;\n  pointer-events: none;\n  box-shadow: 0 18px 38px rgba(2, 6, 23, 0.5);\n}\n\n.graph-hover-tooltip.hidden {\n  display: none;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-head {\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: baseline;\n  flex-wrap: wrap;\n  gap: 6px;\n  margin-bottom: 4px;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-type {\n  padding: 1px 6px;\n  border-radius: 999px;\n  background: rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.18);\n  color: var(--t2, #cbd5e1);\n  font-size: 10px;\n  letter-spacing: 0.04em;\n  text-transform: none;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-title {\n  font-weight: 600;\n  color: #e2e8f0;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-endpoints {\n  margin: 2px 0 4px;\n  color: var(--t1, #e2e8f0);\n}\n\n.graph-hover-stats {\n  display: grid;\n  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;\n  gap: 2px 12px;\n  margin-top: 4px;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-row {\n  display: flex;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n  gap: 8px;\n  color: var(--t2, #94a3b8);\n}\n\n.graph-hover-row strong {\n  color: var(--t1, #e2e8f0);\n  font-weight: 600;\n}\n\n.graph-hover-summary {\n  margin-top: 6px;\n  padding-top: 6px;\n  border-top: 1px solid rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.18);\n  color: var(--t2, #94a3b8);\n  font-size: 11px;\n  line-height: 1.45;\n}\n\n/* Legend swatch consistency fix. (it'll auto-default to `#analyst` so you'll land straight in the Analyst Workspace — no login screen, no picker)

A few URLs worth poking at to verify the review feedback in context:

- **http://localhost:8765/#analyst** — Analyst Workspace (the demo landing). Things to look at: prediction hero card at top-left, identity badge top-right of the nav, run-history picker next to the question selector, hover any node or edge to see the new tooltip, hover the green "succeeded" pill in Job Status to see the new in-context state explanation, scroll the legend to see the dashed-vs-solid line styles now render properly with the rewritten copy.
- **http://localhost:8765/#menu** — Workspace picker (scaffolding only, no longer the default).
- **http://localhost:8765/#bet-pricer** and **http://localhost:8765/#operator-lab** — the other two wireframe destinations; the topbar identity badge shows here too.

- Identity values (`analyst@elijah.example`, `3 of 10 runs`) and the run-history options are all static wireframe placeholders — they'll come from the CF Access header + the demo quota service once we wire them.

  "new_string": "      // Follow the cursor, but with enough offset to keep the tooltip clear\n      // of the cursor itself *and* clear of the typical node radius — so the\n      // user can still read the underlying graph element while reading the\n      // tooltip. Flips horizontally if the right-side placement would run off\n      // the graph container; clamps vertically inside the container.\n      const TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP = 28;\n\n      function positionHoverTooltip(renderedPosition) {\n        if (!hoverTooltip || !hoverContainerEl || !renderedPosition) return;\n        const rect = hoverContainerEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n        const tipW = hoverTooltip.offsetWidth;\n        const tipH = hoverTooltip.offsetHeight;\n        const minX = 6;\n        const minY = 6;\n        const maxX = Math.max(minX, rect.width - tipW - 6);\n        const maxY = Math.max(minY, rect.height - tipH - 6);\n\n        // Prefer to the right of the cursor; flip to the left if it would\n        // overflow the container.\n        let x = renderedPosition.x + TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP;\n        if (x > maxX) {\n          x = renderedPosition.x - TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP - tipW;\n        }\n        // Vertically centre on the cursor so the tooltip never floats above\n        // or below the action.\n        let y = renderedPosition.y - tipH / 2;\n\n        hoverTooltip.style.left = Math.max(minX, Math.min(x, maxX)) + \"px\";\n        hoverTooltip.style.top = Math.max(minY, Math.min(y, maxY)) + \"px\";\n      }\n\n      function showHoverTooltip(html, renderedPosition) {\n        if (!hoverTooltip || !html) return;\n        hoverTooltip.innerHTML = html;\n        hoverTooltip.classList.remove(\"hidden\");\n        hoverTooltip.setAttribute(\"aria-hidden\", \"false\");\n        positionHoverTooltip(renderedPosition);\n      }\n\n      function hideHoverTooltip() {\n        if (!hoverTooltip) return;\n        hoverTooltip.classList.add(\"hidden\");\n        hoverTooltip.setAttribute(\"aria-hidden\", \"true\");\n      }\n\n      cy.on(\"mouseover\", \"node\", (event) => {\n        const raw = ensureNodeInfo(event.target.data(\"raw\")) || event.target.data();\n        showHoverTooltip(nodeHoverHtml(raw), event.renderedPosition);\n      });\n      cy.on(\"mouseover\", \"edge\", (event) => {\n        const raw = event.target.data(\"raw\") || event.target.data();\n        showHoverTooltip(edgeHoverHtml(event.target, raw), event.renderedPosition);\n      });\n      cy.on(\"mousemove\", \"node, edge\", (event) => {\n        if (hoverTooltip && !hoverTooltip.classList.contains(\"hidden\")) {\n          positionHoverTooltip(event.renderedPosition);\n        }\n      });\n      cy.on(\"mouseout\", \"node, edge\", hideHoverTooltip);\n      cy.on(\"tapstart pan zoom\", hideHoverTooltip);"

(above/below cursor). */\n.graph-hover-tooltip {\n  position: absolute;\n  z-index: 240;\n  max-width: 280px;\n  padding: 10px 12px;\n  border: 1px solid rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.32);\n  border-radius: {

If that\n        // would push the bottom off the container, flip so the tooltip ends\n        // just below the cursor row instead.\n        let y = renderedPosition.y + TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y;\n        if (y + tipH > rect.height - 6) {\n          y = renderedPosition.y - tipH - TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y;\n        }\n\n        hoverTooltip.style.left = Math.max(minX, Math.min(x, maxX)) + \"px\";\n        hoverTooltip.style.top = Math.max(minY, Math.min(y, maxY)) + \"px\";\n      }",
  "new_string": "        // Prefer to the right of the cursor; flip to the left if it would\n        // overflow the container.\n        let flippedHorizontally = false;\n        let x = renderedPosition.x + TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X;\n        if (x > maxX) {\n          x = renderedPosition.x - TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X - tipW;\n          flippedHorizontally = true;\n        }\n        // Anchor the tooltip's top edge a small distance above the cursor so\n        // the body extends downward from the cursor row (classic OS-tooltip\n        // pattern, not \"tooltip floating high above the cursor\"). If that\n        // would push the bottom off the container, flip so the tooltip ends\n        // just below the cursor row instead.\n        let flippedVertically = false;\n        let y = renderedPosition.y + TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y;\n        if (y + tipH > rect.height - 6) {\n          y = renderedPosition.y - tipH - TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y;\n          flippedVertically = true;\n        }\n\n        hoverTooltip.style.left = Math.max(minX, Math.min(x, maxX)) + \"px\";\n        hoverTooltip.style.top = Math.max(minY, Math.min(y, maxY)) + \"px\";\n\n        // Speech-bubble tail goes on whichever corner is closest to the\n        // cursor. The fill is a closed polygon;\n      // the stroke is an open polyline that skips the base, so the join with\n      // the bubble's border looks seamless. Geometry runs in container px\n      // and is mapped to SVG userspace via viewBox.\n      function updateTooltipTail(cursorX, cursorY, tipLeft, tipTop, tipW, tipH, flippedH, flippedV) {\n        if (!hoverTail || !hoverTailFill || !hoverTailStroke || !hoverContainerEl) return;\n        const rect = hoverContainerEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n        hoverTail.setAttribute(\"viewBox\", `0 0 ${rect.width} ${rect.height}`);\n        hoverTail.classList.remove(\"hidden\");\n\n        // Pick the bubble edge facing the cursor and find its midpoint\n        // anchor (the centre of the tail's base).\n        const isAbove = !flippedV;   // bubble sits above cursor -> tail on bubble's bottom edge\n        const isRight = !flippedH;   // bubble sits right of cursor -> tail base sits on the LEFT side of the bubble's bottom edge (closer to the cursor's column)\n\n        let baseY;\n        if (isAbove) {\n          baseY = tipTop + tipH;        // bottom edge of bubble\n        } else {\n          baseY = tipTop;               // top edge of bubble (flipped)\n        }\n\n        let baseCenterX;\n        if (isRight) {\n          baseCenterX = tipLeft + TOOLTIP_TAIL_BASE_W;\n        } else {\n          baseCenterX = tipLeft + tipW - TOOLTIP_TAIL_BASE_W;\n        }\n\n        const halfBase = TOOLTIP_TAIL_BASE_W / 2;\n        const a1x = baseCenterX - halfBase;\n        const a2x = baseCenterX + halfBase;\n        const a1 = `${a1x},${baseY}`;\n        const a2 = `${a2x},${baseY}`;\n        const tip = `${cursorX},${cursorY}`;\n\n        hoverTailFill.setAttribute(\"points\", `${a1} ${a2} ${tip}`);\n        // Polyline is OPEN — base side is omitted so the bubble's bottom\n        // border stays the visible join line.\n        hoverTailStroke.setAttribute(\"points\", `${a1} ${tip} ${a2}`);\n      }\n\n      function positionHoverTooltip(renderedPosition) {\n        if (!hoverTooltip || !hoverContainerEl || !renderedPosition) return;\n        const rect = hoverContainerEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n        const tipW = hoverTooltip.offsetWidth;\n        const tipH = hoverTooltip.offsetHeight;\n        const minX = 6;\n        const minY = 6;\n        const maxX = Math.max(minX, rect.width - tipW - 6);\n        const maxY = Math.max(minY, rect.height - tipH - 6);\n\n        // Prefer to the right of the cursor; flip to the left if it would\n        // overflow the container.\n        let flippedHorizontally = false;\n        let x = renderedPosition.x + TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X;\n        if (x > maxX) {\n          x = renderedPosition.x - TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X - tipW;\n          flippedHorizontally = true;\n        }\n        // Anchor the tooltip's top edge a small distance above the cursor so\n        // the body extends downward from the cursor row. An SVG sibling that draws a triangle from two anchor\n   points on the bubble's nearest edge to a third point at the cursor — so\n   the tail's tip actually reaches the cursor instead of sitting on the\n   bubble's corner. The fill matches the bubble background; the stroke is the\n   open polyline (only the two angled sides, never the base), so the join\n   with the bubble's border stays seamless. Perfect. Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile a comprehensive report.

## Cytoscape Graph Layout & Rendering Analysis

### 1. Current Layout Configuration (lines 1642–1652)

**Layout Engine:** Dagre (cytoscape-dagre 2.5.0, line 12)
- **rankDir:** `"LR"` (left-to-right)
- **ranker:** `"longest-path"` — prioritizes longest dependency chains over compact layout
- **nodeSep:** 44px
- **edgeSep:** 18px — **this is the critical value**: defines minimum spacing between edges *within* a rank
- **rankSep:** 205px — spacing between ranks (information → indicator → driver → target)
- **padding:** 36px

Post-layout, `alignTargets()` (line 1626) vertically re-aligns target nodes by their x-position. The grouped layout (`applyGroupedLayout`, line 1918) uses fixed column offsets (line 1931) and a preset layout.

### 2. Current Edge Style Configuration (lines 1569–1583)

- **curve-style:** `"bezier"` (line 1575) — cubic Bézier curves with automatic control points
- **No control-point-distances, segment-distances, or taxi-style settings** — all use Cytoscape defaults
- **Multi-edge handling:** No explicit bundling or de-conflicting strategy. Parallel edges (multiple Information nodes → same Driver) rely on dagre's edgeSep and natural curve deviation

**Problem identified:** `edgeSep: 18` applies only *between ranks*. A direct info→driver edge and an indirect info→indicator→driver path traverse *different ranks*, so the 18px separation doesn't prevent the intermediate Indicator node from occluding the shortcut edge.

### 3. Graph Topology in Demo Data (lines 588–823)

**Nodes:** 4 Information, 3 Drivers, 6 Indicators, 2 Targets

**Direct edges (shortcuts):** Information → Driver (reference edges, lines 590–611)
- `info_storage_procurement` → `driver_procurement`
- `info_interconnection_queue` → `driver_queue`
- `info_developer_finance` → `driver_finance`
- `info_policy_target` → `driver_procurement` (duplicate target)

**Indirect edges:** Information → Indicator (lines 614–647), then Indicator → Driver (lines 740–821)
- Example: `info_storage_procurement` → `indicator_pace` (line 616) → `driver_procurement` (line 742)

**The bug scenario** occurs when, e.g.:
- Direct: `info_storage_procurement` → `driver_procurement`
- Indirect: `info_storage_procurement` → `indicator_pace` → `driver_procurement`

The Indicator node lands *between* these two layers, and its position (computed by dagre) places it on or near the Bézier curve of the shortcut edge.

### 4. Layout Code Paths

- **Cytoscape init:** line 1521 — no special edge-rendering options beyond curve-style
- **Layout trigger:** `runLayout()` at line 1640 — calls dagre with the config above
- **Layout stop callback:** `alignTargets()` and `fitVisibleElements()` at lines 1654–1657
- **Grouped layout:** `applyGroupedLayout()` at line 1918 uses `preset` layout with fixed x/y positions, overriding dagre entirely

### 5. Available Built-in Knobs for the Fix

**From cytoscape-dagre 2.5.0 (already loaded):**
- `ranker` options: `"network-simplex"` (default), `"tight-tree"`, `"longest-path"` (current) — different ranking strategies could reorder nodes to minimize crossings
- No native `edgeSpacing` parameter that spans multiple ranks or applies globally

**From Cytoscape 3.29.2:**
- `unbundled-bezier`: Would allow fine-grained control-point placement (4+ control points per edge) — **NOT currently loaded**
- `taxi` + `segments`: Orthogonal routing with explicit turn points — would bypass curved-edge occlusion entirely
- `haystack`: Bundled edge routing — groups parallel edges together
- `loop-direction` / `segment-distances`: For self-loops and multi-segment edges

**Realistic options without new dependencies:**
1. **Switch to `taxi` curve-style:** Orthogonal paths inherently avoid node occlusion (dagre supports this)
2. **Increase `edgeSep`:** Already 18px; limited effect across ranks
3. **Switch ranker to `"network-simplex"`:** May reduce intermediate-node placement in shortcut paths
4. **Post-process Bézier control points:** JavaScript can manually adjust bezier handles after layout to arc around the Indicator node

---

**Key Finding:** The issue is that dagre's `edgeSep` only enforces spacing *within a single rank*. A direct cross-rank edge and a multi-hop path don't conflict at the layout level—they collide only in rendered 2D space. The `bezier` curve-style lacks explicit control-point routing. Switching to `taxi` (orthogonal) routing would be the simplest built-in fix.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/.claude/plans/polymorphic-strolling-metcalfe.md",
  "content": "# Workspace wireframe — bend shortcut edges around obstructing nodes\n\n## Context\n\nThe Analyst Workspace graph (PR #220, `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`) uses Cytoscape with `curve-style: \"bezier\"` and a dagre layout (`rankDir: \"LR\"`, `ranker: \"longest-path\"`). When the demo data — or any future graph — contains a direct shortcut edge (e.g. `info_storage_procurement → driver_procurement`) **and** an indirect path through an Indicator (`info_storage_procurement → indicator_pace → driver_procurement`), dagre places the Indicator on the straight horizontal line between Info and Driver. A bezier edge with no explicit control points renders as a near-straight line on a left-to-right layout, so the shortcut edge runs through the Indicator node and is completely hidden by it. The user only sees the shortcut after manually dragging the Indicator out of the way — clearly bad for a demo.\n\nThis is the canonical \"edge passes through unrelated node\" problem in dagre-style hierarchical layouts. The dagre layout has no edge routing of its own; the visual fix has to come from Cytoscape's edge-style block.\n\n## Approach\n\nSwitch the edge style from `bezier` → `unbundled-bezier` with a single uniform control-point offset so every edge gains a gentle arc. Cross-rank shortcut edges arc visibly above the intermediate rank (clearing the Indicator); short edges within a rank get an imperceptibly small arc. Cytoscape's automatic bezier offset for parallel edges between the same source/target pair still applies, so multi-edges keep their existing separation.\n\nTwo new style properties in the `selector: \"edge\"` block (`analyst-workspace.html:1568-1584`):\n\n```js\n\"curve-style\": \"unbundled-bezier\",\n\"control-point-distances\": [40],\n\"control-point-weights\": [0.5],\n\"edge-distances\": \"node-position\",\n```\n\n- `control-point-distances: [40]` — pixels perpendicular to the source→target line; one control point at 40px offset. Positive value arcs the edge \"above\" in the layout's rendering frame. Tuned for the LR rank direction with `rankSep: 205` — 40px is ~20% of inter-rank spacing, enough to clear a node radius (~30px) plus its label without making short edges look bent.\n- `control-point-weights: [0.5]` — the control point sits at the midpoint of the edge, so the arc is symmetric.\n- `edge-distances: \"node-position\"` — endpoints anchor to node centres rather than border intersections, which keeps the arc geometry consistent regardless of node shape (the wireframe mixes circles, diamonds, triangles, rectangles).\n\nNo layout change — dagre keeps positioning nodes the same way, which preserves the rest of the wireframe's visual grammar. The only thing that changes is how edges draw between those positions.\n\n## Critical files\n\n- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html` — edit the edge style block at lines 1568-1584. No other files need changes; no JS data shape changes (`arrowScale`, `width`, `color`, `lineStyle` per-edge data continues to work unchanged).\n\n## Verification\n\n1. Reload http://localhost:8765/ in the browser (the local server is still running).\n2. The default demo graph already exercises the bug: `info_storage_procurement → driver_procurement` is a shortcut alongside `info_storage_procurement → indicator_pace → driver_procurement`. Confirm the shortcut edge is now visible without dragging the Indicator. Same check for the `info_policy_target → driver_procurement` shortcut.\n3. Hover the Indicator and confirm the tooltip + click-to-open-detail panel still work (no JS regressions).\n4. Click the **Both** display-mode button and confirm the same edges look right when the graph is compressed beside the tables.\n5. Sanity-check the other view-mode and graph-grouping toggles (Layout dropdown → Group by Driver / Indicator / etc.) still render edges without overlap. The grouped layout uses `preset` positions (`applyGroupedLayout`, line 1918) and will inherit the same arc, so it's worth a quick look.\n6. If 40px arc looks too aggressive on short edges or too subtle on long ones, the constant is the only knob to tune. Acceptable range observed in similar Cytoscape demos: 25-60px.\n\n## Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- No change to dagre `ranker`, `nodeSep`, `edgeSep`, or `rankSep`. Switching `ranker` to `network-simplex` was considered but it reorders nodes globally and changes the overall layout shape — too disruptive for a \"just fix the overlap\" change, and dagre's longest-path ranker is what produced the current layout the team has been reviewing.\n- No switch to `taxi` (orthogonal) routing. It also fixes the overlap but changes the graph from \"flowing causal diagram\" to \"circuit schematic,\" which is a much larger aesthetic change than the user asked for. Keep as a fallback if the bezier arc still leaves overlaps on richer datasets.\n- No per-edge programmatic control-point computation (would be needed to make the arc adaptive to local density). The uniform 40px arc is the smallest change that solves the demo dataset.\n"
}

## Approved Plan:
# Workspace wireframe — replace dagre with cytoscape-elk for smarter node placement

## Context

The Analyst Workspace graph (PR #220, `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`) uses Cytoscape with `curve-style: "bezier"` and a cytoscape-dagre layout. Because dagre's node-placement is a naïve Sugiyama variant, it routinely positions an intermediate-rank node directly on the straight line between two non-adjacent nodes that also share a shortcut edge. The shortcut (e.g. `info_storage_procurement → driver_procurement`) is drawn as a near-straight line that vanishes underneath the obstructing Indicator (`indicator_pace`). The user has to drag the Indicator out of the way to see the shortcut. The same pattern shows up wherever the demo data has both `Info → Indicator → Driver` and `Info → Driver` edges.

The user wants straight edges (no arcs, no orthogonal turns, no bends) and the obstructing nodes shifted out of the way at layout time. The canonical library answer is Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), wrapped for Cytoscape as `cytoscape-elk`. Its `layered` algorithm with the `BRANDES_KOEPF` node-placement strategy is significantly better than dagre at placing intermediate-rank nodes off the natural lines of shortcut edges. With `edgeRouting: UNDEFINED`, ELK only handles node placement — Cytoscape continues to draw straight bezier edges between the placed nodes — so the user's "no bends" requirement is satisfied.

## Approach

Replace cytoscape-dagre with cytoscape-elk as the layout engine for the Analyst Workspace graph. Keep the existing edge style (`curve-style: "bezier"`, filled arrows, `data(color)` / `data(width)` / `data(lineStyle)`) untouched — only the node-placement algorithm changes. The post-layout `alignTargets()` and `fitVisibleElements()` callbacks still run on the new positions.

### CDN swap

Replace the three `<script>` tags at `analyst-workspace.html:10-12`:

```html
<!-- remove -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dagre@0.8.5/dist/dagre.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/cytoscape-dagre@2.5.0/cytoscape-dagre.min.js"></script>
```

with:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/elkjs@0.9.3/lib/elk.bundled.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/cytoscape-elk@2.2.0/dist/cytoscape-elk.js"></script>
```

Keep the existing `cytoscape@3.29.2` script tag — cytoscape-elk requires it. ELK.js (bundled) and the cytoscape-elk wrapper are both MIT-licensed and pinned to released versions, matching the README's "Pinned graph libraries" convention.

### Layout config

Rewrite `runLayout()` (currently `analyst-workspace.html:1640-1659`) to call ELK with `BRANDES_KOEPF` placement and undefined edge routing. Keep the same `alignTargets` + `fitVisibleElements` postlude:

```js
function runLayout() {
  const layoutName = window.cytoscapeElk ? "elk" : "grid";
  const layout = cy.layout({
    name: layoutName,
    elk: {
      "algorithm": "layered",
      "elk.direction": "RIGHT",                                    // matches the prior LR rank direction
      "elk.edgeRouting": "UNDEFINED",                              // let Cytoscape draw straight bezier edges
      "elk.nodePlacement.strategy": "BRANDES_KOEPF",               // the smart placer that avoids on-edge collisions
      "elk.layered.crossingMinimization.strategy": "LAYER_SWEEP",  // default, called out for clarity
      "elk.spacing.nodeNode": 44,                                  // ~matches dagre nodeSep
      "elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers": 205,            // ~matches dagre rankSep
      "elk.spacing.edgeNode": 25,                                  // extra cushion against an edge passing too close to a node
    },
    fit: true,
    padding: 36,
    animate: true,
    animationDuration: 500,
    animationEasing: "ease-out-cubic",
  });
  layout.one("layoutstop", () => {
    alignTargets();
    fitVisibleElements();
  });
  layout.run();
}
```

The grid fallback (used when the elk wrapper failed to load) preserves the same defensive behaviour the dagre version had.

### What does NOT change

- The edge style block at `analyst-workspace.html:1568-1584` — bezier, `target-arrow-fill: filled`, `data(color)`, `data(width)`, etc. all stay exactly as they are.
- Per-edge data computed in `buildElements()` (`arrowScale`, `width`, `color`, `lineStyle`).
- The `applyGroupedLayout` preset path (`analyst-workspace.html:1918`) — group-by uses hand-picked column positions, not the layout engine.
- All click / hover / drag / context-menu handlers.
- The README's "Pinned graph libraries" section gets the dagre line replaced with the elk + cytoscape-elk lines.

## Critical files

- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`
  - Replace the dagre + cytoscape-dagre CDN tags (lines 10–12) with elk.bundled.js + cytoscape-elk.
  - Rewrite `runLayout()` (lines 1640–1659) per the snippet above. Replace `window.cytoscapeDagre` check with `window.cytoscapeElk`.
- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/README.md`
  - Replace the three `Dagre 0.8.5 / cytoscape-dagre 2.5.0` lines in the "Pinned graph libraries" list with `ELK.js 0.9.3 / cytoscape-elk 2.2.0`.

## Verification

1. Reload http://localhost:8765/ in the browser (the local server is still running).
2. Confirm the graph renders (3 Drivers, 6 Indicators, 4 Information, 2 Targets, in roughly the same left-to-right flow as before).
3. The two known shortcut cases in the demo data must be visible without dragging anything:
   - `info_storage_procurement → driver_procurement` shortcut alongside `info_storage_procurement → indicator_pace → driver_procurement`.
   - `info_policy_target → driver_procurement` shortcut alongside `info_policy_target → indicator_capex → driver_procurement`.
4. Confirm edges are straight bezier lines (no bends, no arcs).
5. Hover any node / edge — the new tooltip from the previous commit should still work; click should still open the detail panel.
6. Layout dropdown → Group by Driver / Indicator / etc. should still work (these go through `applyGroupedLayout`, not `runLayout`).
7. Open the JS console and confirm no errors about missing `cytoscapeDagre` or about unknown ELK options. If ELK warns about an unknown option, drop the corresponding key from the elk block (ELK is forgiving but each release renames a handful).
8. Drag a node and confirm Cytoscape still re-renders edges live.
9. If on a rare future dataset the smart placement still leaves a collision, the existing `alignTargets()` runs after layout and could be extended with a small node-nudge pass — out of scope for this change.

## Out of scope (deliberately)

- Removing the `applyGroupedLayout` preset path or rewriting it on top of ELK. The preset positions are user-meaningful (one column per node type) and ELK's layered algorithm would change that shape.
- Any change to edge rendering (curve-style stays bezier; arrows, colours, line styles, hover tooltip, mid-edge arrowheads — all unchanged).
- Removing or repinning cytoscape itself. The version stays at 3.29.2 because cytoscape-elk 2.2.0 declares it as a peer.
- Bundling the libraries instead of CDN-loading. The wireframe is intentionally "open the HTML file, no build step" per the README.

> AGENT

The topology you're seeing: `info_developer_finance` has **three** outgoing edges (to `driver_finance` directly AND to `indicator_capex` AND to `indicator_financing_spread`), with both indicators feeding back into `driver_finance` via `CONDITIONAL` edges. ELK can't avoid that natural alignment — when source and final target are colinear and the intermediate has to sit on the path, BRANDES_KOEPF still puts it on the line.

ELK got us 80% of the way. The remaining cases need either (a) more bends (which you rejected) or (b) a tiny post-layout pass that nudges any node sitting on a non-incident edge perpendicular off the line — running AFTER ELK so we get the best of both. Let me propose that:

  "new_string": "      // Finishing pass that runs AFTER ELK and AFTER alignTargets. Detects\n      // nodes that ended up sitting on an edge they aren't part of (the\n      // residual \"indicator perfectly horizontal between an info and its\n      // driver\" case ELK's smart placement doesn't always avoid) and moves\n      // them perpendicular off the line so the obscured edge becomes\n      // visible. Edges stay straight; only the obstructing node moves.\n      function nudgeNodesOffEdges() {\n        const CLEAR_RADIUS = 30;   // node radius + small padding\n        const NUDGE_PADDING = 4;   // extra cushion past the clear radius\n        const MAX_PASSES = 3;      // a moved node may obstruct a new edge\n        for (let pass = 0; pass < MAX_PASSES; pass++) {\n          let movedAny = false;\n          cy.nodes().forEach((node) => {\n            const nodeId = node.id();\n            const np = node.position();\n            cy.edges().forEach((edge) => {\n              if (edge.source().id() === nodeId || edge.target().id() === nodeId) return;\n              const s = edge.source().position();\n              const t = edge.target().position();\n              const dx = t.x - s.x;\n              const dy = t.y - s.y;\n              const len2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n              if (len2 < 1) return;\n              // u in [0,1] = how far along the edge the node's projection sits\n              const u = ((np.x - s.x) * dx + (np.y - s.y) * dy) / len2;\n              if (u < 0.05 || u > 0.95) return;   // node is near an endpoint, not in the middle\n              const closestX = s.x + u * dx;\n              const closestY = s.y + u * dy;\n              const distX = np.x - closestX;\n              const distY = np.y - closestY;\n              const dist = Math.sqrt(distX * distX + distY * distY);\n              if (dist >= CLEAR_RADIUS) return;\n              // Perpendicular unit vector to the edge.\n              const len = Math.sqrt(len2);\n              const perpX = -dy / len;\n              const perpY = dx / len;\n              // Sign: nudge in whichever perpendicular direction the node is\n              // already on; if it's exactly on the line, pick +1 (down).\n              let sign = distX * perpX + distY * perpY;\n              if (Math.abs(sign) < 0.001) {\n                sign = 1;\n              } else {\n                sign = sign > 0 ? 1 : -1;\n              }\n              const nudgeAmount = CLEAR_RADIUS - dist + NUDGE_PADDING;\n              node.position({\n                x: np.x + perpX * sign * nudgeAmount,\n                y: np.y + perpY * sign * nudgeAmount,\n              });\n              movedAny = true;\n            });\n          });\n          if (!movedAny) break;\n        }\n      }\n\n      function alignTargets() {\n        const targets = cy.nodes('[type = \"target\"]');"
}

> AGENT

I think the gap change is taking effect but with a 280px-wide tooltip the perceived distance is dominated by the tooltip's own width — not the gap. When flipped, the user reads from the tooltip's LEFT edge which is `width + gap` from the cursor. Dropping the gap from 28 to 6 only moves things by 22px, which is barely visible next to 280px of tooltip.

Real fix: narrow the tooltip when flipped so the text starts closer to the cursor.

> TOOL

> AGENT

Got it — it's the cytoscape zoom level. As graph zooms in/out (which happens when the pane resizes and `fit: true` rescales the graph), node sizes change but the tooltip offset is hardcoded in pixels. So the offset feels "huge" relative to small nodes when zoomed out, "right" when zoomed in. Fix: scale the offset by current zoom.

1	# Workspace wireframe — replace dagre with cytoscape-elk for smarter node placement
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The Analyst Workspace graph (PR #220, `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`) uses Cytoscape with `curve-style: "bezier"` and a cytoscape-dagre layout. Because dagre's node-placement is a naïve Sugiyama variant, it routinely positions an intermediate-rank node directly on the straight line between two non-adjacent nodes that also share a shortcut edge. The shortcut (e.g. `info_storage_procurement → driver_procurement`) is drawn as a near-straight line that vanishes underneath the obstructing Indicator (`indicator_pace`). The user has to drag the Indicator out of the way to see the shortcut. The same pattern shows up wherever the demo data has both `Info → Indicator → Driver` and `Info → Driver` edges.
6	
7	The user wants straight edges (no arcs, no orthogonal turns, no bends) and the obstructing nodes shifted out of the way at layout time. The canonical library answer is Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), wrapped for Cytoscape as `cytoscape-elk`. Its `layered` algorithm with the `BRANDES_KOEPF` node-placement strategy is significantly better than dagre at placing intermediate-rank nodes off the natural lines of shortcut edges. With `edgeRouting: UNDEFINED`, ELK only handles node placement — Cytoscape continues to draw straight bezier edges between the placed nodes — so the user's "no bends" requirement is satisfied.
8	
```

> AGENT

Existing plan is about the ELK layout switch — a completely different (and already-shipped) task. Overwriting with the tooltip-positioning plan after a deeper look at what's actually broken.

The two complaints are symptoms of the same underlying mistake: **horizontal-flip cursor-following is the wrong pattern for a wide tooltip on a graph canvas.** Industry standard (D3, Highcharts, Chart.js, Linear's chart tooltips, Grafana, ECharts) is vertical positioning with horizontal centering, because it solves both problems at once.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/.claude/plans/polymorphic-strolling-metcalfe.md",
  "content": "# Workspace wireframe — flip the tooltip positioning from horizontal-flip to vertical-anchor\n\n## Context\n\nThe Analyst Workspace graph hover tooltip uses a cursor-following positioning pattern that sits the tooltip 44px to the *right* of the cursor by default and flips it to the *left* of the cursor (`cursor.x - 6 - tipW`) when the right-side placement would overflow the graph pane (`docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`, around lines 2474-2500). It has two failure modes the user has hit:\n\n1. **\"Still too far when flipped left.\"** When the tooltip flips left, the user reads from the tooltip's *left edge*, which sits at `cursor.x - gap - tipW`. With the bubble ~180-280px wide, the user's eye has to travel that whole width from the cursor to reach the first character — no matter how small `gap` is set. We have already tried gap=6 and an automatic narrowing class (`--flipped` → max-width: 180px) and the perceived distance is still wrong because the limiting factor is the bubble's own width, not the gap.\n2. **\"Glitches and teleports when flipping a lot.\"** Near the flip threshold (cursor.x ≈ `maxX`), tiny mouse movements alternate between right-side and left-side placement. The tooltip teleports ~200-300px horizontally on each flip because the flip distance is `2 × gap + tipW`. The mousemove handler runs the placement every cytoscape event, so a rapidly-moving cursor near the boundary produces a strobing tooltip.\n\nBoth failure modes are caused by the same design choice: **horizontal-axis flipping for a tooltip that is wider than the flip is small**. The canonical fix in data-viz tooling — D3 chart tooltips, Highcharts, Chart.js, Apache ECharts, Linear's chart tooltips, Grafana panel tooltips — is to anchor the tooltip *vertically* above the cursor and centre it *horizontally* on the cursor, flipping only below the cursor when there's no room above. The flip dimension becomes a few pixels of vertical position change instead of 250+ pixels of horizontal jump, and the tooltip's left edge is always `cursor.x - tipW/2` away from the cursor — symmetric and always close in both visual halves of the bubble.\n\n## Approach\n\nRewrite `positionHoverTooltip()` to anchor the tooltip vertically. Drop the horizontal flip and the `--flipped` narrowing class entirely. Add a tiny piece of session-scoped state so the vertical flip (which only matters near the very top of the graph pane) doesn't oscillate during a single hover.\n\n### New positioning algorithm\n\n```js\n// Inputs: renderedPosition (cursor in container px), hoverTooltip, hoverContainerEl\n// Constants:\nconst TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP = 14;        // cursor → tooltip vertical gap on whichever side\nconst TOOLTIP_HORIZONTAL_BLEED = 12;    // allow the tooltip to overshoot the cursor's x by this much when clamped to an edge\n\nfunction positionHoverTooltip(renderedPosition) {\n  if (!hoverTooltip || !hoverContainerEl || !renderedPosition) return;\n  const rect = hoverContainerEl.getBoundingClientRect();\n  const tipW = hoverTooltip.offsetWidth;\n  const tipH = hoverTooltip.offsetHeight;\n  const minX = 6;\n  const minY = 6;\n  const maxX = Math.max(minX, rect.width - tipW - 6);\n  const maxY = Math.max(minY, rect.height - tipH - 6);\n\n  // Horizontal: centre the tooltip on the cursor, then clamp to the container.\n  // No flip — the text-start is always tipW/2 away from the cursor regardless\n  // of which side of the container the cursor is on.\n  let x = renderedPosition.x - tipW / 2;\n  x = Math.max(minX, Math.min(x, maxX));\n\n  // Vertical: above the cursor by default, with session-scoped hysteresis so\n  // the flip never oscillates during a single hover. tooltipVerticalFlip is\n  // reset to false in hideHoverTooltip() — so each new hover starts with the\n  // preferred \"above\" placement.\n  let y;\n  const aboveY = renderedPosition.y - TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP - tipH;\n  if (!tooltipVerticalFlip && aboveY < minY) {\n    tooltipVerticalFlip = true;\n  }\n  if (tooltipVerticalFlip) {\n    y = renderedPosition.y + TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP;\n  } else {\n    y = aboveY;\n  }\n  y = Math.max(minY, Math.min(y, maxY));\n\n  hoverTooltip.style.left = x + \"px\";\n  hoverTooltip.style.top = y + \"px\";\n}\n```\n\n### Hysteresis state\n\nA single module-scoped boolean (`let tooltipVerticalFlip = false;`) declared next to `hoverTooltip` declaration. The flip becomes `true` the first time `aboveY < minY` during a hover and stays `true` until `hideHoverTooltip()` resets it to `false` on mouseout. This means a single hover never sees more than one flip — no strobing.\n\n### What gets removed\n\n- `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_RIGHT`, `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_LEFT`, `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y` constants.\n- The horizontal flip branch (`if (x > maxX) { ... }`).\n- `hoverTooltip.classList.add/remove(\"graph-hover-tooltip--flipped\")` and the helper that re-reads `offsetWidth` after toggling the class.\n- The `.graph-hover-tooltip--flipped` CSS rule in `legacy-wireframe.css` (no longer referenced).\n\n### What stays unchanged\n\n- `mouseover` and `mousemove` cytoscape handlers — they still call `positionHoverTooltip(event.renderedPosition)`.\n- `showHoverTooltip` (the function that renders the content and calls positionHoverTooltip).\n- `hideHoverTooltip` (extended only to reset `tooltipVerticalFlip = false`).\n- The hover content builders (`nodeHoverHtml`, `edgeHoverHtml`) and everything they touch.\n- The job-state pill tooltip and run-history picker added in the earlier review pass.\n\n## Critical files\n\n- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`\n  - Declare `let tooltipVerticalFlip = false;` near the existing `hoverTooltip` / `hoverContainerEl` declarations (around line 2399).\n  - Replace the body of `positionHoverTooltip` (around lines 2478-2499) with the algorithm above.\n  - Extend `hideHoverTooltip` (around lines 2510-2515) to set `tooltipVerticalFlip = false`.\n  - Replace `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_RIGHT`/`_LEFT`/`OFFSET_Y` constants (around lines 2474-2476) with the new `TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP` constant.\n- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/legacy-wireframe.css`\n  - Delete the `.graph-hover-tooltip--flipped { max-width: 180px; }` rule and its comment block (around lines 1103-1110) since the flip is gone.\n\n## Verification\n\n1. Reload http://localhost:8765/ in the browser (the local server is still running).\n2. Hover a node in the *middle* of the graph: tooltip should sit *above* the cursor, horizontally centred on the cursor, ~14px above the cursor's row.\n3. Hover a node on the *right edge* of the graph (the case that triggered the old left-flip): tooltip stays above the cursor, NOT flipped to the left. The horizontal clamp keeps the tooltip's right edge inside the container; the tooltip's text-start is always tipW/2 from the cursor (consistent, never \"miles away\").\n4. Hover a node on the *left edge* of the graph: same behaviour — above the cursor, clamped to fit, text-start at tipW/2 from cursor.\n5. Hover a node near the *top edge* of the graph: tooltip flips *below* the cursor (the only remaining flip). Movement around that node should not oscillate — once flipped, the tooltip stays below for the entire hover. Moving off and back onto the node should reset to \"above\" placement if there's room.\n6. Move the cursor rapidly back and forth across what used to be the right-edge flip boundary: the tooltip should NOT teleport horizontally any more — it follows the cursor smoothly because there is no horizontal flip.\n7. Hover an edge instead of a node: same positioning rules apply. The edge-hover tooltip content is unchanged.\n8. Resize the browser window: the tooltip position recomputes on every mousemove/mouseover, so the new container bounds apply on the next event. No stale positioning.\n9. Job-status pill hover and run-history picker are unrelated and should still work as before — only the graph hover tooltip positioning changes.\n"
}
