## Approved Plan:
# Workspace wireframe — flip the tooltip positioning from horizontal-flip to vertical-anchor

## Context

The Analyst Workspace graph hover tooltip uses a cursor-following positioning pattern that sits the tooltip 44px to the *right* of the cursor by default and flips it to the *left* of the cursor (`cursor.x - 6 - tipW`) when the right-side placement would overflow the graph pane (`docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`, around lines 2474-2500). It has two failure modes the user has hit:

1. **"Still too far when flipped left."** When the tooltip flips left, the user reads from the tooltip's *left edge*, which sits at `cursor.x - gap - tipW`. With the bubble ~180-280px wide, the user's eye has to travel that whole width from the cursor to reach the first character — no matter how small `gap` is set. We have already tried gap=6 and an automatic narrowing class (`--flipped` → max-width: 180px) and the perceived distance is still wrong because the limiting factor is the bubble's own width, not the gap.
2. **"Glitches and teleports when flipping a lot."** Near the flip threshold (cursor.x ≈ `maxX`), tiny mouse movements alternate between right-side and left-side placement. The tooltip teleports ~200-300px horizontally on each flip because the flip distance is `2 × gap + tipW`. The mousemove handler runs the placement every cytoscape event, so a rapidly-moving cursor near the boundary produces a strobing tooltip.

Both failure modes are caused by the same design choice: **horizontal-axis flipping for a tooltip that is wider than the flip is small**. The canonical fix in data-viz tooling — D3 chart tooltips, Highcharts, Chart.js, Apache ECharts, Linear's chart tooltips, Grafana panel tooltips — is to anchor the tooltip *vertically* above the cursor and centre it *horizontally* on the cursor, flipping only below the cursor when there's no room above. The flip dimension becomes a few pixels of vertical position change instead of 250+ pixels of horizontal jump, and the tooltip's left edge is always `cursor.x - tipW/2` away from the cursor — symmetric and always close in both visual halves of the bubble.

## Approach

Rewrite `positionHoverTooltip()` to anchor the tooltip vertically. Drop the horizontal flip and the `--flipped` narrowing class entirely. Add a tiny piece of session-scoped state so the vertical flip (which only matters near the very top of the graph pane) doesn't oscillate during a single hover.

### New positioning algorithm

```js
// Inputs: renderedPosition (cursor in container px), hoverTooltip, hoverContainerEl
// Constants:
const TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP = 14;        // cursor → tooltip vertical gap on whichever side
const TOOLTIP_HORIZONTAL_BLEED = 12;    // allow the tooltip to overshoot the cursor's x by this much when clamped to an edge

function positionHoverTooltip(renderedPosition) {
  if (!hoverTooltip || !hoverContainerEl || !renderedPosition) return;
  const rect = hoverContainerEl.getBoundingClientRect();
  const tipW = hoverTooltip.offsetWidth;
  const tipH = hoverTooltip.offsetHeight;
  const minX = 6;
  const minY = 6;
  const maxX = Math.max(minX, rect.width - tipW - 6);
  const maxY = Math.max(minY, rect.height - tipH - 6);

  // Horizontal: centre the tooltip on the cursor, then clamp to the container.
  // No flip — the text-start is always tipW/2 away from the cursor regardless
  // of which side of the container the cursor is on.
  let x = renderedPosition.x - tipW / 2;
  x = Math.max(minX, Math.min(x, maxX));

  // Vertical: above the cursor by default, with session-scoped hysteresis so
  // the flip never oscillates during a single hover. tooltipVerticalFlip is
  // reset to false in hideHoverTooltip() — so each new hover starts with the
  // preferred "above" placement.
  let y;
  const aboveY = renderedPosition.y - TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP - tipH;
  if (!tooltipVerticalFlip && aboveY < minY) {
    tooltipVerticalFlip = true;
  }
  if (tooltipVerticalFlip) {
    y = renderedPosition.y + TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP;
  } else {
    y = aboveY;
  }
  y = Math.max(minY, Math.min(y, maxY));

  hoverTooltip.style.left = x + "px";
  hoverTooltip.style.top = y + "px";
}
```

### Hysteresis state

A single module-scoped boolean (`let tooltipVerticalFlip = false;`) declared next to `hoverTooltip` declaration. The flip becomes `true` the first time `aboveY < minY` during a hover and stays `true` until `hideHoverTooltip()` resets it to `false` on mouseout. This means a single hover never sees more than one flip — no strobing.

### What gets removed

- `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_RIGHT`, `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_LEFT`, `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_OFFSET_Y` constants.
- The horizontal flip branch (`if (x > maxX) { ... }`).
- `hoverTooltip.classList.add/remove("graph-hover-tooltip--flipped")` and the helper that re-reads `offsetWidth` after toggling the class.
- The `.graph-hover-tooltip--flipped` CSS rule in `legacy-wireframe.css` (no longer referenced).

### What stays unchanged

- `mouseover` and `mousemove` cytoscape handlers — they still call `positionHoverTooltip(event.renderedPosition)`.
- `showHoverTooltip` (the function that renders the content and calls positionHoverTooltip).
- `hideHoverTooltip` (extended only to reset `tooltipVerticalFlip = false`).
- The hover content builders (`nodeHoverHtml`, `edgeHoverHtml`) and everything they touch.
- The job-state pill tooltip and run-history picker added in the earlier review pass.

## Critical files

- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`
  - Declare `let tooltipVerticalFlip = false;` near the existing `hoverTooltip` / `hoverContainerEl` declarations (around line 2399).
  - Replace the body of `positionHoverTooltip` (around lines 2478-2499) with the algorithm above.
  - Extend `hideHoverTooltip` (around lines 2510-2515) to set `tooltipVerticalFlip = false`.
  - Replace `TOOLTIP_CURSOR_GAP_X_RIGHT`/`_LEFT`/`OFFSET_Y` constants (around lines 2474-2476) with the new `TOOLTIP_VERTICAL_GAP` constant.
- `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/legacy-wireframe.css`
  - Delete the `.graph-hover-tooltip--flipped { max-width: 180px; }` rule and its comment block (around lines 1103-1110) since the flip is gone.

## Verification

1. Reload http://localhost:8765/ in the browser (the local server is still running).
2. Hover a node in the *middle* of the graph: tooltip should sit *above* the cursor, horizontally centred on the cursor, ~14px above the cursor's row.
3. Hover a node on the *right edge* of the graph (the case that triggered the old left-flip): tooltip stays above the cursor, NOT flipped to the left. The horizontal clamp keeps the tooltip's right edge inside the container; the tooltip's text-start is always tipW/2 from the cursor (consistent, never "miles away").
4. Hover a node on the *left edge* of the graph: same behaviour — above the cursor, clamped to fit, text-start at tipW/2 from cursor.
5. Hover a node near the *top edge* of the graph: tooltip flips *below* the cursor (the only remaining flip). Movement around that node should not oscillate — once flipped, the tooltip stays below for the entire hover. Moving off and back onto the node should reset to "above" placement if there's room.
6. Move the cursor rapidly back and forth across what used to be the right-edge flip boundary: the tooltip should NOT teleport horizontally any more — it follows the cursor smoothly because there is no horizontal flip.
7. Hover an edge instead of a node: same positioning rules apply. The edge-hover tooltip content is unchanged.
8. Resize the browser window: the tooltip position recomputes on every mousemove/mouseover, so the new container bounds apply on the next event. No stale positioning.
9. Job-status pill hover and run-history picker are unrelated and should still work as before — only the graph hover tooltip positioning changes.

> AGENT

Found the actual bug. The cytoscape canvas (`#cy`) is offset 96px from the left of the graph pane via `inset: 54px 42px 40px 96px` — but at narrow widths the media query sets `inset: auto`, so the offset becomes 0. The tooltip's `style.left` is relative to the graph pane, while `renderedPosition` is relative to the `#cy` canvas. The 96px (or 0px) mismatch is exactly the "distance changes with screen size" bug.

> TOOL

The #cy canvas is inset\n        // from the graph pane by its CSS inset (96px left / 54px top at\n        // wide screens, 0/0 at narrow screens via media query). {
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/220-wireframe/docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html",
  "old_string": "      // Job-state pill tooltip. Replaces the old `<details>` gallery of all\n      // 7 states with an in-context explanation of the current state only.\n      const jobStatePill = document.getElementById(\"jobStatePill\");\n      const jobStateTooltip = document.getElementById(\"jobStateTooltip\");\n      const JOB_STATE_COPY = {\n        idle: \"Waiting for a run. No work has been queued for this question yet.\",\n        queued: \"Waiting for worker capacity. The job is in line and will start as soon as a worker is free.\",\n        running: \"Evidence and graph steps are active right now. The graph and forecast will refresh when the run completes.\",\n        succeeded: \"Completed with artifacts. The run finished cleanly and produced graph, forecast, and evidence artifacts.\",\n        partial: \"Completed with review flags. Some stages succeeded, others need a second look — open the Probability Forecast card for the breakdown.\",\n        failed: \"Stopped on an error. The most recent attempt did not produce a usable forecast; check the worker logs or re-run.\",\n        cancelled: \"Stopped by operator action. The run was cancelled before it completed; no forecast was produced.\",\n      };\n\n      function updateJobStateTooltip() {\n        if (!jobStatePill || !jobStateTooltip) return;\n        const state = jobStatePill.getAttribute(\"data-job-state\") || \"succeeded\";\n        jobStateTooltip.textContent = JOB_STATE_COPY[state] || \"Status detail unavailable.\";\n      }\n\n      function showJobStateTooltip() {\n        if (!jobStatePill || !jobStateTooltip) return;\n        updateJobStateTooltip();\n        jobStateTooltip.hidden = false;\n      }\n\n      function hideJobStateTooltip() {\n        if (!jobStateTooltip) return;\n        jobStateTooltip.hidden = true;\n      }\n\n      if (jobStatePill && jobStateTooltip) {\n        updateJobStateTooltip();\n        jobStatePill.addEventListener(\"mouseenter\", showJobStateTooltip);\n        jobStatePill.addEventListener(\"mouseleave\", hideJobStateTooltip);\n        jobStatePill.addEventListener(\"focus\", showJobStateTooltip);\n        jobStatePill.addEventListener(\"blur\", hideJobStateTooltip);\n      }",
  "new_string": "      // Job-status stepper. Drives the four steps (idle → queued → running\n      // → terminal) from a single `data-job-state` attribute on the\n      // stepper element. The terminal step adopts the label + colour of\n      // whichever final state was reached (succeeded / partial / failed /\n      // cancelled); past steps fill in completion colour, the current\n      // step gets a ring, future steps stay outlined. Hovering any step\n      // shows the plain-English explanation for that state in the\n      // shared tooltip below the stepper.\n      const jobStatusStepper = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusStepper\");\n      const jobStateTooltip = document.getElementById(\"jobStateTooltip\");\n      const jobStateLabel = document.getElementById(\"jobStateLabel\");\n      const jobStatusTerminalLabel = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusTerminalLabel\");\n\n      const JOB_STATE_COPY = {\n        idle: \"Waiting for a run. No work has been queued for this question yet.\",\n        queued: \"Waiting for worker capacity. The job is in line and will start as soon as a worker is free.\",\n        running: \"Evidence and graph steps are active right now. The graph and forecast will refresh when the run completes.\",\n        succeeded: \"Completed with artifacts. The run finished cleanly and produced graph, forecast, and evidence artifacts.\",\n        partial: \"Completed with review flags. Some stages succeeded, others need a second look — open the Probability Forecast card for the breakdown.\",\n        failed: \"Stopped on an error. The most recent attempt did not produce a usable forecast; check the worker logs or re-run.\",\n        cancelled: \"Stopped by operator action. The run was cancelled before it completed; no forecast was produced.\",\n      };\n\n      // Where each state sits on the forward progression. Anything that's\n      // an \"end state\" (succeeded/partial/failed/cancelled) lives at the\n      // terminal slot; everything earlier walks the steps in order.\n      const JOB_STATE_PROGRESS = { idle: 0, queued: 1, running: 2, succeeded: 3, partial: 3, failed: 3, cancelled: 3 };\n      const TERMINAL_STATES = new Set([\"succeeded\", \"partial\", \"failed\", \"cancelled\"]);\n\n      function titleCaseState(state) {\n        return state ? state.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + state.slice(1) : \"\";\n      }\n\n      function applyJobStatusStepper() {\n        if (!jobStatusStepper) return;\n        const state = (jobStatusStepper.getAttribute(\"data-job-state\") || \"succeeded\").toLowerCase();\n        const progressIndex = JOB_STATE_PROGRESS[state] ?? 3;\n        const isTerminal = TERMINAL_STATES.has(state);\n        if (jobStateLabel) jobStateLabel.textContent = titleCaseState(state);\n        if (jobStatusTerminalLabel) {\n          jobStatusTerminalLabel.textContent = isTerminal ? titleCaseState(state) : \"Succeeded\";\n        }\n        const stepEls = Array.from(jobStatusStepper.querySelectorAll(\".job-status-step\"));\n        stepEls.forEach((stepEl, idx) => {\n          stepEl.classList.remove(\"is-past\", \"is-current\", \"is-future\");\n          // The terminal step adopts the actual end-state name so its CSS\n          // colour reacts (succeeded → green, partial → amber, etc.).\n          if (stepEl.dataset.step === \"terminal\") {\n            stepEl.dataset.terminalState = isTerminal ? state : \"succeeded\";\n          }\n          if (idx < progressIndex) {\n            stepEl.classList.add(\"is-past\");\n          } else if (idx === progressIndex) {\n            stepEl.classList.add(\"is-current\");\n          } else {\n            stepEl.classList.add(\"is-future\");\n          }\n        });\n      }\n\n      // The state described by hovering a step. Past/future steps use their\n      // own state name; the terminal step uses whichever end state is set\n      // on the stepper.\n      function stepStateName(stepEl) {\n        const step = stepEl.dataset.step;\n        if (step !== \"terminal\") return step;\n        return (jobStatusStepper.getAttribute(\"data-job-state\") || \"succeeded\").toLowerCase();\n      }\n\n      function showJobStateTooltipFor(stepEl) {\n        if (!jobStateTooltip || !stepEl) return;\n        const state = stepStateName(stepEl);\n        jobStateTooltip.textContent = JOB_STATE_COPY[state] || \"Status detail unavailable.\";\n        jobStateTooltip.hidden = false;\n      }\n\n      function hideJobStateTooltip() {\n        if (jobStateTooltip) jobStateTooltip.hidden = true;\n      }\n\n      if (jobStatusStepper && jobStateTooltip) {\n        applyJobStatusStepper();\n        jobStatusStepper.querySelectorAll(\".job-status-step\").forEach((stepEl) => {\n          const btn = stepEl.querySelector(\".job-status-step-btn\");\n          if (!btn) return;\n          btn.addEventListener(\"mouseenter\", () => showJobStateTooltipFor(stepEl));\n          btn.addEventListener(\"mouseleave\", hideJobStateTooltip);\n          btn.addEventListener(\"focus\", () => showJobStateTooltipFor(stepEl));\n          btn.addEventListener(\"blur\", hideJobStateTooltip);\n        });\n      }"
}

1	# Workspace Router Wireframes
2	
3	Standalone exportable wireframes for an Elijah logon flow that routes to:
4	
5	- Analyst Workspace
6	- Bet Pricer
7	- Operator Lab
8	
9	Open `index.html` directly in a browser. The prototype has no app-code imports,
10	API calls, external fonts, or build step. The Analyst Workspace graph loads
11	three pinned third-party graph libraries from jsDelivr, so graph interaction
12	requires internet access.
13	
14	The Analyst Workspace route loads `analyst-workspace.html`, a self-contained
15	old-UI wireframe that vendors the legacy graph explorer stylesheet as
16	`legacy-graph.css` instead of importing from the live frontend. Its graph is
17	rendered from an inline JSON shim in the same HTML file using pinned CDN graph
18	libraries, so the checked-in artifact stays small without app-runtime imports.
19	
20	Pinned graph libraries:
21	
22	- Cytoscape `3.29.2`, MIT license
23	- ELK.js `0.9.3`, EPL-2.0 license
24	- cytoscape-elk `2.2.0`, MIT license
25	
26	The graph's information nodes point at four static lorem ipsum Markdown
27	fixtures under `ui-repository/`. These files are placeholder review documents
28	for the future document viewer and are part of the standalone export.
29	
30	## Routes
31	
32	- `index.html#login`
33	- `index.html#menu`
34	- `index.html#analyst` (embeds `analyst-workspace.html`)
35	- `index.html#bet-pricer`

These files are placeholder review documents\nfor the future document viewer and are part of the standalone export.\n\n## Routes\n\n- `index.html` — defaults to `#analyst`.\n- `index.html#analyst` (embeds `analyst-workspace.html`) — the demo landing.\n- `index.html#menu` — workspace picker (scaffolding for the post-demo router\n  vision; not reachable from the default flow).\n- `index.html#bet-pricer` — Bet Pricer screen (scaffolding).\n- `index.html#operator-lab` — Operator Lab screen (scaffolding).\n\nThe in-app login form was removed; Cloudflare Zero Trust authenticates the\nuser at the edge before the SPA loads and the topbar \"Log out\" link routes to\n`/cdn-cgi/access/logout`.\n\n## What's interactive in the Analyst Workspace\n\nMost of the wireframe is static, but a few elements have real behaviour so\nreviewers can preview the full lifecycle of the live UI without editing HTML:\n\n- **Run-history dropdown** (top nav, next to the question selector). Switches\n  the Probability hero card's \"source-run\" line *and* the Job Status stepper\n  to the option's `data-job-state`. Includes one option for every lifecycle\n  state — `idle | queued | running | succeeded | partial | failed |\n  cancelled` — so you can walk every state visually in one click each.\n- **Job Status stepper** (sidebar, \"Job Status\" card). Four-step lifecycle\n  (Idle → Queued → Running → terminal); the terminal step's colour adapts to\n  the actual end state (green / amber / red / grey). The current state's\n  plain-English description is shown directly below the stepper.\n- **Graph hover tooltip** (cytoscape canvas). Hovering any node or edge\n  surfaces a quick \"what is this?\" tooltip up-and-left of the cursor; the\n  click affordance still opens the full node-info detail panel on the left.\n- **Legend / node-type filters** (graph overlay, \"Legend\" card). Each\n  node-type row in the legend is a toggle — click to hide or show that type.\n  The filter UI lives inside the legend so the swatches and the toggles are\n  in one place.\n- **Layout dropdown** (graph controls, \"Layout\" button). Lets you group by\n  node type and adjust horizontal/vertical spacing of the layered layout.\n\n## Identity + demo quota\n\nThe Analyst Workspace sidebar shows a placeholder identity card at the\nbottom-left (avatar, email, \"X of Y runs remaining\"). This\navoids the classic dagre failure mode where an intermediate-rank node sits\ndirectly on the straight line between a non-adjacent shortcut edge —\nsignificantly reducing the cases where an Indicator obscures an\nInfo → Driver shortcut. TITLE: UI/Workspace: Add workspace router wireframe

BODY:
## What this is

@kungfusaini This draft PR adds a standalone, exportable UI wireframe package for the Elijah workspace router. It is intentionally isolated to `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/**` so reviewers can inspect or copy the prototype without pulling in live app code, product APIs, persistence, migrations, or process metadata.

The package includes a logon flow, workspace menu, Analyst Workspace, Bet Pricer, and Operator Lab wireframe screens. The Analyst screen includes the old-UI-style graph workspace, local Cytoscape/Dagre vendor files, Graph/Table/Both display modes, node and edge table views, source document placeholders, and wireframe-only interactions.

## Technical detail

### Summary

- Adds one self-contained static wireframe directory under `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/`.
- Keeps the PR to one commit and 15 files, all under that directory.
- Excludes `agent_rules` run records, sprint metadata, and unrelated dirty worktree changes.

### Approach

- Branched from current `dev` at `47c8693`.
- Restored only `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/` from `dev_sprint` commit `7574603`.
- Vendored all runtime assets needed by the static Analyst graph inside the directory.

### Tests

- `git diff --check dev...HEAD`
- `node` syntax parse over executable script tags in `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/analyst-workspace.html`
- Focused Playwright smoke from a local static server covering direct `index.html`, login -> menu, direct `analyst-workspace.html`, Analyst Graph/Table/Both modes, node-type table filtering, table-row node/edge viewer activation, and desktop/mobile layout sanity.

### Verification

- `git rev-list --count dev..HEAD` returned `1`.
- `git diff --name-only dev...HEAD` contains only `docs/wireframes/workspace-router/**` paths.
- Broad repo pre-push gates were deliberately not run because this is a draft PR for a static isolated wireframe artifact.

### Risks

- The vendor JavaScript files increase the diff size, but keep the artifact exportable and offline-friendly.
- The wireframe is static demo behavior only; it is not wired to production auth, APIs, persistence, or routing.

### Branch-merge

- Source branch: `codex/workspace-router-wireframe`
- Target branch: `dev`
- Draft PR for review; do not merge until explicitly approved.

### Out of scope (deliberately)

- Product authentication, API integration, database persistence, migrations, and live frontend route changes.
- Agent run-record metadata and `agent_rules/runs/INDEX.md` updates.
- Broad repository formatting, mypy, pytest, Docker, or compose gates.

The Analyst Workspace\ngraph loads three pinned third-party graph libraries from jsDelivr, so graph\ninteraction requires internet access.\n\nThe Analyst Workspace route loads `analyst-workspace.html`, a self-contained\nold-UI wireframe that vendors the legacy graph explorer stylesheet as\n`legacy-graph.css` instead of importing from the live frontend. Its graph is\nrendered from an inline JSON shim in the same HTML file using pinned CDN\ngraph libraries, so the checked-in artifact stays small without app-runtime\nimports.\n\nPinned graph libraries:\n\n- Cytoscape `3.29.2`, MIT license\n- ELK.js `0.9.3`, EPL-2.0 license\n- cytoscape-elk `2.2.0`, MIT license\n\nThe graph's information nodes point at four static lorem ipsum Markdown\nfixtures under `ui-repository/`. These files are placeholder review documents\nfor the future document viewer and are part of the standalone export.\n\n## Routes\n\n- `index.html` — defaults to `#analyst`.\n- `index.html#analyst` (embeds `analyst-workspace.html`) — the demo landing.\n- `index.html#bet-pricer` — Bet Pricer screen.\n- `index.html#operator-lab` — Operator Lab (tuning dashboard) screen.\n- `index.html#menu` — workspace picker (scaffolding for the post-demo\n  router vision; not reachable from the default flow).\n\nThe in-app login form was removed; Cloudflare Zero Trust authenticates the\nuser at the edge before the SPA loads and the topbar \"Log out\" link routes to\n`/cdn-cgi/access/logout`.\n\n## What's interactive in the Analyst Workspace\n\nMost of the wireframe is static, but a few elements have real behaviour so\nreviewers can preview the full lifecycle of the live UI without editing HTML:\n\n- **Run-history dropdown** (top nav, next to the question selector). Switches\n  the Probability hero card's \"source-run\" line *and* the Job Status stepper\n  to the option's `data-job-state`. Includes one option for every lifecycle\n  state — `idle | queued | running | succeeded | partial | failed |\n  cancelled` — so you can walk every state visually in one click each.\n- **Job Status stepper** (sidebar, \"Job Status\" card). Four-step lifecycle\n  (Idle → Queued → Running → terminal); the terminal step's colour adapts to\n  the actual end state (green / amber / red / grey). The current state's\n  plain-English description is shown directly below the stepper.\n- **Graph hover tooltip** (cytoscape canvas). Hovering any node or edge\n  surfaces a quick \"what is this?\" tooltip up-and-left of the cursor; the\n  click affordance still opens the full node-info detail panel on the left.\n- **Legend / node-type filters** (graph overlay, \"Legend\" card). Each\n  node-type row in the legend is a toggle — click to hide or show that type.\n  The filter UI lives inside the legend so the swatches and the toggles are\n  in one place.\n- **Layout dropdown** (graph controls, \"Layout\" button). Lets you group by\n  node type and adjust horizontal/vertical spacing of the layered layout.\n\n## Identity + demo quota\n\nThe Analyst Workspace sidebar shows a placeholder identity card at the\nbottom-left (avatar, email, \"X of Y runs remaining\"). The values are static\ntoday; the live wiring will read the email from the\n`Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email` header (set by Cloudflare ZT) and the\nquota from the demo run-cap service. The same identity chip appears in the\ntop-bar of the Bet Pricer / Operator Lab routes (visible only on those\nscaffolding screens).\n\n## Graph layout details\n\nThe Analyst Workspace graph uses the ELK `layered` algorithm with the\n`BRANDES_KOEPF` node-placement strategy and `edgeRouting: UNDEFINED`. This\navoids the classic dagre failure mode where an intermediate-rank node sits\ndirectly on the straight line between a non-adjacent shortcut edge —\nsignificantly reducing the cases where an Indicator obscures an\nInfo → Driver shortcut. A small post-layout pass (`nudgeNodesOffEdges`)\ncatches the remaining residual overlaps by moving any node sitting on an\nedge it isn't part of perpendicular off the line. Edges themselves are\nstraight bezier lines drawn by Cytoscape — no orthogonal turns, no polyline\nbends. Filled triangle arrowheads make edge direction obvious at a glance.\n\n## Source UI References\n\n- `frontend/presentation.html` and `frontend/styles.css` for the old Analyst\n  workspace layout. The exported wireframe copy is `legacy-graph.css`, with\n  `legacy-theme.css` and `legacy-wireframe.css` providing static theme tokens\n  and wireframe-only overrides.\n- `frontend/fs12/index.html` and `frontend/fs12/fs12_styles.css` for the Bet\n  Pricer layout reference.\n- `frontend/fs10/index.html` and `frontend/fs10/fs10_styles.css` for the\n  Operator Lab layout reference.\n"
}

> AGENT

Those four `.md` files are **placeholder source documents** that the wireframe's four "Information" nodes pretend to link to. Their content is just lorem ipsum — the title (e.g. "Storage Procurement Brief") matches the Information node's label, and the file path is referenced in the graph shim via `document_path`:

```json
{
  "id": "info_storage_procurement",
  "type": "information",
  "label": "Storage procurement brief",
  "data": {
    "document_path": "ui-repository/storage-procurement-brief.md",
    "document_title": "Storage Procurement Brief"
  }
}
```

The wireframe doesn't actually open them today — it just exposes the path in the node-info card ("Source" / "Original file" fields, around `analyst-workspace.html:1361`). The intent was to give a future **document viewer** something concrete to navigate to when the live wiring lands (clicking an Information node → load the underlying research doc). For now they're four inert files that ship with the wireframe so reviewers can see the data shape end-to-end.

Cleanup options if you want to thin them out:

1. **Keep as-is** — they're tiny (~1KB each), part of the original Codex commit, and demonstrate the future doc-viewer hook.
2. **Replace with real-looking content** — swap the lorem ipsum for actual short summaries that match the node label, so reviewers see roughly what the document viewer will surface.
3. **Delete entirely** — remove the directory, drop the `document_path` / `document_title` fields from the shim, and the wireframe just shows the node title without a "source file" affordance.

Which way? (No-op is fine too.)

> AGENT

Big chunk of work — let me sketch the shape and confirm the staging approach before diving in.

**Current state**
- Old UI: `frontend/presentation.html` + `explorer_*.js` set, mounted at `/frontend/` by FastAPI (see `services/api/app.py:213-217`).
- New wireframe: just landed under `docs/wireframes/workspaces/` (static HTML, inline JSON shim, no API calls).
- Real API endpoints already exist: graphs, questions, question-sets, jobs, artifacts, runs, documents, etc.

**What "wire it up" requires, roughly in order:**
1. **Lift-and-shift**: copy the wireframe into the frontend tree at a new path (e.g. `frontend/workspaces/`), mount it via FastAPI alongside the existing `/frontend/presentation.html`. URL: `/workspaces/` for the new, old UI untouched. PR-sized: one PR.
2. **Auth identity**: read `Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email` from the request and inject it into the served HTML (the existing `frontend_index` handler already injects the API key via string replace, easy to follow the same pattern).
3. **Run-history + question selector**: fetch from `/api/questions` + `/api/runs?question_id=…`, replace the dropdown's static options.
4. **Graph rendering**: replace the inline JSON shim with `fetch('/api/graphs/{run_id}')`; the cytoscape config stays as-is (data shape matches).
5. **Job-status stepper**: read `runs.status` for the selected run; the stepper already takes a `data-job-state` attribute.
6. **Prediction hero**: read the run's headline forecast from the existing forecast/scorecard endpoints.
7. **Actions** (Run Research, Verify Claims, New Question): wire to the existing job-submit endpoints + run-detail polling.
8. **Cutover**: once everything works on `/workspaces/`, flip the default `/` redirect from `presentation.html` → `/workspaces/`. Keep `presentation.html` reachable for one more release cycle, then delete.

Before I start, a couple of scope decisions:

The wireframe\n                reads `window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL` and replaces the\n                placeholder sidebar / topbar identity text. When the header\n                isn't present (local dev without CF Access in front), the\n                placeholder copy stays — that's intentional.\n                \"\"\"\n                html = (workspaces_dir / filename).read_text()\n                user_email = (request.headers.get(\"Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email\") or \"\").strip()\n                if user_email:\n                    inject = f\"<script>window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL={json.dumps(user_email)};</script>\"\n                    html = html.replace(\"</head>\", f\"{inject}</head>\", 1)\n                return HTMLResponse(content=html)\n\n            @app.get(\"/workspaces\", include_in_schema=False)\n            def workspaces_redirect() -> RedirectResponse:\n                return RedirectResponse(url=\"/workspaces/\", status_code=307)\n\n            @app.get(\"/workspaces/\", response_class=HTMLResponse, include_in_schema=False)\n            def workspaces_index(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:\n                return _serve_workspaces_html(request, \"index.html\")\n\n            @app.get(\"/workspaces/analyst-workspace.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse, include_in_schema=False)\n            def workspaces_analyst(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:\n                return _serve_workspaces_html(request, \"analyst-workspace.html\")\n\n            app.mount(\n                \"/workspaces\",\n                StaticFiles(directory=workspaces_dir),\n                name=\"workspaces\",\n            )"

  "new_string": "    if resolved_config.frontend_dir.exists():\n\n        # Legacy UI now lives under `frontend/legacy/` (was raw at the\n        # `frontend/` root). The canonical URL going forward is\n        # `/legacy/...`; the historic `/frontend/...` mount stays as a\n        # transparent alias so existing bookmarks and absolute links in\n        # the legacy HTML keep working until the cutover to the new UI.\n        legacy_dir = resolved_config.frontend_dir / \"legacy\"\n        legacy_root = legacy_dir if legacy_dir.exists() else resolved_config.frontend_dir\n\n        def _frontend_index_html() -> HTMLResponse:\n            html = (legacy_root / \"presentation.html\").read_text()\n            if resolved_config.api_key:\n                inject = f\"<script>window.ELIJAH_API_KEY={json.dumps(resolved_config.api_key)};</script>\"\n                html = html.replace(\"</head>\", f\"{inject}</head>\", 1)\n            return HTMLResponse(content=html)\n\n        # Canonical legacy URL.\n        @app.get(\"/legacy\", include_in_schema=False)\n        def legacy_redirect() -> RedirectResponse:\n            return RedirectResponse(url=\"/legacy/presentation.html\", status_code=307)\n\n        @app.get(\"/legacy/presentation.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n        def legacy_index() -> HTMLResponse:\n            return _frontend_index_html()\n\n        # Back-compat: the historic `/frontend/presentation.html` URL keeps\n        # serving the same HTML from the new location. Will be removed in\n        # a later PR once we confirm nothing external references it.\n        @app.get(f\"{resolved_config.frontend_mount}/presentation.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n        def frontend_index() -> HTMLResponse:\n            return _frontend_index_html()\n\n        app.mount(\n            \"/legacy\",\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"legacy\",\n        )\n\n        # Mount the historic `/frontend/` prefix at the same legacy root so\n        # relative `/frontend/styles.css`, `/frontend/app.js`, etc. that\n        # the legacy HTML loads from the page keep resolving.\n        app.mount(\n            resolved_config.frontend_mount,\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"frontend\",\n        )"

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227/services/api/app.py",
  "old_string": "        app.mount(\n            \"/legacy\",\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"legacy\",\n        )\n\n        # Mount the historic `/frontend/` prefix at the same legacy root so\n        # relative `/frontend/styles.css`, `/frontend/app.js`, etc. that\n        # the legacy HTML loads from the page keep resolving.\n        app.mount(\n            resolved_config.frontend_mount,\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"frontend\",\n        )",
  "new_string": "        app.mount(\n            \"/legacy\",\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"legacy\",\n        )\n\n        # Mount the historic `/frontend/` prefix at the same legacy root so\n        # relative `/frontend/styles.css`, `/frontend/app.js`, etc. that\n        # the legacy HTML loads from the page keep resolving.\n        app.mount(\n            resolved_config.frontend_mount,\n            StaticFiles(directory=legacy_root),\n            name=\"frontend\",\n        )\n\n        # New per-workspace UIs. Each lives in its own subdirectory under\n        # `frontend/` and ships at its own top-level URL — `/analyst/`,\n        # `/bet-pricer/`, `/tuning/` — so they can be developed and\n        # deployed independently. The historic single workspace-router\n        # SPA that wrapped all three behind a hash router is gone; each\n        # workspace is now a standalone page. Mounts are guarded by\n        # `dir.exists()` so installs without a given workspace dir don't\n        # break at startup.\n        for workspace_slug in (\"analyst\", \"bet-pricer\", \"tuning\"):\n            workspace_dir = resolved_config.frontend_dir / workspace_slug\n\n            def _make_redirect(slug: str):\n                def _redirect() -> RedirectResponse:\n                    return RedirectResponse(url=f\"/{slug}/\", status_code=307)\n\n                _redirect.__name__ = f\"{slug.replace('-', '_')}_redirect\"\n                return _redirect\n\n            if workspace_dir.exists():\n                app.get(f\"/{workspace_slug}\", include_in_schema=False)(_make_redirect(workspace_slug))\n                app.mount(\n                    f\"/{workspace_slug}\",\n                    StaticFiles(directory=workspace_dir, html=True),\n                    name=f\"workspace_{workspace_slug.replace('-', '_')}\",\n                )"
}

The plain-English description of the current state is shown\n  directly below the stepper.\n- **Graph hover tooltip** — anchored up-and-left of the cursor; the\n  click affordance still opens the full node-info detail panel on the\n  left.\n- **Legend / node-type filters** — each legend row in the graph\n  overlay is a toggle; click to hide / show that node type.\n- **Layout dropdown** — group by node type, adjust spacing.\n\n## Identity placeholder\n\nThe bottom-left sidebar identity card and the topbar email chip both\nshow `analyst@elijah.example` today. Each lives in its own subdirectory under\n        # `frontend/` and ships at its own top-level URL — `/analyst/`,\n        # `/bet-pricer/`, `/tuning/` — so they can be developed and\n        # deployed independently. The historic single workspace-router\n        # SPA that wrapped all three behind a hash router is gone; each\n        # workspace is now a standalone page. Mounts are guarded by\n        # `dir.exists()` so installs without a given workspace dir don't\n        # break at startup.\n\n        def _serve_workspace_html(request: Request, file_path) -> HTMLResponse:\n            \"\"\"Serve a workspace HTML file with the Cloudflare Access user\n            identity injected as `window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL`. The wireframe\n            reads the global and replaces the placeholder sidebar / topbar\n            identity text. CF Access only forwards verified\n                # emails so this is defence in depth, not the primary\n                # control.\n                safe_email = json.dumps(user_email).replace(\"</\", \"<\\\\/\")\n                inject = f\"<script>window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL={safe_email};</script>\"\n                html = html.replace(\"</head>\", f\"{inject}</head>\", 1)\n            return HTMLResponse(content=html)\n\n        for workspace_slug in (\"analyst\", \"bet-pricer\", \"tuning\"):\n            workspace_dir = resolved_config.frontend_dir / workspace_slug\n\n            def _make_redirect(slug: str):\n                def _redirect() -> RedirectResponse:\n                    return RedirectResponse(url=f\"/{slug}/\", status_code=307)\n\n                _redirect.__name__ = f\"{slug.replace('-', '_')}_redirect\"\n                return _redirect\n\n            def _make_index(slug: str, index_path):\n                def _index(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse:\n                    return _serve_workspace_html(request, index_path)\n\n                _index.__name__ = f\"{slug.replace('-', '_')}_index\"\n                return _index\n\n            if workspace_dir.exists():\n                app.get(f\"/{workspace_slug}\", include_in_schema=False)(_make_redirect(workspace_slug))\n                # Explicit handler for the index serves HTML with the\n                # CF-Access identity injected.   "old_string": "      const runHistorySelect = document.getElementById(\"runHistorySelect\");\n      const predictionSource = document.getElementById(\"predictionSource\");\n      runHistorySelect?.addEventListener(\"change\", () => {\n        const opt = runHistorySelect.options[runHistorySelect.selectedIndex];\n        if (predictionSource && opt) {\n          predictionSource.textContent = opt.textContent;\n        }\n        const nextJobState = opt?.dataset?.jobState;\n        if (nextJobState && jobStatusStepper) {\n          jobStatusStepper.setAttribute(\"data-job-state\", nextJobState);\n          applyJobStatusStepper();\n        }\n      });",
  "new_string": "      const runHistorySelect = document.getElementById(\"runHistorySelect\");\n      const predictionSource = document.getElementById(\"predictionSource\");\n      const questionSelectEl = document.getElementById(\"questionSelect\");\n      runHistorySelect?.addEventListener(\"change\", () => {\n        const opt = runHistorySelect.options[runHistorySelect.selectedIndex];\n        if (predictionSource && opt) {\n          predictionSource.textContent = opt.textContent;\n        }\n        const nextJobState = opt?.dataset?.jobState;\n        if (nextJobState && jobStatusStepper) {\n          jobStatusStepper.setAttribute(\"data-job-state\", nextJobState);\n          applyJobStatusStepper();\n        }\n      });\n\n      // Wire the question + run-history selectors to the real API when an\n      // API key was injected by the server (see `_serve_workspace_html` in\n      // services/api/app.py). When the key isn't present (local dev with\n      // auth disabled, or the API itself is down), keep the static demo\n      // options so the wireframe still reads cleanly and the demo cycler\n      // for the job-status stepper keeps working.\n      async function wireQuestionAndRunDropdowns() {\n        const apiKey = typeof window.ELIJAH_API_KEY === \"string\" ? window.ELIJAH_API_KEY : \"\";\n        if (!apiKey || !questionSelectEl || !runHistorySelect) return;\n        const headers = { \"X-API-Key\": apiKey, \"Accept\": \"application/json\" };\n\n        async function fetchJson(url) {\n          try {\n            const resp = await fetch(url, { headers, credentials: \"same-origin\" });\n            if (!resp.ok) return null;\n            return await resp.json();\n          } catch (err) {\n            console.warn(\"[analyst] fetch failed:\", url, err);\n            return null;\n          }\n        }\n\n        const questionsPayload = await fetchJson(\"/api/questions\");\n        const questions = (questionsPayload?.questions || []).filter((q) => q && q.id);\n        if (!questions.length) return;\n\n        // Replace the static placeholder with the real question list.\n        questionSelectEl.innerHTML = \"\";\n        for (const q of questions) {\n          const opt = document.createElement(\"option\");\n          opt.value = q.id;\n          opt.textContent = q.label || q.id;\n          questionSelectEl.appendChild(opt);\n        }\n\n        // Walk the live job list and rebuild the run-history dropdown\n        // scoped to the active question. Each option carries the job's\n        // real `state` in `data-job-state`, so the existing change\n        // handler that drives the job-status stepper keeps working\n        // unchanged — it just sees real states instead of demo cycler\n        // values.\n        async function refreshRunHistory(questionId) {\n          const jobs = (await fetchJson(\"/api/jobs\")) || [];\n          const relevant = jobs\n            .filter((j) => Array.isArray(j.requested_question_ids) && j.requested_question_ids.includes(questionId))\n            .sort((a, b) => String(b.submitted_at || \"\").localeCompare(String(a.submitted_at || \"\")));\n          runHistorySelect.innerHTML = \"\";\n          if (!relevant.length) {\n            const opt = document.createElement(\"option\");\n            opt.textContent = \"No runs yet for this question\";\n            opt.dataset.jobState = \"idle\";\n            runHistorySelect.appendChild(opt);\n          } else {\n            for (const job of relevant.slice(0, 10)) {\n              const opt = document.createElement(\"option\");\n              opt.value = job.run_id || job.job_id;\n              const ts = (job.submitted_at || \"\").replace(\"T\", \" \").replace(/\\..*$/, \"\");\n              opt.textContent = `${ts} · ${job.state}`;\n              opt.dataset.jobState = String(job.state || \"succeeded\").toLowerCase();\n              runHistorySelect.appendChild(opt);\n            }\n          }\n          runHistorySelect.dispatchEvent(new Event(\"change\"));\n        }\n\n        await refreshRunHistory(questions[0].id);\n        questionSelectEl.addEventListener(\"change\", () => {\n          refreshRunHistory(questionSelectEl.value);\n        });\n      }\n\n      wireQuestionAndRunDropdowns().catch((err) => console.warn(\"[analyst] wiring failed:\", err));"
}

  "new_string": "        // Pull the current question catalog from the API, rebuild the\n        // question <select>, and return the question list so callers can\n        // decide which one to select next. Exposed via analystState so\n        // the CRUD handlers (in initNewQuestionModal) can call it after\n        // POST/PATCH/DELETE without re-doing the fetch + DOM build dance.\n        async function refreshQuestionList(selectedId) {\n          const payload = await fetchJson(\"/api/questions\");\n          const qs = (payload?.questions || []).filter((q) => q && q.id);\n          analystState.questionSets = payload?.question_sets || [];\n          questionSelectEl.innerHTML = \"\";\n          for (const q of qs) {\n            const opt = document.createElement(\"option\");\n            opt.value = q.id;\n            opt.textContent = q.label || q.id;\n            if (selectedId && q.id === selectedId) opt.selected = true;\n            questionSelectEl.appendChild(opt);\n          }\n          return qs;\n        }\n\n        const questions = await refreshQuestionList();\n        if (!questions.length) return;"
}

1	"""Per-user run-cap enforcement.
2	
3	Counts the user's "in-flight or completed" jobs and rejects a fresh submit
4	when the count is already at the user's ``max_runs`` ceiling. The counted
5	states are decided at the call site (the storage layer owns what
6	``count_counted_jobs`` returns); this module just compares the integer
7	against the user's cap.
8	
9	The rule:
10	- ``user is None`` → no enforcement (auth disabled / shared-key fallback).
11	- ``user.is_admin`` → uncapped.
12	- ``user.max_runs is None`` → uncapped (typical for admin entries; also
13	  applies to any TOML entry that omits the field).
14	- otherwise: raise ``RunCapExceeded`` if ``current_count >= user.max_runs``.
15	
16	The parallel-submit race is accepted; see the auth plan (decision #15).
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	from dataclasses import dataclass
22	
23	from .registry import User
24	
25	
26	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
27	class RunCapExceeded(Exception):
28	    """Raised when a submit would exceed the user's ``max_runs`` cap.
29	
30	    Carries enough structured detail for the API layer to translate into a
31	    structured error response (HTTP 429, ``run_cap_exceeded``)."""
32	
33	    user_id: str
34	    used: int
35	    max_runs: int
36	
37	    def __str__(self) -> str:
38	        return f"User {self.user_id!r} has used {self.used} of {self.max_runs} demo runs."
39	
40	
41	def check_run_cap(user: User | None, current_count: int) -> None:
42	    """Raise ``RunCapExceeded`` if submitting one more job would exceed
43	    the user's ``max_runs`` cap. Callers must pass the count of "counted"
44	    jobs (queued + running + succeeded) for this user."""
45	    if user is None:
46	        return
47	    if user.is_admin:
48	        return
49	    if user.max_runs is None:
50	        return
51	    if current_count >= user.max_runs:
52	        raise RunCapExceeded(
53	            user_id=user.user_id,
54	            used=int(current_count),
55	            max_runs=int(user.max_runs),
56	        )
57	
58	
59	__all__ = [
60	    "RunCapExceeded",
61	    "check_run_cap",
62	]
63

1	"""Current-user surface for the GUI.
2	
3	Exposes ``GET /api/users/me`` so the frontend can render "who am I"
4	(identity, admin flag) and "how many runs do I have left" (used vs.
5	max_runs) without scraping other endpoints.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
11	
12	from packages.auth import User, get_current_user
13	from packages.contracts import CurrentUserResponse
14	
15	from ..dependencies import get_job_service
16	from ..job_service import JobService
17	
18	router = APIRouter()
19	
20	
21	_ANONYMOUS_USER_ID = "anonymous"
22	
23	
24	@router.get("/users/me", response_model=CurrentUserResponse)
25	def get_me(
26	    job_service: JobService = Depends(get_job_service),
27	    current_user: User | None = Depends(get_current_user),
28	) -> CurrentUserResponse:
29	    """Identity and run-cap usage for the calling user.
30	
31	    When auth is disabled (dev mode, empty registry, no CF header) the
32	    response shape stays the same with ``user_id = "anonymous"`` and zero
33	    usage so the frontend doesn't have to special-case missing identity."""
34	    if current_user is None:
35	        return CurrentUserResponse(user_id=_ANONYMOUS_USER_ID)
36	    used = job_service.job_queue.count_counted_jobs(submitted_by=current_user.user_id)
37	    return CurrentUserResponse(
38	        user_id=current_user.user_id,
39	        email=current_user.email,
40	        is_admin=current_user.is_admin,
41	        max_runs=current_user.max_runs,
42	        used=used,
43	    )
44	
45	
46	__all__ = ["router"]
47

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227/frontend/bet-pricer/index.html",
  "old_string": "  <script>\n    // If the API injected window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL (from the\n    // Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email request header), use it to replace\n    // the placeholder identity chip in the topbar. Without the global,\n    // the static placeholder stays for local dev.\n    (function () {\n      const userEmail = typeof window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL === \"string\" ? window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL.trim() : \"\";\n      if (!userEmail) return;\n      const topbarEmail = document.getElementById(\"identityEmail\");\n      if (topbarEmail) topbarEmail.textContent = userEmail;\n    })();\n  </script>",
  "new_string": "  <script>\n    // Identity + quota chip wiring.\n    //\n    // The brand-identity row above the Bet Pricer heading shows the\n    // signed-in user's email and a lifetime run-cap quota chip (\"X of Y\n    // runs\"). The email comes from window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL (server-side\n    // injection from the Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email request\n    // header, see services/api/app.py `_serve_workspace_html`). The\n    // quota comes from /api/users/me, which the API exposes as\n    // `{user_id, email, is_admin, max_runs, used}` — `used` counts the\n    // calling user's queued + running + succeeded jobs. When auth is\n    // disabled (no API key, no CF header), both fall back to the static\n    // wireframe placeholders so the page still reads cleanly.\n    (function () {\n      const emailEl = document.getElementById(\"identityEmail\");\n      const quotaEl = document.getElementById(\"identityQuota\");\n\n      const userEmail = typeof window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL === \"string\" ? window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL.trim() : \"\";\n      if (userEmail && emailEl) emailEl.textContent = userEmail;\n\n      const apiKey = typeof window.ELIJAH_API_KEY === \"string\" ? window.ELIJAH_API_KEY : \"\";\n      if (!apiKey || !quotaEl) return;\n\n      async function refreshQuota() {\n        try {\n          const resp = await fetch(\"/api/users/me\", {\n            credentials: \"same-origin\",\n            headers: { \"X-API-Key\": apiKey, \"Accept\": \"application/json\" },\n          });\n          if (!resp.ok) return;\n          const me = await resp.json();\n          if (me.email && emailEl) emailEl.textContent = me.email;\n          if (typeof me.max_runs === \"number\" && typeof me.used === \"number\") {\n            const remaining = Math.max(0, me.max_runs - me.used);\n            quotaEl.textContent = `${remaining} of ${me.max_runs} runs left`;\n            quotaEl.title = `${me.used} used of ${me.max_runs} total demo runs (lifetime)`;\n          } else if (me.is_admin) {\n            quotaEl.textContent = \"unlimited runs\";\n            quotaEl.title = \"Admin user — no run cap\";\n          }\n        } catch (err) {\n          console.warn(\"[bet-pricer] /api/users/me fetch failed:\", err);\n        }\n      }\n\n      refreshQuota();\n    })();\n  </script>"
}

> AGENT

Yep — all the wiring is in the served file (23 hits across CRUD + research + verify + URLs) AND the demo cycler is still there (8 `data-job-state` options in the run-history dropdown). Two separate things:

### 1. Real wiring (PRs #302, #304, #305)

The HTML contains the JS to:
- Fetch real questions from `/api/questions` and populate the question selector
- Fetch real jobs from `/api/jobs` and populate the run-history dropdown
- POST `/api/jobs/research` when "Run Research" is clicked, poll, update the stepper
- POST `/api/jobs/{id}/cancel`, POST `/api/iw-trigger/...` for Cancel / Verify Claims
- POST/PATCH/DELETE `/api/questions` for the New / Edit / Delete Question buttons

But all of this is gated on `window.ELIJAH_API_KEY` being set. The plain `python3 -m http.server` you're running doesn't inject it (only the FastAPI `_serve_workspace_html` handler does). So with the static server, every wiring function short-circuits and falls back to wireframe-only behaviour.

### 2. Wireframe demo behaviour (what you ARE seeing)

- **Run-history dropdown**: 7 static options each carrying a `data-job-state` — Latest run / Previous / A week ago / Right now / In the queue / Old / New question. Pick any of them → the Job Status stepper flips through `succeeded / partial / failed / running / queued / cancelled / idle` accordingly. That's the "examples of the new research job" demo cycler.
- **New Question modal**: "Generate Values" still uses local heuristics; "Approve Question" prints "approved in this demo" message and updates the title — same as the original wireframe.
- **Run Research** / **Cancel** / **Verify Claims** / **Delete Question**: clicking them right now does a `fetch()` against `/api/jobs/research` etc., which 404s on the static server → buttons re-enable, nothing visible happens. No wireframe-only fallback for those (they only mean something against a real backend).

### To see the real wiring in action

Either:
- Point your browser at the live staging URL (the FastAPI app there serves these files with `window.ELIJAH_API_KEY` injected → all wiring activates), or
- Run the FastAPI app locally (`uv run uvicorn services.api.app:create_app --factory --reload`) and hit `http://localhost:8000/analyst/` — same injection, same wiring.

Want me to spin up the local FastAPI so you can poke at the real flow?

{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && gh pr create --base dev --head sumeet/workspaces-quota-and-identity-layout --draft --title \"FS-Workspaces: Wire analyst workspace to real backend APIs\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What this is\n\nThis PR rolls up six previously-stacked PRs (#301-#306) into a single change so the entire wired-up analyst workspace lands on \\`dev\\` as one reviewable unit. The earlier stack-merges fired into chain-parent branches rather than into \\`dev\\`, so the work is consolidated here. PR #300 (the workspace reorg) already landed; this PR brings everything from the next slice up through quota + identity wiring.\n\nThe analyst workspace at \\`/analyst/\\` is now fully wired to the real backend instead of running on the wireframe's static demo data. A signed-in analyst lands on the page and sees their actual question library, run history, prediction graphs, prediction forecasts, and lifetime demo-run quota. They can submit research, cancel running jobs, verify claims, and create/edit/delete questions — all gated on the API key the server injects from config, with graceful degradation to the wireframe demo behaviour when the page is served without auth (e.g. during local development against a no-auth API).\n\nUser-visible outcome: \\`/analyst/\\` becomes a working production UI alongside the legacy \\`/frontend/presentation.html\\`. The cutover (flipping \\`/\\` from legacy → \\`/analyst/\\`) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up PR so the new UI can be exercised on staging at its dedicated URL before the legacy mount is retired. \\`/bet-pricer/\\` and \\`/tuning/\\` ship the identity + quota chip in this PR; their workspace-specific wiring lands in later slices.\n\n## Technical detail\n\n### Summary\n\nSix logical slices, one rollup PR:\n\n1. **Identity injection** — \\`Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email\\` header read by FastAPI and injected into served HTML as \\`window.ELIJAH_USER_EMAIL\\`; the \\`X-API-Key\\` from config injected as \\`window.ELIJAH_API_KEY\\`. JSON-encoded + \\`</\\` escaped to be XSS-safe.\n2. **Question + run-history dropdowns** wired to \\`GET /api/questions\\` and \\`GET /api/jobs\\`.\n3. **Graph render** driven by \\`GET /api/questions/{id}/graph\\` (replaces the wireframe's inline JSON shim).\n4. **Prediction hero card** driven by the graph response's \\`summary\\` block.\n5. **Run / Cancel / Verify Claims buttons** wired to \\`POST /api/jobs/research\\`, \\`POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel\\`, \\`POST /api/iw-trigger/questions/{id}\\` with poll-until-terminal job tracking.\n6. **New / Edit / Delete Question CRUD** wired to \\`POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/questions\\` (with modals; the \\`numeric_bracket\\`/\\`binary\\`/\\`categorical\\` enum + UI label mapping).\n7. **Run-cap quota chip** wired to \\`GET /api/users/me\\` returning \\`{max_runs, used}\\`; chip refreshes on submit (both 2xx and 429 \\`run_cap_exceeded\\`) and on poll-terminal events. Identity (\\`email + runs left\\`) moved into the analyst nav under the Elijah brand title; sidebar identity card removed.\n\n### Approach\n\n* Frontend: extend the existing wireframe IIFE with a closure-scoped \\`analystState\\` bridge object holding API key, headers, question-set cache, and refresh closures. 1	"""
2	Deterministic seed data for frontend API regression tests.
3	
4	This fixture is richer than `seed_repo_state`: it covers every node type
5	(question/target/driver/indicator/evidence), both edge types (REFERENCE +
6	CONDITIONAL), visibility filtering, cross-question edges, parent/sub-question
7	hierarchy, and every optional field on NodeRecord/EdgeRecord that the
8	frontend may render.
9	
10	The goal is: capture the current API output from `main` into a golden
11	JSON file, then guarantee that future refactors (Phase 3 repository
12	rewrite, Phase 4 short IDs, etc.) don't change the frontend-visible
13	response shape.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import json
19	from pathlib import Path
20	
21	from packages.storage import (
22	    EdgeRecord,
23	    GraphIndex,
24	    NodeRecord,
25	    QuestionRecord,
26	    QuestionSetRecord,
27	    StorageRuntimeConfig,
28	    build_database_worker_storage_adapters,
29	)
30	from services.api.config import ApiConfig
31	
32	REGRESSION_API_KEY=[REDACTED]"
33	
34	
35	def seed_regression_fixture(tmp_path: Path, *, frontend_dir: Path | None = None) -> ApiConfig:
36	    """Seed a rich, deterministic workspace that exercises every API response field."""
37	    graphs_dir = tmp_path / "graphs"
38	    graphs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
39	    resolved_frontend_dir = frontend_dir or (tmp_path / "frontend")
40	    resolved_frontend_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
41	    output_root = tmp_path / "runtime" / "runs"
42	
43	    storage_runtime = StorageRuntimeConfig(
44	        database_url=f"sqlite+pysqlite:///{(tmp_path / 'regression.db').as_posix()}",
45	        local_workspace_root=tmp_path / "workspace",
46	        project_root=tmp_path,
47	    )
48	    adapters = build_database_worker_storage_adapters(storage_runtime)
49	    repo = adapters.graph_store_repository
50	
51	    question_sets = _build_question_sets()
52	    questions = _build_questions()
53	    nodes = _build_nodes()
54	    edges = _build_edges()
55	    graph = GraphIndex(
56	        graph_id="gjopen_2026",
57	        title="Regression Test Graph",
58	        node_ids=sorted(node.node_id for node in nodes),
59	        edge_ids=sorted(edge.edge_id for edge in edges),
60	    )
61	
62	    repo.save_graph_store_bundle(
63	        graphs_path=graphs_dir / "graphs.json",
64	        nodes_path=graphs_dir / "nodes.json",
65	        edges_path=graphs_dir / "edges.json",
66	        questions_path=graphs_dir / "questions.json",
67	        graphs=[graph],
68	        nodes=nodes,
69	        edges=edges,
70	        questions=questions,
71	        question_sets=question_sets,
72	    )
73	
74	    summary_payload = _build_summary_payload()
75	    (graphs_dir / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary_payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
76	
77	    (resolved_frontend_dir / "presentation.html").write_text(
78	        "<!doctype html><title>Elijah regression frontend</title>",
79	        encoding="utf-8",
80	    )
81	
82	    upsert_summary_entry = getattr(repo, "upsert_summary_entry", None)
83	    summaries = summary_payload.get("summaries")
84	    if callable(upsert_summary_entry) and isinstance(summaries, dict):
85	        for question_id, entry in summaries.items():
86	            if isinstance(entry, dict):
87	                upsert_summary_entry(question_id=str(question_id), summary_entry=entry)
88	
89	    return ApiConfig(
90	        project_root=tmp_path,
91	        frontend_dir=resolved_frontend_dir,
92	        graphs_dir=graphs_dir,
93	        questions_path=graphs_dir / "questions.json",
94	        summary_path=graphs_dir / "summary.json",
95	        output_root=output_root,
96	        default_graph_id="gjopen_2026",
97	        api_key=[REDACTED],
98	        storage_runtime=storage_runtime,
99	    )

{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && python3 << 'PY'\nimport json, collections\nnodes = json.load(open('/tmp/realgraphs/nodes.json'))['nodes']\nedges = json.load(open('/tmp/realgraphs/edges.json'))['edges']\nquestions = json.load(open('/tmp/realgraphs/questions.json'))['questions']\n\n# Group nodes by question_id (from data.question_id) - real key is 'id'\nby_q = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {'nodes': [], 'edges': []})\nfor n in nodes:\n    qid = (n.get('data') or {}).get('question_id')\n    if qid:\n        by_q[qid]['nodes'].append(n)\nnodeids_per_q = {q: {n['id'] for n in d['nodes']} for q, d in by_q.items()}\n# Edges: bucket edges to a question if either endpoint is in that question's nodes\nfor e in edges:\n    for qid, nids in nodeids_per_q.items():\n        if e['from_id'] in nids or e['to_id'] in nids:\n            by_q[qid]['edges'].append(e)\n            break  # ignore cross-question — pick first match\n\nprint(f\"{'qid':<70} | {'type':<22} | nodes | edges | label\")\nprint('-'*180)\nranked = []\nfor q in questions:\n    qid = q.get('id')\n    qtype = q.get('classification') or '?'\n    label = (q.get('label') or '')[:70]\n    nc = len(by_q[qid]['nodes'])\n    ec = len(by_q[qid]['edges'])\n    type_counts = collections.Counter(n['type'] for n in by_q[qid]['nodes'])\n    print(f\"{qid[:70]:<70} | {qtype:<22} | {nc:>5} | {ec:>5} | {label}\")\n    print(f\"{'':>70} | {'':<22} | {'':>5} | {'':>5} | types={dict(type_counts)}\")\n    ranked.append((nc + ec, qid, label, dict(type_counts)))\nprint()\nprint('TOP 3 by richness (nodes+edges):')\nfor score, qid, label, types in sorted(ranked, reverse=True)[:3]:\n    print(f\"  score={score}  {label}  types={types}\")\nPY",
  "description": "Rank questions by graph richness"
}

as the single demo question on staging.\nWipes the prior regression seeds (reg_q_*) first.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom packages.storage import (\n    EdgeRecord,\n    GraphIndex,\n    NodeRecord,\n    QuestionRecord,\n    QuestionSetRecord,\n    StorageRuntimeConfig,\n    build_database_worker_storage_adapters,\n)\nfrom sqlalchemy import create_engine, text\n\n# --- Load fixture ----------------------------------------------------\nsrc = json.loads(Path(\"/tmp/uk_cpi_subset.json\").read_text())\nquestion_id = src[\"question_id\"]\nquestion_label = src[\"label\"]\nraw_nodes = src[\"nodes\"]\nraw_edges = src[\"edges\"]\n\nprint(f\"Loaded subset: {len(raw_nodes)} nodes, {len(raw_edges)} edges\")\n\n# --- Wipe prior regression seeds + their graph -----------------------\ndb_url = os.environ[\"DATABASE_URL\"]\nengine = create_engine(db_url)\nwith engine.begin() as conn:\n    deleted = conn.execute(\n        text(\"DELETE FROM questions WHERE question_id LIKE 'reg_q_%' RETURNING question_id\"),\n    ).fetchall()\n    print(f\"Deleted {len(deleted)} prior reg_q_* rows\")\n    # Also wipe any prior graphs/nodes/edges/summaries that referenced them\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM nodes WHERE node_id LIKE 'reg_q_%'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM reference_edges WHERE edge_id LIKE 'reg_%'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM conditional_edges WHERE edge_id LIKE 'reg_%'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM graph_summaries WHERE graph_id = 'gjopen_2026'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM graphs WHERE graph_id = 'gjopen_2026'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM question_sets WHERE question_set_id = 'regression_set'\"))\n    conn.execute(text(\"DELETE FROM questions WHERE question_id = :qid\"), {\"qid\": question_id})\n\n# --- Build records ---------------------------------------------------\n# Map legacy 'evidence' node type → current 'information' enum\nTYPE_MAP = {\n    \"evidence\": \"information\",\n    \"question\": \"driver\",  # 'question' node type is legacy; current schema renders the question root as a driver\n}\n\n\ndef map_type(t: str) -> str:\n    return TYPE_MAP.get(t, t)\n\n\nquestion_set = QuestionSetRecord(\n    id=\"demo_set\",\n    label=\"Demo Questions\",\n    description=\"Curated demo questions seeded for the staging analyst workspace.\",\n)\n\nquestion = QuestionRecord(\n    question_id=question_id,\n    url=f\"local://demo/{question_id}\",\n    label=question_label,\n    toi=\"2026-12-31T00:00:00Z\",\n    target_date=\"2026-12-31T00:00:00Z\",\n    options=[\"Yes\", \"No\"],\n    question_set=\"demo_set\",\n    question_set_label=\"Demo Questions\",\n    classification=\"categorical_outcome\",\n    data_mode=\"categorical_events\",\n    target_date_text=\"2026-12-31\",\n    closing_date_text=\"2026-12-31\",\n    data={\n        \"question_id\": question_id,\n        \"question_set\": \"demo_set\",\n        \"question_set_label\": \"Demo Questions\",\n        \"domain\": \"macroeconomics\",\n        \"region\": \"united_kingdom\",\n        \"keywords\": [\"uk\", \"cpi\", \"inflation\", \"macro\"],\n        \"hierarchy_role\": \"standalone\",\n    },\n)\n\nnodes: list[NodeRecord] = []\nfor n in raw_nodes:\n    mapped_type = map_type(n[\"type\"])\n    nodes.append(\n        NodeRecord(\n            node_id=n[\"id\"],\n            type=mapped_type,\n            label=n[\"label\"],\n            toi=n.get(\"toi\"),\n            baseline_p=n.get(\"baseline_p\"),\n            posterior_p=n.get(\"posterior_p\"),\n            instrument=n.get(\"instrument\"),\n            split_from_driver_id=n.get(\"split_from_driver_id\"),\n            data=n.get(\"data\") or {\"question_id\": question_id},\n        )\n    )\n\nedges: list[EdgeRecord] = []\nfor e in raw_edges:\n    edges.append(\n        EdgeRecord(\n            edge_id=e[\"id\"],\n            from_node=e[\"from_id\"],\n            to_node=e[\"to_id\"],\n            toi=e.get(\"toi\"),\n            weight=e.get(\"weight\", 1.0),\n            type=e[\"type\"],\n            data=e.get(\"data\") or {\"question_id\": question_id},\n        )\n    )\n\ngraph = GraphIndex(\n    graph_id=\"demo_uk_cpi\",\n    title=\"UK CPI > 3% — Dec 2026 (demo)\",\n    node_ids=sorted(n.node_id for n in nodes),\n    edge_ids=sorted(e.edge_id for e in edges),\n)\n\n# --- Write to DB -----------------------------------------------------\nstorage_runtime = StorageRuntimeConfig(\n    database_url=db_url,\n    local_workspace_root=Path(\"/tmp/seed_workspace\"),\n    project_root=Path(\"/tmp/seed_workspace\"),\n)\nPath(\"/tmp/seed_workspace\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nPath(\"/tmp/seed_graphs\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nadapters = build_database_worker_storage_adapters(storage_runtime)\nrepo = adapters.graph_store_repository\n\nrepo.save_graph_store_bundle(\n    graphs_path=Path(\"/tmp/seed_graphs/graphs.json\"),\n    nodes_path=Path(\"/tmp/seed_graphs/nodes.json\"),\n    edges_path=Path(\"/tmp/seed_graphs/edges.json\"),\n    questions_path=Path(\"/tmp/seed_graphs/questions.json\"),\n    graphs=[graph],\n    nodes=nodes,\n    edges=edges,\n    questions=[question],\n    question_sets=[question_set],\n)\n\nprint(f\"DONE — seeded 1 set, 1 question, {len(nodes)} nodes, {len(edges)} edges\")\n"
}

- **Persistent** (small repo PR): add a `./config:/app/config:ro` mount in `compose.staging.yml` + put the real toml on the Betty filesystem at `/home/elijah/staging/config/`. Persists across deploys.

21	    user_id  = "alice"
22	    email    = "alice@example.com"
23	    api_key  = "..."
24	    max_runs = 5              # explicit per-user cap
25	
26	Backward-compat: when no ``config/api_users.toml`` is present, the registry
27	falls back to ``ELIJAH_API_KEY`` (single anonymous user, no email). Existing
28	single-key deployments keep working unchanged.
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import logging
34	import os
35	import secrets
36	import tomllib
37	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
38	from pathlib import Path
39	from typing import Any
40	
41	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
42	
43	_DEFAULT_USERS_PATH = Path("config/api_users.toml")
44	_USERS_PATH_ENV = "ELIJAH_API_USERS_PATH"
45	
46	
47	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
48	class User:
49	    user_id: str
50	    name: str
51	    role: str = "operator"
52	    email: str | None = None
53	    is_admin: bool = False
54	    max_runs: int | None = None
55	    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
59	class RegistryDefaults:
60	    """Values used to auto-provision unknown CF-authenticated emails."""
61	
62	    max_runs: int | None = None
63	
64	
65	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
66	class UserRegistry:
67	    by_api_key: dict[str, User] = field(default_factory=dict)
68	    by_email: dict[str, User] = field(default_factory=dict)
69	    defaults: RegistryDefaults = field(default_factory=RegistryDefaults)
70	    fallback_mode: bool = False
71	
72	    @property
73	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
74	        return not self.by_api_key and not self.by_email
75	
76	    @property
77	    def n_users(self) -> int:
78	        return len({user.user_id for user in self.by_api_key.values()} | {user.user_id for user in self.by_email.values()})
79	
80	    def lookup(self, api_key: str) -> User | None:
81	        if not api_key:
82	            return None
83	        for stored_key, user in self.by_api_key.items():
84	            try:
85	                if secrets.compare_digest(stored_key, api_key):
86	                    return user
87	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
88	                continue
89	        return None
90	
91	    def lookup_by_email(self, email: str) -> User | None:
92	        if not email:
93	            return None
94	        return self.by_email.get(email.strip().lower())
95	
96	    def provision_for_email(self, email: str) -> User:
97	        """Synthesize a non-admin ``User`` for a CF-authenticated email not in
98	        the registry. Uses ``defaults.max_runs`` as the run cap."""
99	        normalized = email.strip().lower()
100	        return User(
101	            user_id=normalized,
102	            name=normalized,
103	            email=normalized,
104	            is_admin=False,
105	            max_runs=self.defaults.max_runs,
106	        )
107	
108	
109	def load_user_registry(
110	    *,
111	    users_path: Path | None = None,
112	    fallback_api_key: str | None = None,
113	    fallback_user_id: str = "shared",
114	    fallback_user_name: str = "shared",
115	) -> UserRegistry:
116	    candidate_path: Path | None = users_path
117	    if candidate_path is None:
118	        env_path = os.environ.get(_USERS_PATH_ENV, "").strip()
119	        if env_path:
120	            candidate_path = Path(env_path)
```

```json
{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && gh pr create --base dev --head sumeet/compose-mount-api-users-toml --draft --title \"Cross-FS: Mount api_users.toml from host into staging + prod compose\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What this is\n\nToday the api_users.toml (the per-user run-cap + admin list that the API service loads at startup) only exists inside the container image. There is no bind mount, so any file written to \\`/app/config/api_users.toml\\` on staging is wiped on the next \\`dev\\` push (because \\`docker compose up -d\\` pulls a fresh image and recreates the container). The same gap exists on prod — there's no place for an operator to drop the toml that survives a redeploy.\n\nThis PR adds a small bind mount to the API service in both \\`compose.staging.yml\\` and \\`compose.prod.yml\\`. The mount source is \\`./elijah-config/\\` next to the compose file on the deploy host, and it lands inside the container at \\`/etc/elijah/\\`. The API container's \\`ELIJAH_API_USERS_PATH\\` env var is set to \\`/etc/elijah/api_users.toml\\` so the loader reads from the mounted file.\n\nUser-visible outcome: operators can now manage \\`api_users.toml\\` on Betty (or any future deploy host) and have it survive redeploys. Drop the file at \\`/home/elijah/staging/elijah-config/api_users.toml\\` or \\`/home/elijah/prod/elijah-config/api_users.toml\\` and restart the api service.\n\n## Technical detail\n\n### Summary\n\nTwo-file diff. Each compose file's \\`api:\\` service gets:\n\n- \\`ELIJAH_API_USERS_PATH=/etc/elijah/api_users.toml\\` env var\n- \\`volumes: - ./elijah-config:/etc/elijah:ro\\` read-only bind mount\n\nNothing else changes — workers, db, litellm, healthchecks all untouched.\n\n### Approach\n\nThe user registry loader (\\`packages/auth/registry.py\\`) already supports an \\`ELIJAH_API_USERS_PATH\\` env override. When the file at that path is missing, the loader falls back to the single shared \\`ELIJAH_API_KEY\\` mode (\\`fallback_mode=true\\`), which is the current behaviour on both environments. So this PR is safe to merge before the prod toml exists on disk: prod stays in single-key mode until an operator puts a file at \\`/home/elijah/prod/elijah-config/api_users.toml\\`.\n\nBind-mount target is \\`/etc/elijah/\\` (a fresh path) rather than \\`/app/config/\\` so we don't risk clobbering the in-image config files (\\`llm_tasks.toml\\`, \\`run_profile.toml\\`, etc.) with a directory mount.\n\n### Tests\n\nNo code-path change. \\`compose.staging.yml\\` and \\`compose.prod.yml\\` are validated by the existing CI yaml lint. Loader behaviour (missing-file fallback) is already covered in \\`packages/auth\\` tests.\n\n### Verification\n\n- [x] \\`uv run python -c \\\"import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('compose.staging.yml')); yaml.safe_load(open('compose.prod.yml'))\\\"\\` — both parse\n- [x] Staging operator state already prepared on Betty at \\`/home/elijah/staging/elijah-config/api_users.toml\\` so the first post-merge deploy mounts cleanly\n- [x] Prod path \\`/home/elijah/prod/elijah-config/\\` will be auto-created by docker as an empty dir on first deploy; loader falls back to \\`ELIJAH_API_KEY\\` until a real toml is placed there\n\n### Risks\n\n- If \\`docker compose up -d\\` auto-creates the host directory before the file exists, the loader sees no file and falls back to \\`ELIJAH_API_KEY\\` mode — same as today. No regression.\n- The \\`:ro\\` flag prevents the api container from accidentally writing into the host config dir.\n- Worker container is intentionally not mounted; it doesn't authenticate users.\n\n### Branch-merge\n\nIndependent infra change. No dependency on the in-flight analyst PRs (#308 hide-hero, #309 demo-sentinel, #310 placeholder flash).\n\n### Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- The actual prod \\`api_users.toml\\` is not added in this PR — that's an operator-managed file, kept off-repo (the existing \\`config/api_users.toml\\` is gitignored; only \\`api_users.example.toml\\` ships in the repo).\n- No env-var-based user list support added; the only path remains the toml on disk.\n\n@kungfusaini\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open the compose mount PR"
}

> AGENT

Root cause located:

- `services/api/worker_dispatch.py:88` passes `model_set=`, `run_config_id=`, `run_config_snapshot=` to `run_research_driver_over_questions`
- `services/worker/research_driver_pipeline.py:95` (and the batch pipeline at `research_driver_batch_pipeline.py:417`) doesn't accept any of those three kwargs in its signature
- Came in with **SPI-236** (commit `cfdec24`, "Port API auth, run-config propagation, and worker context") — the dispatcher learned the new kwargs but the pipeline signatures never got updated to receive them

This is a regression that breaks every research submission, not just yours — `submitted_by='demo'` succeeded only because that demo job was hand-inserted as already-succeeded (it never went through the worker).

Two ways to fix:

**A. Quick — drop the kwargs from the dispatcher.** The pipeline already runs inside `model_set_context(model_set)`, so `model_set` propagates via context. `run_config_id`/`run_config_snapshot` are similarly read from context downstream. ~2-line diff, low risk.

**B. Proper — add the three kwargs to both pipeline entry points and thread them down explicitly.** Matches the dispatcher's intent (explicit args > implicit context). Bigger PR, more test work.

Want me to push A as a hotfix PR now (gets you unblocked) and file B as follow-up?

def run_research_driver_single_step_job(
    *,
    questions_path: Path,
    graphs_dir: Path,
    output_root: Path,
    run_id: str,
    graph_id: str,
    question_ids: list[str],
    request_context: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    storage_adapters: WorkerStorageAdapters | None = None,
    graph_store_paths: GraphStorePaths | None = None,
    progress_callback: Callable[..., None] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    resolved_storage = resolve_worker_storage_adapters(storage_adapters)
