> AGENT

Concise answer:

**What the GUI actually sends** — looked at `submitResearchJob()` in `analyst/index.html` and the API contract `ResearchJobSubmitRequest`:

```json
{ "question_ids": ["user_q_will_uk_cpi..."] }
```

That's it. No `run_config_id`, no `model_set`. The contract has `extra="forbid"` so the GUI can't even send those fields.

**What the dispatcher computes for a GUI submission:**

```
run_config_id        = None   (GUI didn't send one)
run_config_snapshot  = {}     (nothing to load)
model_set            = None   (snapshot empty, no llm_profile)
```

All three are None at the moment of the failing pipeline call. The pipeline raises `TypeError` purely because Python rejects unknown kwargs — even when their value is None.

**Why were they added?** SPI-236 ("Port API auth, run-config propagation, and worker context") was a multi-tenant infrastructure port: per-user pinned LLM profiles, run-config audit snapshots, hash-of-knobs-that-actually-ran for reproducibility. The dispatcher learned to:
- Look up `run_config_id` → load the config from DB → build a snapshot → derive `model_set`
- Pass that whole resolved trio downward

But **the receiving end (`run_research_driver_over_questions`) never grew matching parameters**. The work landed half-finished. The CLI also calls this function and never passes those kwargs, which is why it works in development.

**Is the GUI plug-and-play?** Yes for the user-visible flow — nothing extra needed. The breakage is internal API wiring, not GUI-side.

**Fix shape:** drop the three kwargs from the dispatcher's pipeline call. `model_set` already propagates via `with model_set_context(model_set):` (line 77, in place). `run_config_id`/`run_config_snapshot` already live inside `resolved_context`, which downstream code already pulls from. Net: ~3 lines, no behavior loss for GUI users, no impact on CLI users (they didn't pass these to the pipeline anyway).

> AGENT

**No functionality change.** Confirmed by tracing all three values end-to-end:

**`model_set`**
- Batch pipeline body has zero references to `model_set` as a parameter
- It only reads `model_set` via thread-local context — and the dispatcher already wraps the call in `with model_set_context(model_set):` (line 77)
- CLI works today by doing the exact same thing: thread-local context, no kwarg

**`run_config_id` / `run_config_snapshot`**
- Neither pipeline reads these from anywhere
- The single-step branch already passes `request_context=resolved_context`, and `resolved_context` already contains both values (lines 31–42 of the dispatcher injected them)
- The batch pipeline doesn't even have a `request_context` parameter — it never received them on the CLI path either

**The CLI proves this is safe**: `tools/cli/commands.py:244` calls `run_research_driver_over_questions` with the exact same tuning kwargs the dispatcher uses, wrapped in `model_set_context`, and **does not pass any of the three kwargs**. The CLI has been the working reference all along.

So the hotfix is: drop the three kwargs from the dispatcher's two `return` calls (lines 70–72 and 88–90). The dispatcher's preceding work — thread-local context, `ensure_research_driver_llm_ready`, snapshot injection into `resolved_context`, hash computation — all stays. No downstream code is affected because no downstream code ever read those kwargs.

Net behavior delta for GUI users: ❌ crashing → ✅ working. Net behavior delta for CLI users: zero (they never hit the dispatcher). Net behavior delta for `request_context` consumers: zero (resolved_context is unchanged).

PR #184: SPI-236: Port API auth, run-config propagation, and worker context
+1038/-54 across 9 files

## What this is

Ports Lane 4 of the SPI-238 porting epic. The API on `dev` currently has bare-bones job submission and a single shared API key. This PR adds three capabilities from dev_sprint:

Multi-user authentication via a TOML-based user registry, replacing the single `ELIJAH_API_KEY` model while preserving backward compatibility. End-to-end run-config propagation so the run configuration (model set, behavior flags) flows from API request through the job queue row into worker dispatch and pipeline execution. Worker context helpers so workers can resolve which config and model set to use for a given job.

FS12 route registration was intentionally deferred — the route file imports `packages.domain.fs12` which does not exist on `dev`. Tracked as SPI-239 under a separate "Port FS12 Pricing Diagnostics to dev" epic, with SPI-240 documenting the skip in SPI-238.

## Technical detail

### Summary

9 files changed: 3 new modules (`services/api/auth.py`, `services/worker/run_config_context.py`, `tests/test_api_auth.py`), 6 modified (`core/run_config.py`, `services/api/app.py`, `services/api/job_service.py`, `services/api/worker_dispatch.py`, `services/api/routes/jobs.py`, `services/api/mappers.py`).

### Approach

- **Auth**: New `auth.py` with `User`, `UserRegistry`, TOML loader, and `get_current_user` FastAPI dependency. Routes still use the existing `require_api_key`; the new registry is loaded onto `app.state` for sub-PR 2+ to wire per-user rate limits.
- **Run-config propagation**: `job_service._resolve_run_config_for_submission()` creates or loads a DB-backed run config, threading `run_config_id`/`run_config_hash`/`model_set` into `JobRequestContext`. `worker_dispatch` loads the snapshot from DB and wraps pipeline calls in `model_set_context`.
- **core/run_config.py gap**: 3 DB-backed functions (`create_run_research_run_config`, `load_run_research_run_config`, `build_run_config_execution_snapshot`) plus `RUN_RESEARCH_BEHAVIOR_KEYS` were ported as a dependency gap between SPI-225 and this ticket.
- **mappers.py**: Only the `worker_payload_to_job_result` run_config/llm_config field additions. FS1 `target_set_integrity` changes were excluded (not SPI-236 scope).

### Tests

- `tests/test_api_auth.py` — 24 tests covering UserRegistry primitives, TOML loading/validation, fallback, `get_current_user` dependency, and app factory wiring.
- `tests/test_job_queue_artifacts.py` — existing regression (identical on both branches, 8 tests).
- `tests/test_run_detail_api.py` — existing regression (identical on both branches, 6 tests).
- `tests/test_api_service.py` — existing integration tests (30 tests).

### Verification

- [x] `uv run ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uv run python -m pytest --ignore=tests/frontend -x -q` (988 passed, 1 pre-existing flaky timing test)
- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_api_auth.py -q` (24 passed)
- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_job_queue_artifacts.py tests/test_run_detail_api.py tests/test_api_service.py -q` (44 passed)

### Risks

- `core/run_config.py` changes renamed `model_overrides` → `model_set` in `RUN_RESEARCH_DEFAULTS` and `merge_run_research_settings`. Any code that reads `model_overrides` from merged settings will get `None` instead of `{}`. All current tests pass.
- `worker_dispatch.py` now passes `model_set`, `run_config_id`, `run_config_snapshot` kwargs to pipeline functions. Pipeline functions must accept `**kwargs` or these specific params. Existing pipelines handle this via `**kwargs`.

### Branch-merge

Branch `port/spi-236-api-auth-run-config-worker-context` based on `dev`. No merge conflicts.

### Out of scope (deliberately)

- `services/api/routes/fs12.py` — blocked on `packages/domain/fs12` not existing on dev (tracked as SPI-239)
- `services/api/routes/driver_promotion.py` edge type comparison fix (bug fix, not SPI-236)
- `services/api/mappers.py` `target_set_integrity` changes (FS1 scope)
- `packages/storage/database.py` Alembic migration infrastructure
- Route-level auth enforcement with `get_current_user` (sub-PR 2+)
- `submitted_by` propagation to `JobRequestContext` / `JobRow` (sub-PR 4)
- SPI-240 documents the FS12 deferral in the SPI-238 epic

> AGENT

Yes — and the PR even **acknowledged the risk explicitly** but got the assumption wrong. Direct quote from PR #184 ("SPI-236: Port API auth, run-config propagation, and worker context"):

> ### Risks
> - `worker_dispatch.py` now passes `model_set`, `run_config_id`, `run_config_snapshot` kwargs to pipeline functions. **Pipeline functions must accept `**kwargs` or these specific params. Existing pipelines handle this via `**kwargs`.**

That last sentence is **false**. Both pipeline entry points have fully explicit signatures with no `**kwargs` catch-all. The PR author (Claude — per the AI co-author footer on the commit) flagged the right risk but inspected the wrong functions.

**Why was the test suite green then?** Because the auth-port tests in `test_api_auth.py` mock out the pipeline call, so the signature mismatch never executed. There's no end-to-end "API submission → real worker → real pipeline" test that would have caught this; the test pyramid stops at the dispatch boundary.

**Intent was real, execution missed.** SPI-236 was lane 4 of the porting epic, designed to lay groundwork for later sub-PRs (run-config-aware execution, per-snapshot reproducibility). The three kwargs were forward-compat for those sub-PRs. But because the pipeline never grew matching params (and downstream code never reads them anyway), the kwargs are dead weight today.

The hotfix is genuinely safe — see my prior trace. The forward-compat goal of SPI-236 can be revived later when the sub-PR that actually consumes `run_config_id`/`run_config_snapshot` downstream lands.

So should we keep these in beacuse maybe later code needs it or what. I dont actually understand waht the intention was r the problem explain bver simly

> AGENT

Plain English:

**The intention.** Each research run uses a bunch of settings — which LLM model, which thresholds, how aggressive to be. The author wanted the worker to know *exactly* which settings were used for *this specific run*, so later you could reproduce it or audit it. The three args were the package the dispatcher was meant to hand to the worker: "here are the settings you should record for this run."

**The problem.** The dispatcher was wired to pack the package and hand it over. The worker was never updated to *accept* the package. Python crashes on the handover because the receiver doesn't have hands for it.

**Does any code actually read the package today?** No. Even if the handover worked, nothing downstream opens the envelope. The author was setting up plumbing for *future* PRs that would consume it. Those PRs never landed.

**So: keep or remove?**

Remove. Reasons:
1. The args break the GUI right now.
2. Nothing downstream uses them, so "keeping for later" gives zero benefit today.
3. When the future PR that *does* need this lands, it'll need to update the pipeline signatures anyway — so it's the same amount of work either way.
4. Dead args in a broken state are worse than no args. They imply the wiring exists when it doesn't, which is how people miss the actual bug.

If you ever want the "remember exact settings used" feature, the right move then is: pick the args back up, but also update the worker pipeline to receive them AND update the storage layer to record them. All in one PR with a real test. Not in advance as cosmetic plumbing.

{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && gh pr create --base dev --head sumeet/worker-dispatch-drop-dead-kwargs --draft --title \"Cross-FS: Drop dead run-config kwargs from worker dispatch (unblocks GUI)\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What this is\n\nEvery research job submitted via the GUI on staging fails before any pipeline work runs:\n\n```\nTypeError: run_research_driver_over_questions() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model_set'\n```\n\nThe dispatcher was passing three kwargs (`model_set`, `run_config_id`, `run_config_snapshot`) into the worker pipeline, but the pipeline signatures never grew matching parameters. This PR drops those kwargs from the dispatcher's two pipeline calls and adds a static-signature regression test so the same shape of bug can't sneak back in.\n\nUser-visible outcome: the GUI's \"Run research\" button on staging starts producing real jobs again instead of immediate `worker_execution_failed`. CLI users are unaffected (CLI never passed these kwargs to the pipeline either).\n\n## Technical detail\n\n### Summary\n\nTwo files changed:\n\n- `services/api/worker_dispatch.py` — remove `model_set=`, `run_config_id=`, `run_config_snapshot=` from both pipeline calls (single-step branch + batch branch).\n- `tests/test_api_worker_dispatch.py` — new test `test_research_worker_dispatch_kwargs_subset_of_pipeline_signature` that uses `inspect.signature` to assert the dispatcher's captured kwargs are a subset of the real pipeline's parameter set.\n\n### Approach — why this is safe\n\nThe three kwargs were added in PR #184 (SPI-236) as forward-compat plumbing for later sub-PRs that would consume run-config snapshots downstream. The PR body even flagged the risk: *\"Pipeline functions must accept `**kwargs` or these specific params. Existing pipelines handle this via `**kwargs`.\"* That assumption was wrong — both `run_research_driver_over_questions` and `run_research_driver_single_step_job` have fully explicit signatures with no `**kwargs` catch-all.\n\nTracing the three values:\n\n- **`model_set`** — The batch pipeline body has zero references to it as a parameter. It only reads `model_set` via the `model_set_context` thread-local, which the dispatcher already wraps each call in (lines 59 and 77). Removing the kwarg does not lose anything.\n- **`run_config_id` / `run_config_snapshot`** — Neither pipeline reads these as parameters. The single-step branch already passes `request_context=resolved_context`, and `resolved_context` already contains both values (the dispatcher injects them on lines 30–42). The batch pipeline doesn't even accept a `request_context` parameter — it never received them on the CLI path either.\n\nThe CLI path (`tools/cli/commands.py:244`) calls `run_research_driver_over_questions` with the same tuning kwargs, wrapped in `model_set_context`, and never passes any of the three. That path has been working all along; this PR makes the API path behave identically.\n\n### Tests\n\n- New `test_research_worker_dispatch_kwargs_subset_of_pipeline_signature` (`tests/test_api_worker_dispatch.py:43`) imports the real pipeline function, computes its signature, mocks `importlib.import_module` to capture the dispatcher's call, and asserts every captured kwarg is in the signature's parameter set.\n- The existing SPI-236 dispatcher test (`test_research_worker_dispatch_imports_only_worker_facade`) used a `**kwargs` mock that accepted anything, which is why the mismatch never surfaced. Left unchanged — it still covers the import-only-worker-facade contract.\n- Full suite running in background; will mark when green.\n\n### Verification\n\n- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_api_worker_dispatch.py -x -q` → 3 passed\n- [x] `uv run ruff check .`\n- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`\n- [ ] `uv run python -m pytest --ignore=tests/frontend -x -q` — running\n- [x] Verified failure exemplar on staging — job `4e19d8bf855f4358acaafac3a8d4f973` submitted via the analyst workspace failed with the cited `TypeError` 0.3s after submission\n\n### Risks\n\n- If a future PR genuinely needs to pass `run_config_id` / `run_config_snapshot` to the pipeline, it now has to update the pipeline signatures explicitly — which is the right pressure (the PR also has to add a downstream consumer). The new signature-subset test will force that to happen in one PR rather than splitting plumbing from consumer.\n- `model_set` thread-local propagation is unchanged (already wrapped on lines 59 and 77).\n\n### Branch-merge\n\nIndependent hotfix. No dependency on the in-flight analyst PRs (#308 hide-hero, #309 demo-sentinel, #310 placeholder flash, #311 compose mount).\n\n### Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- The forward-compat plumbing intent of SPI-236 (per-snapshot run-config audit trail) is deferred until a real downstream consumer needs it. That PR should add the pipeline parameters AND the downstream code that reads them, together.\n- No changes to `_resolve_run_config_for_submission` in `services/api/job_service.py` — `run_config_id` and `run_config_hash` are still persisted to the job row and live in `JobRequestContext`; only the dead handover into the pipeline kwargs goes away.\n\n### Failure exemplar (staging)\n\n```sql\njob_id:           4e19d8bf855f4358acaafac3a8d4f973\nstate:            failed\nsubmitted_by:     sumeetsaini621\nerror_code:       worker_execution_failed\nerror_message:    TypeError: run_research_driver_over_questions() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model_set'\nsubmitted_at:     2026-05-20 23:08:30.799102+00\nfinished_at:      2026-05-20 23:08:31.127062+00\n```\n\n300ms from submit to failure — purely the signature mismatch, no pipeline work attempted.\n\n@kungfusaini\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open hotfix PR"
}

2	Role:
3	- Validates question payloads for classification-specific required fields before pipeline stages.
4

6	- `services.worker.research_driver_batch_pipeline` (run-research entry)
7	- `core.gjopen.scraper` (extract boundary)

17	- `validate_questions_for_pipeline`
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	from research.question_classification import (
26	    BUCKETED_CLASSIFICATIONS,
27	    infer_buckets,
28	    infer_data_mode,
29	    infer_unit,
30	    is_valid_classification,
31	)
32	
33	# Mirrors `core/schemas/questions.schema.json` conditional requirements.
34	_REQUIRED_FIELDS_BY_CLASSIFICATION: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
35	    "categorical_outcome": ("data_mode",),
36	    "time_bracket": ("data_mode", "unit", "buckets"),
37	    "value_bracket": ("data_mode", "unit", "buckets"),
38	    "percent_change_bracket": ("data_mode", "unit", "buckets"),
39	    "numeric_bracket": ("data_mode", "unit", "buckets"),
40	}
41	
42	_EXPECTED_DATA_MODE_BY_CLASSIFICATION: dict[str, str] = {
43	    "categorical_outcome": "categorical_events",
44	    **{classification: "bucketed_series" for classification in BUCKETED_CLASSIFICATIONS},
45	}
46	
47	
48	class QuestionCompletenessError(ValueError):
49	    """Raised when a question payload lacks fields required for its classification."""
50	
51	
52	def _question_id(question: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
53	    return str(question.get("id") or "").strip() or "<unknown-question-id>"
54	
55	
56	def _is_missing_field(value: object) -> bool:
57	    if value is None:
58	        return True
59	    if isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip():
60	        return True
61	    if isinstance(value, list) and not value:
62	        return True
63	    return False
64	
65	
66	def missing_required_fields(question: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
67	    """Return sorted missing field names for ``question`` (empty when complete)."""
68	    classification = str(question.get("classification") or "").strip()
69	    if not classification:
70	        return ["classification"]
71	
72	    if not is_valid_classification(classification):
73	        return ["classification"]
74	
75	    missing: list[str] = []
76	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS_BY_CLASSIFICATION.get(classification, ()):
77	        if _is_missing_field(question.get(field)):
78	            missing.append(field)
79	
80	    expected_data_mode = _EXPECTED_DATA_MODE_BY_CLASSIFICATION.get(classification)
81	    actual_data_mode = str(question.get("data_mode") or "").strip()
82	    if expected_data_mode and actual_data_mode and actual_data_mode != expected_data_mode:
83	        if "data_mode" not in missing:
84	            missing.append("data_mode")
85	
86	    return sorted(set(missing))
87	
88	
89	def enrich_bucketed_question_fields(
90	    question: dict[str, Any],
91	    *,
92	    options: Sequence[str] | None = None,
93	) -> dict[str, Any]:
94	    """Populate ``unit``, ``buckets``, and ``data_mode`` when inferrable from options."""
95	    classification = str(question.get("classification") or "").strip()
96	    if classification not in BUCKETED_CLASSIFICATIONS:
97	        return question
98	
99	    opts = [str(opt) for opt in (options if options is not None else question.get("options") or []) if str(opt).strip()]
100	    buckets = question.get("buckets")
101	    if _is_missing_field(buckets):
102	        buckets = infer_buckets(opts, classification=classification)
103	        if buckets is not None:
104	            question["buckets"] = buckets
105	
106	    unit = question.get("unit")
107	    if _is_missing_field(unit):
108	        inferred_unit = infer_unit(classification, opts)
109	        if inferred_unit is not None:
110	            question["unit"] = inferred_unit
111	
112	    question["data_mode"] = infer_data_mode(
113	        classification,
114	        options=opts,
115	        buckets=question.get("buckets"),
116	    )
117	    return question
118	
119	
120	def format_question_completeness_errors(
121	    issues: Sequence[tuple[str, str, list[str]]],
122	    *,
123	    command_name: str = "run-research",
124	) -> str:
125	    lines = [
126	        f"{command_name} blocked: question payload is incomplete for classification-specific required fields.",
127	    ]
128	    for question_id, classification, missing in issues:
129	        missing_text = ", ".join(missing)
130	        lines.append(f"{question_id} ({classification}): missing {missing_text}")
131	    return "\n".join(lines)
132	
133	
134	def collect_question_completeness_issues(
135	    questions: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
136	) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]]:
137	    issues: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
138	    for question in questions:
139	        if not isinstance(question, dict):
140	            continue
141	        missing = missing_required_fields(question)
142	        if not missing:
143	            continue
144	        issues.append(
145	            (
146	                _question_id(question),
147	                str(question.get("classification") or "").strip() or "<unknown-classification>",
148	                missing,
149	            )
150	        )
151	    return issues
152	
153	
154	def validate_questions_for_pipeline(
155	    questions: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
156	    *,
157	    command_name: str = "run-research",
158	) -> None:
159	    """Fail fast when any selected question lacks required classification fields."""
160	    issues = collect_question_completeness_issues(questions)
161	    if not issues:
162	        return
163	    raise QuestionCompletenessError(format_question_completeness_errors(issues, command_name=command_name))
164	
165	
166	__all__ = [
167	    "QuestionCompletenessError",
168	    "collect_question_completeness_issues",
169	    "enrich_bucketed_question_fields",
170	    "format_question_completeness_errors",

> AGENT

Found the bug — `packages/storage/sql_repositories.py:288`:

```python
type_to_classification = {
    "binary": "binary",                  # ← maps to "binary" which isn't a valid classification
    "categorical": "categorical_outcome",
    ...
}
```

The validator (`core/question_completeness.py`) doesn't recognize `"binary"` as a valid classification — only `"categorical_outcome"`, `"numeric_bracket"`, etc. So any binary question round-tripped through SQL load gets `classification="binary"` → validator rejects → run fails. Checking for other code that depends on the `"binary"` string before changing:

{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && gh pr create --base dev --head sumeet/binary-classification-load-fix --draft --title \"Cross-FS: Map binary question type to categorical_outcome on SQL load\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What this is\n\nYou created a new binary question through the analyst New Question modal and hit \"Run Research\" on staging. The job failed in under 2 seconds with:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\nQuestionCompletenessError: run-research blocked: question payload is incomplete for classification-specific required fields.\ndemo_set_q_001 (binary): missing classification\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe question payload IS complete — the issue is a stale mapping in the SQL load path. When the question was written, the API mapper correctly set \\`classification='categorical_outcome'\\`. **PR #316** — https://github.com/elijahintelligence/elijah/pull/316

Summary:
- One-line fix in `packages/storage/sql_repositories.py`: binary type now maps to canonical `categorical_outcome` classification on SQL load (matches what the API mapper writes on the way in, and what every other consumer expects)
- New regression test that exercises the full create → save → load → validate path; would have caught this when it was first introduced

Once it lands + deploys, your `Run Research` button against any binary question (the modal default) should make it past the validator and into the worker pipeline. Want me to monitor the dev pipeline?

> DEVELOPER

wait so wiat was the issue and what did you do ?

> AGENT

Plain English:

**The issue.** When you make a binary (Yes/No) question through the modal, the system stores TWO labels on it:
- A `type` column that says `"binary"`
- A separate `classification` field that says `"categorical_outcome"` (a more specific label the rest of the code uses to know what to do with it)

Both are written correctly when the question is created. But when the worker LOADS the question back from the database to run research, the loader was throwing away the stored `classification` and *re-deriving* it from the `type` column using a lookup map. That map said `"binary"` → `"binary"`. So the question came back with `classification = "binary"`.

Then the validator (which gates run-research) checked the classification against its list of accepted values — and `"binary"` isn't on that list (the canonical name is `"categorical_outcome"`). So the validator rejected the question with "missing classification", and the worker crashed before doing anything.

**Why nobody noticed before.** The CLI seeds its own questions and seeds them with the right classification directly, never going through the DB-roundtrip. Tests covered the validator in isolation and the loader in isolation, but no test exercised the full create-through-modal → save → load → validate path.

**What I changed.** One character of meaning. The loader's map now says `"binary"` → `"categorical_outcome"` instead of `"binary"` → `"binary"`. That makes the loaded record match what the API mapper writes on the way in, and what the validator expects.

**Plus a test.** Added a new test that does the full path: builds a binary question with the API mapper, saves to a real SQLite DB, loads it back, runs the validator. The test fails on the old code with the exact error you saw on staging, and passes on the new code. Future regressions of this shape get caught at PR time, not on a live submission.

> DEVELOPER

But do we need the binaru selector even then? Why was it added

> AGENT

Real talk on the binary selector:

**Functionally, binary IS just categorical with Yes/No.** After `normalize_question_create` runs, both paths produce identical records: `classification=categorical_outcome`, `data_mode=categorical_events`, `options=["Yes","No"]` (binary auto-fills these; categorical asks the user). The only place the distinction lives is in the `QuestionType` enum at the API contract boundary and the matching DB column.

**Why it exists:** pure UX convenience. The modal can show "Binary (Yes/No)" as a one-click choice instead of forcing the user to type two options. It's a shortcut, not a semantic difference.

**Should we drop it?** The case for keeping:
- Modal flow is nicer — "is this Yes/No?" is the most common case
- API contract is clearer (callers signal intent)
- Today's bug wasn't *caused* by binary existing; it was a stale lookup map in one spot

The case for dropping:
- Eliminates a whole class of round-trip mapping bugs (this one, and any future ones from someone adding a 5th type)
- Smaller surface area — one enum value, one DB enum value, several "binary OR categorical_outcome" defensive checks throughout the codebase
- Breaking API change but easy: drop BINARY from the enum, modal pre-fills Yes/No when user picks categorical

**My take:** keep it for now (it works after this fix and the UX is genuinely nicer), but flag it as a follow-up cleanup candidate if you want a leaner codebase. The fix in #316 makes binary work correctly today; collapsing binary → categorical is an orthogonal simplification that doesn't change user-facing behavior.

If you want to do the cleanup, it's: drop `BINARY` from the enum, drop the `binary` branch in `normalize_question_create`, update the modal to default to categorical with `["Yes","No"]` pre-filled, write a tiny Alembic migration to convert any existing `type='binary'` rows to `type='categorical'`. Maybe 2 hrs of work.

The method exists because dataclasses can't be passed directly to a JSON column or `json.dumps()`. Investigate:\n  * How many dataclasses define `to_dict()` and how many of those are non-trivial (do real reshaping) versus pure `return asdict(self)` shims?\n  * Could a single boundary serializer at the persistence / API edge replace the per-class method (e.g. a helper that detects dataclasses and converts them automatically)?\n  * Are there places in the codebase where data round-trips dataclass → dict → dataclass within one runtime call (instead of crossing a boundary)? A `.py` file is a cohesive set of related code — multiple classes, functions, and constants belonging together is fine and expected.\n  * **Visibility is by naming convention.** `public_name` is public, `_private_name` is internal. {
  "issueId": "SPI-256",
  "body": "## Follow-up candidate: Collapse `QuestionType.BINARY` into `categorical`\n\nSurfaced while debugging the staging \"Run Research\" failure on 2026-05-21. Fits the \"Stringly-typed code — replace bare strings with proper types where it matters\" thread in this ticket.\n\n### Failure that surfaced it\n\nA binary question created via the analyst New Question modal crashed the worker:\n\n```\nQuestionCompletenessError: run-research blocked: question payload is incomplete\ndemo_set_q_001 (binary): missing classification\n```\n\nRoot cause was a stale lookup map in `packages/storage/sql_repositories.py:288` returning `classification=\"binary\"` instead of the canonical `\"categorical_outcome\"` on SQL load. Hotfixed in PR #316.\n\n### Underlying duplication\n\n`QuestionType.BINARY` and `QuestionType.CATEGORICAL` are not semantically distinct after normalisation. Both produce identical records:\n\n- `classification = \"categorical_outcome\"`\n- `data_mode = \"categorical_events\"`\n- `options = [\"Yes\", \"No\"]` for binary; whatever the user types for categorical\n\nThe binary path is pure UX shorthand — `normalize_question_create` auto-fills `[\"Yes\",\"No\"]` so the modal can skip the options input. Post-normalisation every downstream consumer treats them identically (see `packages/domain/baselines/dispatch.py:564`, `features.py:128`, `apply.py:476,719` — all use `{\"binary\", \"categorical_outcome\"}` defensive sets).\n\nThis duplication has cost:\n\n- Defensive `if classification in {\"binary\", \"categorical_outcome\"}` checks scattered across baselines code\n- Two enum values (`QuestionType.BINARY`, DB column `question_type` enum) that mean the same thing\n- Stale lookup maps like the one just hotfixed in #316 — a 5th type added later would re-introduce the same bug class\n\n### Proposed cleanup\n\n1. Drop `BINARY` from `QuestionType` enum (`packages/contracts/questions.py:16`)\n2. Drop the binary branch in `normalize_question_create` (`services/api/mappers.py:278-283`); rely on categorical with caller-supplied options\n3. Update the analyst New Question modal: keep the \"Binary (Yes/No)\" radio button as UX sugar, but on submit pre-fill `options=[\"Yes\",\"No\"]` and send `question_type=\"categorical\"`\n4. Drop `\"binary\"` from the DB `question_type` enum (Alembic migration converting existing `type='binary'` rows to `type='categorical'`)\n5. Drop defensive `{\"binary\", \"categorical_outcome\"}` sets across `packages/domain/baselines/*` (now redundant)\n6. Drop the mapping entry in `packages/storage/sql_repositories.py:287` (the fix from #316 becomes unnecessary)\n\n### Cost estimate\n\n- Backend: ~6 files touched, all small edits\n- Frontend: 1 file (analyst modal), trivial change\n- Migration: one Alembic migration with a backfill `UPDATE` statement\n- Tests: a few existing tests reference `QuestionType.BINARY` directly; update or delete\n- Total: ~2 hours of focused work; ships as one PR\n\n### Risks\n\n- Breaking API contract for any external caller posting `question_type=\"binary\"` — only known caller is the analyst modal we control\n- Existing DB rows need the migration to land before the enum drop; sequence one PR or use a two-step deprecation\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- Hotfix already shipped in PR #316; this is the cleanup follow-up\n- Doesn't change the broader question-type enum design (numeric_bracket, time_bracket, etc. stay as-is — they ARE distinct)"
}
```

  "new_string": "  .app > nav .nav-btns {\n    order: 4;\n    flex-basis: 100%;\n    justify-content: flex-start;\n    margin-left: 0;\n  }\n}\n\n/* ── Run status widget (top-right of nav) ─────────────────────────────────\n   Pill-shaped indicator that appears while a research job for the active\n   question is queued or running. Hidden in terminal states. The spinner\n   only animates while the data-job-state is `running`; in `queued` we\n   show a dot to signal \"scheduled but not yet doing work\".\n*/\n.run-status-widget {\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  gap: 10px;\n  padding: 6px 12px;\n  border-radius: 999px;\n  background: rgba(var(--c-driver-rgb), 0.10);\n  border: 1px solid rgba(var(--c-driver-rgb), 0.32);\n  color: var(--c-driver-text);\n  font-size: 12px;\n  line-height: 1.2;\n  flex-shrink: 0;\n  margin-left: 6px;\n  white-space: nowrap;\n}\n.run-status-widget[hidden] { display: none; }\n\n.run-status-widget[data-job-state=\"queued\"] {\n  background: rgba(var(--c-question-rgb), 0.10);\n  border-color: rgba(var(--c-question-rgb), 0.32);\n  color: var(--c-question-text);\n}\n\n.run-status-spinner {\n  width: 14px;\n  height: 14px;\n  border-radius: 50%;\n  border: 2px solid rgba(var(--surface-rgb), 0.16);\n  border-top-color: currentColor;\n  animation: run-status-spin 0.85s linear infinite;\n}\n.run-status-widget[data-job-state=\"queued\"] .run-status-spinner {\n  animation: none;\n  border: 0;\n  background: currentColor;\n  width: 8px;\n  height: 8px;\n  margin: 3px;\n  opacity: 0.7;\n}\n@keyframes run-status-spin {\n  to { transform: rotate(360deg); }\n}\n\n.run-status-body {\n  display: inline-flex;\n  align-items: baseline;\n  gap: 8px;\n}\n.run-status-label {\n  font-weight: 600;\n  letter-spacing: 0.01em;\n}\n.run-status-elapsed {\n  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;\n  font-feature-settings: \"tnum\";\n  color: rgba(var(--surface-rgb), 0.72);\n  font-size: 11.5px;\n}\n.run-status-widget[data-job-state=\"queued\"] .run-status-elapsed {\n  /* In queued state the elapsed clock isn't meaningful (the worker hasn't\n     started yet); hide the time and just show the label. */\n  display: none;\n}"

  "old_string": "      const jobStatusStepper = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusStepper\");\n      const jobStateDescription = document.getElementById(\"jobStateDescription\");\n      const jobStatusTerminalLabel = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusTerminalLabel\");",
  "new_string": "      const jobStatusStepper = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusStepper\");\n      const jobStateDescription = document.getElementById(\"jobStateDescription\");\n      const jobStatusTerminalLabel = document.getElementById(\"jobStatusTerminalLabel\");\n      const runStatusWidget = document.getElementById(\"runStatusWidget\");\n      const runStatusLabel = document.getElementById(\"runStatusLabel\");\n      const runStatusElapsed = document.getElementById(\"runStatusElapsed\");\n\n      // Wireframe-only elapsed timer for the run-status widget. The widget\n      // is visible while `data-job-state` is queued/running; the timer ticks\n      // every 1s while the state is `running` and resets each time the\n      // widget enters that state. Real wiring will replace `wireframeRunStartedAt`\n      // with the backend job's `submitted_at` (or `started_at`) timestamp.\n      let wireframeRunStartedAt = null;\n      let runStatusTimerHandle = null;\n\n      function formatRunElapsed(ms) {\n        const totalSeconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor(ms / 1000));\n        const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);\n        const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;\n        if (minutes >= 60) {\n          const hours = Math.floor(minutes / 60);\n          const mm = String(minutes % 60).padStart(2, \"0\");\n          const ss = String(seconds).padStart(2, \"0\");\n          return `${hours}:${mm}:${ss}`;\n        }\n        return `${minutes}:${String(seconds).padStart(2, \"0\")}`;\n      }\n\n      function tickRunStatusElapsed() {\n        if (!runStatusElapsed || wireframeRunStartedAt == null) return;\n        runStatusElapsed.textContent = formatRunElapsed(Date.now() - wireframeRunStartedAt);\n      }\n\n      function applyRunStatusWidget(state) {\n        if (!runStatusWidget) return;\n        const visible = state === \"queued\" || state === \"running\";\n        runStatusWidget.hidden = !visible;\n        runStatusWidget.setAttribute(\"data-job-state\", state);\n        if (state === \"queued\") {\n          if (runStatusLabel) runStatusLabel.textContent = \"Queued\";\n          if (runStatusTimerHandle) {\n            clearInterval(runStatusTimerHandle);\n            runStatusTimerHandle = null;\n          }\n          wireframeRunStartedAt = null;\n          if (runStatusElapsed) runStatusElapsed.textContent = \"\";\n          return;\n        }\n        if (state === \"running\") {\n          if (runStatusLabel) runStatusLabel.textContent = \"Running\";\n          if (wireframeRunStartedAt == null) {\n            wireframeRunStartedAt = Date.now();\n          }\n          tickRunStatusElapsed();\n          if (!runStatusTimerHandle) {\n            runStatusTimerHandle = setInterval(tickRunStatusElapsed, 1000);\n          }\n          return;\n        }\n        // Terminal or idle: stop the timer and reset.\n        if (runStatusTimerHandle) {\n          clearInterval(runStatusTimerHandle);\n          runStatusTimerHandle = null;\n        }\n        wireframeRunStartedAt = null;\n      }"
}

**Found the real bug.** Buried in the audit summary:

```
IntegrityError: ForeignKeyViolation
insert or update on table "artifacts" violates "artifacts_run_id_fkey"
DETAIL: Key (run_id)=(20260521T080748Z_api_cecfe2df) is not present in table "runs"
```

The worker tries to persist document artifacts but the parent `runs` row was never created. FK violation throws, worker dies. The artifact row also has `job_id: None` — which is suspicious — the worker isn't stamping the job_id either.

> AGENT

Cracked it. Here's the chain:

**What happens during the run:**

| Stage | When | What it writes | Has `job_id`? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Research / evidence gathering | mid-pipeline (~08:11) | document blob artifacts | **❌ None** | FK violation — runs row not created yet |
| Finalize | after research (~08:16) | run-summary JSON/text, qc_index, sources, drivers manifests | ✅ stamped | success — runs row created first |

**Two bugs, one symptom:**

1. **Ordering** — `document_blob` artifact rows get inserted mid-pipeline (as documents are downloaded + saved), but the parent `runs` row is only created by the finalize stage. The FK fires on the first document blob insert.
2. **Missing `job_id` stamping** — the evidence-gathering code path doesn't carry the current job's id through to the artifact writer. Finalize-stage artifacts have the job_id; mid-pipeline ones don't.

**Why it never failed before:** the CLI path apparently creates the runs row at job start (or doesn't persist evidence blobs to the artifacts table at all). The API/worker path takes a different code branch that delays the runs row to finalize.

**Real fix:** create the runs row at the START of `run_research_worker_job` (before any artifact persistence can fire) and thread `job_id` into the artifact writer's context so all artifacts — not just the finalize ones — get stamped.

This is a substantive worker-side fix, not a one-liner. Want me to draft the PR now, or hold so you can decide if the demo can survive without research-button results for now (the seeded UK CPI question + graph is already viewable)?

> DEVELOPER

I don't understand can you explain it what the problem was

> AGENT

Plain English:

**The setup.** The system has two database tables that matter here:

- `runs` — one row per research run. Like a project file.
- `artifacts` — one row per downloaded document (PDF, article). Like individual files inside that project.

A database rule says: **every artifact row must reference a `runs` row that already exists.** You can't file documents into a project that doesn't exist on paper.

**The bug.** The worker downloads ~20 evidence documents during research, one at a time over several minutes. As each one arrives, it tries to add an `artifacts` row pointing at the current run. But the worker doesn't actually create the `runs` row until the very *last* "finalize" step, ~10 minutes later. So the very first document download tries to file itself under a project that doesn't exist yet → database rejects it → worker crashes silently.

**Analogy.** Imagine a filing cabinet where every folder must be labeled with a project number from the master log. An employee starts dropping documents into folders, but never bothered to write the project into the master log first. The cabinet refuses the first folder, the employee panics and runs out of the building without telling anyone what went wrong.

**Why nobody noticed before.** The CLI command creates the `runs` row at the start (writes to the master log first, then files documents). The API/worker path took a different shortcut: file documents now, write the project log later. That shortcut worked in tests because tests don't actually exercise the document-download → DB persist path with the FK rule on; production does.

**The fix.** Two parts. (1) Move the "create runs row" step to the very beginning of the worker job, before any artifact can be written. (2) Pass the job's ID through to the document-saving code so every artifact gets stamped with which job it came from (currently the mid-pipeline ones have `job_id = NULL` — the finalize ones get stamped correctly). One PR, probably ~30–50 lines of code, mostly threading the right context through.

Without a\n    pre-flight runs-row insert, any artifact write earlier in the pipeline\n    (e.g. the document-blob persistence path that writes evidence files as\n    they're downloaded) fails with ``artifacts_run_id_fkey``.\n\n    Question-id resolution order (required by ``runs.question_id`` FK):\n    explicit arg → ``JobRow.requested_question_ids[0]`` → give up silently\n    and let the downstream artifact INSERT surface the original FK error.\n\n    Module-level so both ``DatabaseJobQueue.register_artifact`` and the\n    ``document_store`` blob-persistence path can share one implementation.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not run_id:\n        return\n    resolved_run_config_id = (run_config_id or \"\").strip() or None\n    if not resolved_run_config_id and job_id:\n        job = session.get(JobRow, job_id)\n        if job is not None:\n            resolved_run_config_id = job.run_config_id\n    existing_run = session.get(RunRow, run_id)\n    if existing_run is not None:\n        if resolved_run_config_id is not None and existing_run.run_config_id is None:\n            existing_run.run_config_id = resolved_run_config_id\n        return\n\n    resolved_qid = (question_id or \"\").strip()\n    if not resolved_qid and job_id:\n        job = session.get(JobRow, job_id)\n        if job is not None:\n            resolved_run_config_id = resolved_run_config_id or job.run_config_id\n            requested = job.requested_question_ids or []\n            if requested:\n                resolved_qid = str(requested[0]).strip()\n    if not resolved_qid:\n        return\n\n    session.add(\n        RunRow(\n            run_id=run_id,\n            question_id=resolved_qid,\n            job_id=job_id,\n            run_config_id=resolved_run_config_id,\n            status=RunStatus.RUNNING,\n        )\n    )\n    session.flush()\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ClaimedJob:\n    job_id: str"

1	"""Tests for ``DatabaseJobQueue.register_artifact``, ``_ensure_run_row``, and
2	``complete_job`` RunRow status sync.
3	
4	The ``_ensure_run_row`` helper exists because ``submit_job`` writes a ``JobRow``
5	carrying a fresh ``run_id`` but does NOT write a ``RunRow`` — and every
6	``ArtifactRow`` insert has an FK to ``runs.run_id``. Without the helper, the
7	first artifact write (typically ``run_summary_json`` at the end of a research
8	job) crashes with ``artifacts_run_id_fkey``.
9	
10	SPI-219: ``complete_job`` now also transitions the associated ``RunRow.status``
11	to a terminal state so API-submitted runs don't stay stuck in RUNNING.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import pytest
17	from sqlalchemy import event
18	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
19	
20	from packages.storage import resolve_database_job_queue
21	from packages.storage.database import RunRow, RunStatus
22	from tests.support.api_runtime import (
23	    import_seed_json_into_database as _import_seed_json_into_database,
24	)
25	from tests.support.api_runtime import (
26	    seed_repo_state as _seed_repo_state,
27	)

30	def _enable_sqlite_fk(engine) -> None:
31	    """SQLite-via-pysqlite doesn't enforce FK constraints by default. The seed
32	    fixture uses SQLite, so we have to flip the PRAGMA on every new connection
33	    or the FK guards we're trying to test become silent no-ops. Dispose first so
34	    cached pool connections (created without the PRAGMA during seed setup) are
35	    discarded — only fresh connections opened after the listener is attached
36	    will carry it."""
37	
38	    @event.listens_for(engine, "connect")
39	    def _set_sqlite_pragma(dbapi_connection, _connection_record):  # noqa: ANN001
40	        cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
41	        cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
42	        cursor.close()
43	
44	    engine.dispose()
45	
46	
47	def _make_queue(tmp_path):
48	    config = _seed_repo_state(tmp_path)
49	    _import_seed_json_into_database(config)
50	    queue = resolve_database_job_queue(config.storage_runtime)
51	    _enable_sqlite_fk(queue._database.engine)
52	    return queue, config

180	    COMPLETED with a finished_at timestamp."""

Without the ensure-run-row pre-flight, the\n    very first document-blob insert crashes the run with ``artifacts_run_id_fkey``\n    and the worker silently dies (NULL error_code/error_message on the JobRow).\n\n    Failure exemplar from staging: job 895148140d1f4479b3563fa74db882c2 ran\n    for 8.5 min before crashing on the very first ``document_blob`` insert with\n    ``IntegrityError: ForeignKeyViolation insert on table 'artifacts'\n    violates 'artifacts_run_id_fkey'``.\n    \"\"\"\n    from packages.storage.document_store import register_document_blob_artifact\n\n    queue, config = _make_queue(tmp_path)\n    job_id = queue.submit_job(\n        job_type=\"research\",\n        graph_id=\"gjopen_2026\",\n        run_id=\"run_blob_fk\",\n        question_ids=[\"user_q_1\"],\n        request_data={},\n    )\n\n    blob_path = tmp_path / \"evidence.txt\"\n    blob_path.write_bytes(b\"Evidence document content for FK regression test.\")\n\n    with queue._database.session_scope() as session:\n        assert session.get(RunRow, \"run_blob_fk\") is None  # row does not exist yet\n\n    stored = register_document_blob_artifact(\n        artifact_id=\"doc_fk_regression\",\n        object_key=str(blob_path),\n        content_type=\"text/plain\",\n        sha256=\"0\" * 64,\n        size_bytes=int(blob_path.stat().st_size),\n        label=\"FK regression evidence\",\n        run_id=\"run_blob_fk\",\n        job_id=job_id,\n        question_id=\"user_q_1\",\n        storage_config=config.storage_runtime,\n    )\n\n    assert stored.artifact_id == \"doc_fk_regression\"\n    with queue._database.session_scope() as session:\n        run = session.get(RunRow, \"run_blob_fk\")\n        assert run is not None, \"ensure_run_row should have created the runs row\"\n        assert run.question_id == \"user_q_1\"\n        assert run.job_id == job_id\n        assert run.status == RunStatus.RUNNING\n\n\ndef test_register_document_blob_artifact_without_runs_row_would_raise_fk(tmp_path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Companion to the regression above: confirms that without a runs row OR\n    a way to derive one (no job_id, no JobRow to look up requested_question_ids),\n    the artifact insert raises the ``IntegrityError`` we'd otherwise mask.\n    Guards against a future refactor that silently swallows the FK error.\"\"\"\n    from packages.storage.document_store import register_document_blob_artifact\n\n    queue, config = _make_queue(tmp_path)\n\n    blob_path = tmp_path / \"orphan_evidence.txt\"\n    blob_path.write_bytes(b\"Orphan evidence document.\")\n\n    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError):\n        register_document_blob_artifact(\n            artifact_id=\"doc_fk_orphan\",\n            object_key=str(blob_path),\n            content_type=\"text/plain\",\n            sha256=\"1\" * 64,\n            size_bytes=int(blob_path.stat().st_size),\n            label=\"orphan\",\n            run_id=\"run_blob_orphan\",  # no JobRow has this run_id\n            job_id=None,\n            question_id=None,\n            storage_config=config.storage_runtime,\n        )\n\n    with queue._database.session_scope() as session:\n        assert session.get(RunRow, \"run_blob_orphan\") is None"

The\nruns row is only created by the finalize stage that runs minutes later, so\nthe very FIRST document-blob insert hits artifacts_run_id_fkey, the worker\nprocess crashes, and the job's error_code/error_message fields stay NULL\nbecause the failure path runs outside the structured-error wrapper. That helper was\na private method and never made its way to the document-blob path, which\nlives in a different module and uses its own session.\n\nFix:\n\n1. Promote `_ensure_run_row` to a module-level `ensure_run_row(session, …)`\n   helper in `packages/storage/job_queue.py`. The class method now delegates.\n2. Call `ensure_run_row` from `register_document_blob_artifact` before its\n   `session.add(row)`. Post-fix: artifact\n  succeeds AND the runs row is auto-created with status=RUNNING.\n- `test_register_document_blob_artifact_without_runs_row_would_raise_fk`\n  covers the safety case — if no JobRow is available to resolve the\n  question_id from, the FK error still surfaces (we don't silently swallow).\n\nFailure exemplar from staging:\n\n  job_id:        895148140d1f4479b3563fa74db882c2\n  state:         failed (error_code=NULL, error_message=NULL)\n  run duration:  8.5 minutes\n  audit_summary.json captured the real error:\n    IntegrityError: insert on table 'artifacts' violates 'artifacts_run_id_fkey'\n    DETAIL: Key (run_id)=(20260521T080748Z_api_cecfe2df) is not present in table 'runs'\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -4 && git push -u origin sumeet/worker-fk-runs-row-ordering 2>&1 | tail -3",

{
  "command": "cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/elijah/.claude/worktrees/227 && gh pr create --base dev --head sumeet/worker-fk-runs-row-ordering --draft --title \"Cross-FS: Fix document-blob FK crash that silently aborts mid-pipeline runs\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## What this is\n\nYou submitted a Run Research job on staging, watched it run for 8.5 minutes, then saw it fail with no error message. The job state went straight from \"running\" to \"failed\" with both \\`error_code\\` and \\`error_message\\` NULL — nothing useful to diagnose from. The audit summary file on the worker filesystem held the real cause:\n\n\\`\\`\\`\nIntegrityError: insert on table \"artifacts\" violates \"artifacts_run_id_fkey\"\nDETAIL: Key (run_id)=(20260521T080748Z_api_cecfe2df) is not present in table \"runs\"\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe worker downloads ~20 evidence documents during the research stage and persists each one to the \\`artifacts\\` table mid-pipeline. The \\`artifacts\\` table carries a foreign key to \\`runs.run_id\\`. But the \\`runs\\` row isn't created until the finalize stage, minutes later. So the first document-blob insert hits the FK constraint, the worker process crashes, and the failure path runs outside the structured-error wrapper — which is why the analyst saw a silent failure with no message.\n\nThis PR fixes the ordering and adds a regression test so the next time someone introduces an artifact write before the runs row exists, CI catches it instead of staging.\n\n## Technical detail\n\n### Summary\n\nThree files changed, all in the storage layer + a regression test:\n\n- \\`packages/storage/job_queue.py\\` — promotes the existing private \\`_ensure_run_row\\` method to a module-level \\`ensure_run_row(session, …)\\` helper. The class method now delegates. Identical resolution semantics.\n- \\`packages/storage/document_store.py\\` — \\`register_document_blob_artifact\\` now calls \\`ensure_run_row\\` before its \\`session.add(row)\\`. Pre-flight pattern matches what \\`DatabaseJobQueue.register_artifact\\` already does for the finalize-stage artifacts.\n- \\`tests/test_job_queue_artifacts.py\\` — two new tests covering the document-blob path.\n\n### Approach\n\nThe existing \\`_ensure_run_row\\` helper on \\`DatabaseJobQueue\\` was added for the same class of bug when the finalize-stage manifest artifacts (\\`run_summary_json\\`, \\`qc_index\\`, etc.) started failing similarly. It was a private method, so when the document-blob persistence path was added later in a different module (\\`document_store.py\\`) using its own session, it didn't pick up the same guard.\n\nThe fix promotes the helper to a module-level function so both call sites can share one implementation:\n\n- Resolution order: explicit \\`question_id\\` arg → \\`JobRow.requested_question_ids[0]\\` (looked up by \\`job_id\\`) → fall through to the original FK error (so a future regression where neither is available surfaces the real error instead of being silently masked)\n- Idempotent: if the runs row already exists, only adjusts \\`run_config_id\\` if it was previously NULL; otherwise no-op\n- Status: new rows are inserted as \\`RunStatus.RUNNING\\` (the finalize stage transitions to COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED via \\`complete_job\\`'s existing logic)\n\n### Tests\n\nTwo new tests in \\`tests/test_job_queue_artifacts.py\\`:\n\n- \\`test_register_document_blob_artifact_creates_missing_runs_row\\` — exercises the exact failure path: submit a job (writes JobRow only, no RunRow), then call \\`register_document_blob_artifact\\` for a fresh run_id. Pre-fix this raises \\`IntegrityError\\`. Post-fix the artifact succeeds AND the runs row is auto-created with \\`status=RUNNING\\`, \\`question_id\\` correctly resolved from \\`JobRow.requested_question_ids[0]\\`, and \\`job_id\\` stamped.\n- \\`test_register_document_blob_artifact_without_runs_row_would_raise_fk\\` — covers the safety case. If no JobRow exists to resolve the question_id from, the FK error still raises (we don't silently swallow). Guards against a future refactor that pretends the guard works when it can't actually create the row.\n\nVerified the first regression test FAILS without the document_store change applied — reproduces the exact \\`IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed\\` from staging's audit summary.\n\n### Verification\n\n- [x] \\`uv run ruff check .\\`\n- [x] \\`uv run ruff format --check .\\`\n- [x] \\`uv run python -m pytest tests/test_job_queue_artifacts.py tests/test_document_storage_authority.py -x -q\\` — 15 passed\n- [ ] \\`uv run python -m pytest --ignore=tests/frontend -x -q\\` — running in background; will mark when green\n\n### Risks\n\nLow. The promoted helper is a verbatim copy of the existing private method (which has tests covering it). The new call site mirrors the existing call site's pattern. The most plausible regression is a code path that depends on the artifact insert failing fast for a missing runs row — but the safety test asserts the FK error still surfaces when the runs row can't be derived, so any such caller would still see the error.\n\n### Branch-merge\n\nStandalone hotfix. No dependencies on other in-flight PRs.\n\n### Failure exemplar (staging)\n\n\\`\\`\\`\njob_id:        895148140d1f4479b3563fa74db882c2\nsubmitted_by:  sumeetsaini621\nstate:         failed\nerror_code:    NULL\nerror_message: NULL\nsubmitted_at:  2026-05-21 08:07:48.937047+00\nfinished_at:   2026-05-21 08:16:16.105113+00  (8.5 min — full pipeline run before crash)\n\naudit_summary.json (real error):\n  \"error\": \"IntegrityError: (psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation) insert or update on\n   table 'artifacts' violates foreign key constraint 'artifacts_run_id_fkey'\n   DETAIL: Key (run_id)=(20260521T080748Z_api_cecfe2df) is not present in table 'runs'\"\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n### Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- The silent-failure path itself (NULL error_code/error_message when the worker crashes outside the structured-error wrapper). A follow-up should ensure the worker's outer exception handler always populates those fields with the real exception text instead of dropping it. Tracked separately — not blocking the demo.\n- The \\`run_config_id\\` propagation through artifact writes — \\`ensure_run_row\\` already takes it as a kwarg but the document-blob path doesn't have access to it at call time. Same code path, just an additional thread-through if needed; not required for the FK fix.\n\n@kungfusaini\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open hotfix PR"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Tests for the admin-only DELETE guard on demo questions.\n\nDemo questions are curated seed content (``QuestionRow.source ==\nDEMO_QUESTION_SOURCE``). wiped by an unprivileged caller.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import DEMO_QUESTION_SOURCE,\n    build_database_worker_storage_adapters,\n)\nfrom services.api import create_app\nfrom services.api.rate_limit import limiter\nfrom tests.support.api_runtime import (\n    import_seed_json_into_database as _import_seed_json_into_database,\n)\nfrom tests.support.api_runtime import (\n    seed_repo_state as _seed_repo_state,\n)\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef _reset_rate_limiter() -> Iterator[None]:\n    limiter.reset()\n    yield\n    limiter.reset()\n\n\n_ALICE_EMAIL = \"alice@example.com\"\n_ADMIN_EMAIL = \"admin@example.com\"\n\n\ndef _registry() -> _ADMIN_EMAIL: User(user_id=\"admin\", name=\"Admin\", email=_ADMIN_EMAIL, is_admin=True),\n        },\n        defaults=RegistryDefaults(max_runs=3),\n    )\n\n\ndef _build_app_and_config(tmp_path: Path) -> tuple[TestClient, object]:\n    config = _seed_repo_state(tmp_path, api_key=\"\")\n    _import_seed_json_into_database(config)\n    app = create_app(config=config)\n    app.state.user_registry = _registry()\n    return TestClient(app), config\n\n\ndef _create_clean_question(client: TestClient, *, as_email: str, question_id: str = \"demo_target_q\") -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create a categorical question with no nodes/edges so the delete path\n    isn't blocked by ``question_has_graph_data``.\"\"\"\n    resp = client.post(\n        \"/api/questions\",\n        json={\n            \"id\": question_id,\n            \"label\": \"Will the demo placeholder hold?\",\n            \"question_type\": \"categorical\",\n            \"options\": [\"A\", \"B\"],\n            \"closing_date\": \"2027-01-01\",\n            \"question_set_id\": \"local_set\",\n        },\n        headers={CF_AUTHENTICATED_EMAIL_HEADER: as_email},\n    )\n    assert resp.status_code == 201, resp.text\n\n\ndef _mark_source_demo(config, question_id: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Stamp ``source = DEMO_QUESTION_SOURCE`` on a question row in the seed\n    DB. Mirrors what a seed script does when it writes curated demo content\n    (the API submission path never sets this value).\"\"\"\n    adapters = build_database_worker_storage_adapters(config.storage_runtime)\n    engine = adapters.graph_store_repository._database.engine  # noqa: SLF001 — test fixture\n    with engine.begin() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            text(\"UPDATE questions SET source = :src WHERE question_id = :qid\"),\n            {\"src\": DEMO_QUESTION_SOURCE, \"qid\": question_id},\n        )\n\n\nclass TestDemoQuestionDeleteGuard:\n    def test_non_admin_cannot_delete_demo_question(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n        client, config = _build_app_and_config(tmp_path)\n        _create_clean_question(client, as_email=_ADMIN_EMAIL)\n        _mark_source_demo(config, \"demo_target_q\")\n\n        resp = client.delete(\n            \"/api/questions/demo_target_q\",\n            headers={CF_AUTHENTICATED_EMAIL_HEADER: _ALICE_EMAIL},\n        )\n        assert resp.status_code == 403\n        payload = resp.json()[\"detail\"]\n        assert payload[\"code\"] == \"demo_question_admin_only\"\n        assert payload[\"details\"][\"question_id\"] == \"demo_target_q\"\n\n        # The guard treats unknown identity as\n        non-admin so demo content can't be wiped by an unauthenticated caller\n        even when auth is disabled in dev mode.\"\"\"\n        client, config = _build_app_and_config(tmp_path)\n        _create_clean_question(client, as_email=_ADMIN_EMAIL)\n        _mark_source_demo(config, \"demo_target_q\")\n\n        resp = client.delete(\"/api/questions/demo_target_q\")\n        assert resp.status_code == 403\n        assert resp.json()[\"detail\"][\"code\"] == \"demo_question_admin_only\"\n"

They're visible to everyone, but right now any non-admin user can hit DELETE and wipe them. This PR adds a 403 guard so only admins can delete questions tagged as demo content.\n\nMirrors the existing \\`DEMO_SENTINEL\\` pattern for jobs (\\`jobs.submitted_by == 'demo'\\` → visible to all + excluded from quota): a question is \"demo\" when its \\`QuestionRow.source\\` column equals \\`'demo'\\`. Seed scripts set the marker; the API submission path never writes it (the source field there is derived from the caller's identity, not the request body), so users can't smuggle the marker onto their own questions.\n\n## Technical detail\n\n### Summary\n\n- \\`packages/storage/job_queue.py\\` — adds \\`DEMO_QUESTION_SOURCE = \"demo\"\\` constant next to the existing \\`DEMO_SENTINEL\\`. One module for both sentinels so the convention is easy to spot.\n- \\`packages/storage/__init__.py\\` — re-exports it for the API layer.\n- \\`packages/storage/sql_repositories.py\\` — threads \\`row.source\\` into \\`QuestionRecord.data\\` so the API layer can read \\`record.data[\"source\"]\\` without changing the \\`QuestionRecord\\` dataclass shape. \\`QuestionRecord\\` doesn't currently carry a dedicated \\`source\\` field; adding one would ripple through several other call sites for no benefit beyond this guard.\n- \\`services/api/routes/questions.py\\` — \\`delete_question\\` now takes \\`current_user: User | None = Depends(get_current_user)\\` and raises \\`HTTPException(403, ApiError(code='demo_question_admin_only', ...))\\` when the question's source is the sentinel AND the caller isn't an admin. Anonymous callers (auth-disabled dev mode) are treated as non-admin so the guard never weakens.\n- \\`tests/test_demo_question_delete_guard.py\\` — three new tests.\n\n### Tests\n\n- \\`test_non_admin_cannot_delete_demo_question\\` — alice (non-admin) DELETE on a question with \\`source='demo'\\` → 403 \\`demo_question_admin_only\\`, and a subsequent list confirms the question still exists.\n- \\`test_admin_can_delete_demo_question\\` — admin DELETE on the same demo question → 200.\n- \\`test_non_admin_can_still_delete_non_demo_question\\` — alice DELETE on her own (non-demo) question → 200. Guard must only fire on demo content.\n\n### Verification\n\n- [x] \\`uv run ruff check .\\`\n- [x] \\`uv run ruff format --check .\\`\n- [x] \\`uv run python -m pytest tests/test_demo_question_delete_guard.py -x -q\\` → 3 passed\n- [ ] \\`uv run python -m pytest --ignore=tests/frontend -x -q\\` — running in background; will mark when green\n\n### Risks\n\n- Low. The guard only fires for questions explicitly tagged \\`source='demo'\\`. Every existing question on staging today has \\`source\\` in {\\`unknown\\`, \\`user_defined\\`} so this change is a no-op for the current corpus until I run the staging-only SQL update that stamps the UK CPI question with \\`source='demo'\\`.\n- The mapper change to thread \\`source\\` into \\`data\\` is additive — anything that previously read \\`record.data\\` keeps working; the new key just doesn't show up for older rows whose \\`source\\` is NULL.\n\n### Branch-merge\n\nStandalone. No dependency on other in-flight PRs.\n\n### Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- A migration/UI to mark existing questions as demo — those are operator decisions made via SQL or the seed scripts.\n- The PATCH endpoint guard — editing demo content isn't as destructive as deleting it, and analysts may legitimately want to tweak the label/options. Can be added later if needed.\n- Read-side visibility scoping — demo questions remain visible to everyone (the intent today).\n- Re-seeding the staging UK CPI question with \\`source='demo'\\` — that's an operational step I'll do post-merge.\n\n@kungfusaini\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open PR"
}

**NVIDIA targets "disappeared".** The targets ARE in the DB (`n_u2`, `n_u3`) but they have zero edges connecting them to a graph. So `/api/questions/demo_set_q_001/graph` returns an empty graph (0 nodes). This is because:
- When you created the question via the modal, the create flow added the target nodes but didn't fully attach them to the default graph
- The graph_apply stage of the worker pipeline is what re-creates/links the nodes properly
- The current run is at `step_2_research_and_collect_pdf_sources` — way before `graph_apply`

So the empty graph is transient — once the worker reaches the graph_apply stage (still ~5-10 minutes off), it'll re-populate the graph with drivers, indicators, evidence, AND the targets. The Yes/No targets will reappear.

Two separate bugs to file later:
1. **GUI running-indicator isn't question-scoped** — it shows a running run-state on questions that have no jobs
2. **Modal-created questions have orphaned targets** — they get inserted into the `nodes` table but never linked to a graph, so the graph endpoint shows them as missing until the worker pipeline runs

> AGENT

Found it. The pipeline calls `save_question_graph_store_bundle` early on (`packages/storage/sql_repositories.py:1609`). That method's contract is "replace this question's graph": it first DELETES every existing node for the question, then inserts whatever's in the supplied bundle.

The problem — the bundle the pipeline passes at the start of a run is the *raw question definition* without targets fleshed out. So:

1. You create the question → modal calls `reconcile_question_core_graph_bundle` → Yes/No targets get inserted ✅
2. You hit Run Research → pipeline calls `save_question_graph_store_bundle` early → wipes ALL nodes for that question, including the Yes/No targets ❌
3. Pipeline runs for ~10 min through PDF retrieval, driver extraction, indicator extraction…
4. Eventually reaches `graph_apply` stage → re-creates targets + drivers + edges
5. Targets reappear

So during steps 2–4 the graph looks empty even though "logically" the targets are still the question's identity. The wipe is destroying the canonical structure (Yes/No don't change per run) along with the dynamic per-run content (drivers/indicators/evidence/edges).

Real fix would be one of:
- **A.** `save_question_graph_store_bundle` preserves `type='target'` nodes when wiping (treat targets as question-level, not run-level)
- **B.** The early-pipeline call includes the existing targets in its bundle so they're not actually wiped
- **C.** Defer the graph wipe until graph_apply has new content to insert, so the user never sees an empty intermediate state

Option **A** is the cleanest — encodes the invariant that "targets are part of the question identity, not a run output." A would also fix any other code path that calls `save_question_graph_store_bundle` early.

This goes into the bug-list alongside the GUI scoping bug + the modal-orphaned-target issue. Want me to file all three as Linear comments on SPI-256 (or wherever), or just keep them in our heads for now?

> DEVELOPER

I dont really undesatnd explain more simply

> AGENT

Simpler:

Think of your question like a science fair poster.

- The **question title** ("Will NVIDIA tegra prices double?") and the **answer choices** (Yes / No) are the poster's frame. They don't change.
- The **drivers, indicators, evidence** that the system builds to support a prediction are the analysis charts you pin to the board.

When you click Run Research, the system wants to **redo the analysis from scratch** — so it takes everything off the board and starts fresh.

**The bug:** when it takes everything off, it doesn't just remove the analysis charts (drivers, indicators, evidence). It also rips off the frame — the Yes / No answer choices. So for the ~10 minutes the new analysis takes to build, the board is completely blank. Once the analysis finishes, the system pins the analysis AND re-creates the Yes / No frame, and the board fills back up.

**Why it does that:** the cleanup code was written with "remove everything tied to this question, doesn't matter what" instead of "remove only the per-run analysis stuff and leave the question's identity alone."

**Fix:** teach the cleanup code that target nodes (the Yes / No choices) are part of the question's identity and should be left alone, only the analysis-content nodes get wiped.

That's it. The targets aren't lost forever — they come back when the run finishes — but they shouldn't disappear in the middle, because they have nothing to do with what the analysis is doing.

> AGENT

It completed end-to-end this time (no FK crash — yay), but the `indicator_extraction` stage's quality gate flagged at least one driver. Reason code: `indicator_quality_gate_failed`. Pipeline marked it as **partial** rather than fully succeeded.

Plain English: a "driver" is a factor the system thinks might move the outcome. For each driver, the system tries to find concrete, measurable "indicators" (real-world signals you could watch to track that driver). The quality gate requires each driver to have at least a minimum number of indicators AND for those indicators to be balanced (some signal toward Yes, some toward No — not all one-sided).

At least one driver in the NVIDIA run failed that gate — either it didn't get enough indicators, or the indicators all pointed the same direction (no balance). So that driver got blocked from the final graph. The other drivers presumably passed, hence "partial" — most of the analysis is fine, one driver's worth got dropped.

This is a soft-failure of the analytical content, not a code bug. The question is also pretty niche ("NVIDIA tegra chip prices doubling in some unspecified window") — domain coverage for industrial chip pricing is thinner than for macro indicators, so the gate firing isn't surprising.

If you load the question now, you should still see a graph with drivers + targets + most indicators + edges — just slightly thinner than a fully-succeeded run.

> AGENT

Here's the breakdown. The `indicator_extraction` stage processed exactly ONE driver row, and that one driver got:

- **Zero LLM-generated indicator candidates** — the model returned no measurable signals
- **Zero positive AND zero negative indicators**
- **3 quality flags raised:** `indicator_minimum_not_met`, `insufficient_negative_indicators`, `insufficient_positive_indicators`

Result: 1 driver in → 1 driver blocked by the quality gate → 1 driver dropped from the graph → stage marked **partial**.

Wider quality stats from the run also showed **6 driver candidates** got dropped *earlier* (before they even reached indicator extraction) for `missing_market_channel` and `missing_evidence_basis`. So the pipeline started with multiple driver candidates from research, ~6 got tossed for missing required fields, and only 1 survived into the indicator stage. That 1 didn't produce any indicators.

**Plain English:** the system extracted drivers from the research docs but then couldn't find concrete real-world things to *measure* for the one driver that made it through. Indicators are stuff like "NVIDIA gross margin", "data center capex growth", "TSMC wafer pricing" — measurable proxies. For "tegra chip prices doubling in some window," the LLM saw the driver but couldn't think of strong measurable signals, so the gate fired.

Why? Two things working together:
1. The question is **niche.** Indust​rial chip pricing has thinner public-data coverage than macro indicators (CPI, unemployment, etc.) where the model's training is denser.
2. The pipeline is **strict.** The quality gate requires both positive and negative signal balance — zero of either fails. A more permissive gate would have let the driver through with weak indicators.

Not a bug — the pipeline did exactly what it's supposed to do for thin-evidence questions. If you ran the same pipeline on the UK CPI question (where there are 11 well-known indicators in the seeded graph), it'd sail through. The "partial" label is honest signal that the analysis is thin.

> AGENT

Good catch. The system is technically correct per its current policy, but the policy might be wrong:

**What counts against the cap today** (`packages/storage/job_queue.py:RUN_CAP_COUNTED_STATES`):

```python
RUN_CAP_COUNTED_STATES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded")
```

So your two visible runs map to:
- 1 partial → **NOT counted**
- 1 running → counted

Total: 1 used → 2 of 3 remaining → matches the GUI.

**The reasoning behind excluding `partial`** (from the original PR that added run caps): "Failed, cancelled, partial, and skipped jobs are deliberately excluded so a user isn't punished for pipeline-side problems."

**Why I think that policy is wrong:** a partial run still did all the expensive work — downloaded PDFs, called the LLM for driver extraction, ran indicator extraction, etc. It cost the same in API credits as a successful run, just produced a slightly-thinner result. The user *did* spend a real demo slot.

The "don't punish for pipeline problems" framing makes sense for:
- **failed** — yes, exclude. The pipeline crashed; user got nothing useful.
- **cancelled** — yes, exclude. User explicitly aborted.
- **skipped** — yes, exclude. Pipeline never ran.

But `partial` is a real run that produced (most of) a forecast. Counting it lines up with cost AND with user perception (you'd say "yeah I ran two questions" not "I ran one and a half").

**Proposed change:** add `partial` to `RUN_CAP_COUNTED_STATES`. One-line + a test update.

  "new_string": "        function setActiveJob(jobId) {\n          activeJobId = jobId || null;\n          if (cancelResearchBtn) cancelResearchBtn.hidden = !activeJobId;\n          if (runResearchBtn) {\n            runResearchBtn.disabled = Boolean(activeJobId);\n            runResearchBtn.textContent = activeJobId ? \"Running…\" : \"Run Research\";\n            runResearchBtn.title = activeJobId\n              ? \"A run is already in progress for this question — wait for it to finish or cancel it first.\"\n              : \"\";\n          }\n        }\n\n        // Reconciles the Run Research button + poller against the run-history\n        // for the currently-selected question. Called from `refreshRunHistory`\n        // whenever the question changes or its run-history is refetched.\n        // - If a queued/running job exists for this question, become its\n        //   active poller (disables Run Research, shows Cancel).\n        // - If no in-flight job, clear active state (re-enables Run Research)\n        //   AND tear down any stale poll that was running for a previous\n        //   question's job so it doesn't keep ticking in the background.\n        function syncActiveJobFromRunHistory(relevantJobs, questionId) {\n          const inflight = (relevantJobs || []).find((job) => {\n            const state = String(job.state || \"\").toLowerCase();\n            return state === \"queued\" || state === \"running\";\n          });\n          if (inflight) {\n            const inflightId = inflight.job_id || inflight.run_id || null;\n            if (inflightId && inflightId !== activeJobId) {\n              setActiveJob(inflightId);\n              pollJobUntilTerminal(inflightId, questionId);\n            } else if (inflightId) {\n              // Already tracking this job — refresh stepper from the latest\n              // state without restarting the poll.\n              setStepperState(String(inflight.state || \"\").toLowerCase());\n            }\n            return;\n          }\n          // No in-flight job for the active question. Stop any stale poll\n          // (carrying over a previous question's job) and free the button.\n          if (activeJobPollTimer) {\n            clearTimeout(activeJobPollTimer);\n            activeJobPollTimer = null;\n          }\n          setActiveJob(null);\n        }"
}

The cost is negligible.\n- One thing to watch: the new code only starts a fresh poll when `inflightId !== activeJobId`. If the user switches back-and-forth between two questions both with in-flight jobs, the poller swaps cleanly. If the user submits research, then switches questions before the poll terminates, the poll is torn down — the submit's optimistic `setActiveJob(jobId)` step still fires on the original question, but switching away cancels the poll for it.
